AMENDED AGAIN 2026-08-10 - LP v3.5 -> v3.6, Rules 1 and 2 ALIGNED WITH SECONDARY (the revisit fix).

CAUSE - Rule 2's own cap, and it is arithmetic. 'Two adjacent periods' x 5 sections = 10 body units; the top needs 11. The model could not place unit 11 without breaking something, so it broke both rules available: one run of three on 7.3 (Rule 2) and three returns (Rule 1). The constraint binds exactly when body_units > 2 x sections, and the corpus tracks it: ch7 top 11>10 binds (3 revisits) - ch7 p10 10=10 marginal (1) - ch7 p07 7<10 slack (0) - maths IX ch4 14<16 slack (0) - science IX ch8 slack (0).

MATHS SECONDARY HAS NO CAP, which is why IX never revisits: its Rule 7 FULL-SECTION COVERAGE says a section may span more than one period where its content warrants it, emphasis following substance, and forbids any numerical allocation formula across sections; its Rule 2 is not a packing rule at all. Middle's PERIOD BIN-PACKING was the outlier in the maths family and the only one of the three naming a number. So this is a PORT, not an invention.

WHAT LANDED: Rule 1 gains one sentence making 'interleave' concrete (a section's periods are CONTIGUOUS; a later period MUST NOT re-anchor a completed section; consolidation belongs inside the run). Rule 2 renamed FULL-SECTION COVERAGE - cap removed (as many ADJACENT periods as content warrants, emphasis follows substance never effort_index), surplus budget spent by DEEPENING inside a run, secondary's two prohibitions ported (no numerical allocation formula, no front-loading), two-goal split generalised from 'period N / N+1' to earlier/later periods of the run. Full coverage and the ban on dropping a section untouched.

SECTION 9: CONSTITUTION CHANGE IN THE FULL SENSE - the relaxation-only carve-out does NOT apply. The cap removal is a relaxation but Rule 1's contiguity sentence and Rule 2's two ported prohibitions are TIGHTENINGS, and one tightening forfeits the carve-out. OWED WITH THIS, AND FREE: a certifier check that no section appears in two non-contiguous runs. Rule 1 has forbidden interleaving all along and nothing ever tested it - which is why three revisits reached a paid artefact and were found by eye.

SERVE WALL TIME: 3.4 ms median cold, against a 5000 ms budget. Three orders of magnitude inside it.

MEASURED HONESTLY — the first numbers were wrong and I caught it. load_genon_streams memoises compiled canonicals per file mtime (api/data._stream_cache), so a naive loop measures the WARM path and reported 0.6 ms. Clearing the cache before every run, as a fresh process would be, gives the real cold figure. Recording both, because the difference is the point:
   COLD (compile cache cleared each run, n=15) : median 3.4 ms · min 3.1 · max 13.0
   WARM (library already compiled in-process)  : median 0.6-0.7 ms
   SPLIT: load + compile all 4 canonicals 3.0 ms · select + serve 0.3 ms

So the cost is ALL in reading and compiling the library; the actual serve — selection, duration scaling, band integerisation, assessment remap — is 0.3 ms. That is what "serving is SELECTION, never composition" buys, and it is the number to quote when anyone asks what the architecture is for.

TIMED ACROSS EVERY MODE, warm, n=20 each (all medians):
   45x9  synthesis borrow       0.6 ms      45x5  below floor, 2 drops   0.6 ms
   60x3+45x7 mixed + scaled     0.6 ms      45x13 surrender             0.7 ms
   45x12 identity (12 sittings) 0.7 ms

C14.comment:
COPYRIGHTS REVIEW — no wholesale reproduction, no third-party material, nothing unattributed. ONE borderline string sent to the human gate as a subjective call, per the step's own doctrine.

METHOD: genon/copyright_scan.py over all 12 files (4 canonicals + 8 served, including the founder's 45x15), shingling the chapter's textbook PDF and summary and reporting maximal verbatim runs. 14 hits >= 12 words, but only THREE DISTINCT STRINGS — the rest are the same items repeated across served plans, which is expected since every served plan carries its base canonical's assessment verbatim.

WHERE THEY SIT, and this is the headline: ALL FOURTEEN ARE IN ASSESSMENT ITEMS. Zero in band text, zero in teacher notes, zero in activity titles, zero in homework. The lesson plan prose — the bulk of what a teacher reads — collides with the source nowhere at 12 words or more. That is the right shape: the LP is original activity design, and the collisions are where a question must restate a mechanism to test it.

1 · NO VERBATIM REPRODUCTION BEYOND SHORT QUOTATION
 (a) 12 words, MCQ option: "from a region of high pressure to a region of low pressure" (and its "higher/lower" twin in an ECR look_for). PASS — this is the DEFINITION of wind. There is no other way to say it; any physics text on earth says it the same way. Definition, not expression, exactly the case the scanner's own docstring exempts.
 (b) 12 words, question stem: "strong upward and downward winds cause water droplets and ice particles to" — source: "Strong upward and downward winds cause water droplets and ice particles to rub against each other, generating static electric charges." PASS, weakly. The stem sets up a mechanism question and stops before the payload the student must supply. The phrasing is plain — "strong upward and downward winds" is the ordinary description, not a turn of phrase — and a question testing this mechanism can hardly avoid naming it.
 (c) **18 words, MCQ option: "charge build up is large enough to break down air s insulating property a sudden discharge lightning occurs"** — source: "When the charge build-up is large enough to break down air's insulating property, a sudden discharge — lightning — occurs." SUBJECTIVE, FLAGGED, and the one string on this chapter I would not wave through on my own authority.
     FOR accepting: it is a correct-answer option in an MCQ about the discharge mechanism; the option must state the mechanism accurately, and 18 words is one sentence.
     AGAINST: "break down air's insulating property" is an EXPRESSIVE choice, not the only way to put it — "overcomes air's resistance", "ionises the air path" both work — so this is not the definitional case (a) is. 18 consecutive words carrying a distinctive phrase is past what "short quotation" comfortably covers.
     Per C14's closing rule ("subjective calls are flagged as such with the strings quoted, and land at the human gate — same doctrine as C3's register judgements") this goes to the founder rather than becoming a defect on my say-so. If he rules it over the line, the remedy is a reworded option at zero cost via a repair pass, not a regeneration.

2 · NO THIRD-PARTY COPYRIGHTED MATERIAL — ZERO hits across all 12 files for poems, lyrics, verse, stanzas, story excerpts, brand names or copyright marks. Nothing appears in a stimulus or activity that the textbook does not itself carry. The chapter's own content (bag straps, spring balances, balloons, lightning conductors, cyclone safety) is all NCERT material used as subject matter, not reproduced as text.

3 · QUOTED SOURCE TEXT IS ATTRIBUTED — vacuously satisfied: NOTHING is presented as a quotation. Zero quoted strings in teacher notes or activity titles across all 12 files. There is no unattributed quotation because there is no quotation.

F2 CONTEXT (docs/NCERT_copyright_review.md, the sole open finding): F2 is ENGLISH verbatim task-text in served plans, and does not arise here — science·middle carries no textbook task text; its homework is authored, not lifted, and there is no (p.NN) convention on this stage. This step polices F2 and finds it not applicable to S6.

EXIT: zero unattributed or wholesale reproductions. One string (c) carried to the human gate as a subjective call with the text quoted in full.

MEASURED 2026-08-10. Cache-miss serve path, engine side, timed in the sandbox (5 runs per matrix, median).

  library load + compile of all 3 canonicals   13.10 ms   (cold, once per request)
  serve — selection + remap                     0.27 ms   (worst of six matrices)
  JSON serialize (51.4 KB plan)                 0.52 ms
  write + fsync to disk                         4.63 ms
  ------------------------------------------------------
  TOTAL CACHE-MISS PATH                        18.52 ms  =  0.019 s
  C11 threshold                                 5.000 s  →  270x headroom

PER-MODE serve time (median of 5): identity 0.23 ms · fill/single 0.24 ms · below floor 0.21 ms · surrender 0.25 ms · synthesis borrow 0.27 ms · mixed 4x50+7x40 matrix 0.27 ms. The spread across modes is ~0.06 ms — selection genuinely costs nothing, which is the architectural claim v2.0 rests on ('serving is SELECTION, never composition'). The dominant cost is the 13 ms library load, and the second is the 4.6 ms fsync — i.e. the serve itself is not the work; reading three canonicals off disk is.

WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, stated plainly: this is the ENGINE path, not the HTTP round trip. C11 asks for `curl -w '%{time_total}'`, and the sandbox proxy cannot reach the local API (testing.md 0.1), so FastAPI overhead, request parsing, the prepared-plans register write and the response serialization are excluded. The verdict is safe regardless: the API would have to add 4.98 s to breach a 5 s threshold. A Terminal curl would close it exactly, and is worth folding into the same run that owes C10.2's cache-hit half.

NOTE the cache makes even this an upper bound — a repeat request serves the file without touching the engine, so 18.5 ms is the worst case a teacher meets, once per (chapter, matrix).

TWO METHOD DECISIONS, AND BOTH CHANGED THE ANSWER.
(a) THE SUMMARY IS NOT THE COPYRIGHT SOURCE AND IS SCORED APART. The textbook is the protected
work; ch_07_summary.json is Aruvi's own asset. Scored together the longest 'verbatim' run reads
45 WORDS; against the book alone it is 18. The 45 was the pipeline quoting itself. Every hit
below is attributed to one source or the other, never to their union.
(b) THE DETECTOR WAS VALIDATED FIRST. A 20-word passage lifted from the PDF is detected at 20
words; the check-2 regexes fire on planted brand/poem/URL strings. PDF extraction verified sound
— 34 pages, 7,687 words, no empty page — because a clean result is exactly what a broken
extraction returns.

CHECK 1 · NO VERBATIM REPRODUCTION BEYOND SHORT QUOTATION — PASS, measured.
   1,033 of 1,193 strings (86.6%) share NOTHING with the book at 8 words.
   1,916 of 39,240 plan words (4.9%) sit inside any 8-word shared run.
   82 of the chapter's 7,143 8-grams are reached by any plan string — 1.15% OF THE CHAPTER.
   10 distinct runs >= 12 words. Longest 18 words. Longest PROSE run 16 words.
   All 10 are also carried in full by Aruvi's own summary.
FIVE OF THE TEN ARE MEASUREMENT DATA — '(a) 3 cm, 75 deg, 7 cm; (b) 6 cm, 25 deg, 3 cm...',
'(a) 1, 100, 100; (b) 3, 6, 9...'. They survive normalisation as 'words' because a measurement
becomes tokens. Facts, not expression: there is no other way to set the same construction
exercise. FOUR DISTINCT PROSE RUNS REMAIN, the longest 16 words, each carrying a locator, and
against the book's own sentences they are demonstrably condensation rather than lifting:
  BOOK p.168: 'Cut out a paper triangle. Fix one of the sides as the base. Fold it in such a way
  that the resulting crease is an altitude from the top vertex to the base. Justify why the
  crease formed should be perpendicular to the base.'
  PLAN: 'Altitudes Using Paper Folding: cut out a paper triangle, fix one side as the base, and
  fold so the crease is the altitude from the top vertex to the base. Justify why the crease is
  perpendicular to the base.'
Section anchors are exempt by the step's own terms and were excluded from every run above.

CHECK 2 · NO THIRD-PARTY COPYRIGHTED MATERIAL — PASS. Zero hits across all 13 plans for 30
Indian and global brand marks, for poem/stanza/verse/lyric/excerpt-from/copyright markers, and
for any external image or url (http, www., <img, xlink:href, .jpg/.png/.svg). ZERO of the 114
items carries a populated visual_stimulus, so there is no externally-sourced image anywhere.
Worth stating plainly rather than reporting a hollow pass: this chapter is ruler-and-compass
geometry, and its cardboard boxes, paper folding, set squares and spider are NCERT's own subject
matter used AS subject matter. The F2 risk class lives in English.

CHECK 3 · QUOTED SOURCE TEXT IS ATTRIBUTED — PASS. 519 quoted passages, 90 distinct; 81 carry a
locator in the same field; the 9 that do not share ZERO 8-word runs with the book and are

one sentence', 'What do you notice about the three numbers in each row?') plus two
apostrophe-split regex artefacts. 41 of the 90 carry the '....' truncation marker, which says on
its face that text was cut. 97 distinct strings carry a book locator — the compliant pattern the
review's T5 answer depends on: a locator points INTO a book the school already owns and
reproduces nothing of it.

F2 — THE SOLE OPEN CAMPAIGN FINDING. Maths-middle is the NEAREST THING TO F2 OUTSIDE ENGLISH and
is still not it, which is worth saying precisely rather than filing another N/A. Rule 10 of this
stage's LP constitution MANDATES an inline quotation (book_ref ("description....")) where
maths-SECONDARY mandates a bare locator — so this stage does have a conduit, and S4's C14 finding
('mathematics has no such conduit') does not port across the family. What keeps it clear of F2 is
that what flows through the conduit is the SUMMARY's condensation, not the book's sentences:
1.15% of the chapter reached, 16-word prose ceiling. F2 stays open and stays owed by S9/S10/S11.

ONE DEFECT RAISED — ARV-D-108, and it is a COMPLIANCE defect, not a copyright one. Rule 10 caps
the inline quotation at 10 words; 75 of 88 band quotations (85%) exceed it, median 18.5, max 39.

breached at 85%, and on this chapter it holds only because the summary paraphrases. Set a chapter
whose summary tracks its source more closely and the same 85% breach lands on the book's own

globbed only ch_NN_summary.txt. Science and social_sciences carry .txt; MATHEMATICS, ENGLISH and

COST SHAPE - THIS CHAPTER SHARPENS THE STANDING FINDING RATHER THAN REPEATING IT. Input is flat (17.9k every run, 3 dp of variation), so cost is all output. But output does NOT track plan length:
  p11 = 79% of the standard's units -> 99.6% of its output, 99.7% of its cost
  p08 = 57% of the standard's units -> 89.4% of its output, 90.7% of its cost

The compacts carry MORE items than the standard, because Rule 2 emits one item per retained handoff task and a shorter plan's free authoring retained more of them. BUDGET PER RUN, NEVER PER UNIT - and note that the saving from a compact is small enough that a fourth canonical, if C8 ever asks for one, costs very nearly a full run.

C11 - serve wall time. PASS by three orders of magnitude; the design premise holds.

MEASURED in the engine (selection + compile, which is what C11 is about), 20 runs at each X across the whole band 6..15:
  median 0.4 ms · mean 0.4 ms · max 1.4 ms across 200 serves
  every mode timed the same: identity 0.3-0.4, fill 0.4, complete_rescue 0.4, synthesis 0.4, surrender 0.4
  library compile (all 3 canonicals): 4.1 ms COLD, 0.4 ms WARM - mtime-keyed memo in api/data._compiled
  WORST CASE, a cache-miss request that also pays a cold library compile: 5.6 ms

EXIT is < 5000 ms. Measured 5.6 ms. PASS with ~900x headroom.

WHAT THIS CONFIRMS, which is the point of the check rather than the number: serving is SELECTION, not generation. The whole premise of the variant-canonical architecture is that a teacher's request costs milliseconds because the thinking was paid for once at authoring time. A serve that took seconds would mean the engine was doing work it should not be doing. It is doing none: no mode is measurably slower than any other, so neither the Xth-unit choice set, the exact-fit rescue, the synthesis borrow nor proportional duration scaling costs anything perceptible.

SCOPE OF THE MEASUREMENT, stated plainly: this times the ENGINE, not the HTTP round trip. A live curl would add FastAPI overhead, the prepared-plans register read/write and the JSON write to disk - all small, none in the engine's path, and none of them the thing C11 is checking. The founder's own C6 requests through the running app returned without perceptible delay, which is the corroborating observation.

THE COST SHAPE DOES NOT MATCH THE BENCHMARK, AND THE INVERSION IS STRUCTURAL. WHAT THE P-PREP'S OWN AMENDMENTS DID, LIVE.
- FULL SPINE COVERAGE (new at v1.2) HELD AT THE FLOOR: 5 of 5 cells in all three canonicals, ZERO drops at 7 periods. The stage's legacy saved plan (iii ch 1) carries 3 of 5 under the old drop licence. Pressure went to TASK level exactly as the rule intends - p07 anchors 10 of 11 summary tasks, the top 11 of 11.
- RULE 9's WHICH SUBHEADING clause did precisely the job it was added for: three of this chapter's five cells carry a MERGED section_name ('Let us think + Let us speak' etc.) and the merged string is used verbatim ZERO times in either file - briefs name the single subheading ('Let us think (p.72)', 'Let us write A (p.74)').
- RULE 1's CLOSING-UNIT EXCEPTION is used as written: u12 names all five spines with tasks_in_class empty, teaching no cell of its own. Every OTHER unit stays inside the one-or-two bound, and the single ordinary two-spine unit (u11) satisfies clause (d) exactly - one task each.
- A1: one row {40,12} / {40,7}, every unit at 40, all 19 units tiling 0..40 EXACTLY.
- A6/RULE 8A: period_ref, period_number and unit_ref emitted NOWHERE. The prohibition confirmed at P2 holds on its first live outing.
- THE PAIR: 10 items = 2 x 5 contributions in all three files, at 12, 10 and 7 units - v1.4's invariance line proved live.

FAIL 1 (cross-stage, points at the RULE) - RULE 9's NARRATION FORMAT HAS NEVER BEEN FOLLOWED BY ANY ENGLISH LIBRARY, INCLUDING A CERTIFIED ONE. The mandated shape '<spine_section_name> (“brief <= 10 words”)' appears in 1 of 49 bands (top), 1 of 34 (p07), 1 of 47 (english VI ch 8, S10) and 1 of 69 (english IX ch 7, S11, CERTIFIED) - four libraries, three stages, 199 bands, essentially zero compliance, and every hit is an incidental parenthetical rather than the format. What the model writes instead satisfies the rule's stated REQUIREMENT ('names the task by anchor location + brief') but not its stated FORMAT: 'Let us recite - teacher reads the poem aloud with full expression...'. time_bands[].activity is the NARRATIVE of the minutes; a rule demanding it be 'Let us recite (“choral echo reading”)' would empty the timed spine of content. The Format line reads like a spec for a terse label and plausibly predates the field's current role - it survived P3's rename unexamined at this stage and at both siblings. FILED, NOT REPAIRED.

FAIL 2 (points at the RULE, with the founder's call named) - THE ASSESSMENT SLOT TABLE IS BREACHED IN ONE CONSISTENT PLACE AND TWO ONE-OFFS. writing slot 1 is FILL_IN in 3 of 3 files where the table prescribes SCR; p07's beyond_text slot 1 is FILL_IN where the table permits MATCH only; p10's reading slot 2 is ORAL_PROMPT where the table prescribes SCR. THE DEMAND AXIS IS SATISFIED EVERYWHERE (recognition then production) - it is the TYPE column that is breached, and Rule 2's own demand wording includes 'completes', which is what FILL_IN is, so the table and the demand axis disagree on this cell. The writing breach is content-driven: this section's writing tasks ARE sorting and column-filling ('write round things in can eat / cannot eat columns'), so FILL_IN tests what was taught and an SCR would have to invent a different task. The two one-offs are weaker: p10's reading slot 2 as ORAL_PROMPT loses the written response the reading spine is meant to elicit.

FAIL 3 - RULE 11's <= 8-WORD RUBRIC BULLETS BENT ON FIRST CONTACT. Top: Q-ORAL-B-2 at 10 words, Q-WORD-B-2 at 9, against '3 bullets, each <= 8 words'. Bullet COUNT is 3 everywhere. Preparatory's <= 8 is the NARROWEST rubric cap in the english family (middle 3-4 / <= 10, secondary 3-5 / <= 12) and had never been exercised; it bends by 1-2 words on bullets that are not padded ('Describes at least one sense - taste, smell or texture.'). p07's six open items are all inside 8.

FAIL 4 - task_brief <= 18 BREACHED TWICE, AND BOTH ARE HOMEWORK. 20 words ('Let us think (p.72): write one sentence about what happened to the laddoo after it was thrown into the sea.') and 19 at u8. IN-CLASS briefs max at 14. A homework brief has to stand alone without the teacher's voice, which is why it runs longer - and P1's simulation that set 18 measured IN-CLASS briefs only. The cap is one word short of the evidence, and the evidence says homework wants its own number. THIS IS THE S4 LESSON LANDING ON A NUMBER SET THE SAME DAY.

SUBJECTIVE FAIL 1 - p07's Q-WORD-B-2 IS ANSWERABLE WITHOUT READING THE SECTION. 'Think about a laddoo you have seen or eaten. Say two sentences that describe it... Use words that tell us more about the laddoo.' That is Rule 3's first prohibition, and it also fails the word_work clause requiring the concept be NAMED in the stem. The top's counterpart does both: 'Think of the giant laddoo in the poem - round, sweet, and enormous. Choose TWO describing words...'. Subjective because 'grounded' is a judgement; the quoted strings are what it rests on.

SUBJECTIVE FAIL 2 (minor) - ONE TEACHER-PROSE LEAK. Top u6 teacher_notes: 'The blend words (pl-, cl-, bl-) connect to the WORD-WORK SPINE content'. 'spine' is a schema key (spines_taught, source_spine) and Rule 9 bans schema keys and planner identifiers from teacher-facing prose. One occurrence; zero in p07.

THE POEM LOCATOR PASSED, AND IT IS THE ITEM THE PILOT WAS CHOSEN FOR. p07's Q-READ-B-1 is the mandated form exactly: 'Read the stanza on page 70 beginning "If all the laddoos were one Laddoo". What does the poet imagine in this stanza?' - page reference, incipit in double quotes, SEVEN words against a cap of eight, no ellipsis. No poem line reaches visual_stimulus, suggested_answer or any rubric field in either file. A NUANCE WORTH CARRYING TO C14: this poem's lines run 4-9 words, so a COMPLIANT eight-word incipit can BE a whole line - a scanner looking for reproduced lines flags this item and reading clears it. That is the mirror of the copyright review's own caveat ('an 8-gram scan is blind to a compliant incipit'), and together they mean C14 ON A PREPARATORY POEM CHAPTER CANNOT BE AUTOMATED IN EITHER DIRECTION.

RULE 12 PARTIAL: total_items was NEVER EMITTED (grep -c total_items = 0 in the raw generation output). Nothing downstream reads it - the certifier counts items itself - so it costs nothing today, but a rule nothing enforces and nothing consumes should either be enforced or struck.

TWO READING NOTES FOR LATER C-STEPS. (a) Rule 6 / Rule 12 HEADERS must be audited in the LEDGER file (genon/out/canonical/), not the installed one: build_library.py's install rewraps into the app's saved-plan shape and moves header fields to the wrapper or drops them. The model emitted the full header correctly. (b) Three rules are VACUOUS PASSES at this stage and should not be read as evidence: Rule 2 STEP 2 (proportional allocation - every preparatory chapter is one main_section), Rule 3's listening bands and Rule 10's transcript_ref (this chapter's oracy tasks carry no transcript). A transcript-bearing chapter is owed at pre-warm.

A9 GOT EMPHATIC EVIDENCE AND IT BELONGS IN THE RULE TABLE TOO: across the library the correct option was authored at position B in FIVE OF FIVE MCQ/TRUE_FALSE items, and the deterministic sort scattered them to C, D, B, C, B. THE PERCENTAGE WENT UP, 2.00% → 2.51%, AND THAT IS THE REPAIR WORKING. The old figure was flattered by text that LOOKED like quotation and was not. 26 paragraph-length passages exist in the whole English corpus (24 at IX, 2 at VII, all in visual_stimulus, 24 of 26 EXTRACT_ANALYSIS; zero paragraph-length quotations anywhere in the lesson plans, across 93 canonicals). FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-14 — the reproduction is ACCEPTED, and F2 closes on that ruling rather than on the reproduction being absent. Reasoning: 'extracts are functional requirements and if we compromise or cross refer it will impact negatively the effectiveness.' An EXTRACT_ANALYSIS item exists to make a student read the author's words closely; a page reference converts a five-minute question into a book-hunt. The corpus itself is the argument — every attempt in it to avoid reproduction produced a fabrication. So: quote, accurately, with the page. All 14 are now inverted-commas quotations carrying their page; paraphrase carries NO quotation marks, so provenance is legible on sight. C14 test 2 (no third-party material the book does not carry) and test 3 (every quotation attributed) PASS outright. Test 1 ('no verbatim reproduction beyond short quotation') is ACCEPTED, not passed — 126, 110, 87 and 86-word runs stand, attributed. OWED, and it is what makes the ruling durable: docs/NCERT_permission_request_letter.docx exists in the repo and is not sent. Until then the ruling rests on s.52(1)(i) of the Copyright Act 1957 (reproduction in the course of instruction) — read by a founder and an AI, neither a lawyer. A length cap (e.g. 60 words, page reference beyond) remains available and would bring ch 01, 15, 07 and 11 under it.

waiver.comment:
REGISTER WAIVER · english·middle · founder ruling 2026-08-15. Closing checklist §5 item 3 asks for ZERO register ban hits library-wide. This stage closes with 8, and every one is a scanner false positive that was ruled rather than repaired. Recorded here so the gap is a DECISION on the record, not something the next reader re-derives — and deliberately NOT fixed at the scanner, so the next english library re-raises them and the ruling is re-made with evidence rather than inherited silently.

GROUP A — bridges? (to|toward) the firing where nothing points forward (4). Founder: "ignore it, no repair needed." The pattern was added 2026-08-03 (ARV-D-038) for "bridges toward the … sections that follow"; it matches the bare phrase.
  • vi/ch_01_canonical.json U6 — "a bridge to the phonics work FROM the speaking unit": a BACKWARD reference, legal since v1.10.
  • vii/ch_02_canonical.json U10 — "a genuine bridge to the science curriculum": cross-curricular, names no unit.
  • viii/ch_06_canonical.json U1 — "bridge to the text": into this unit's own text.
  • viii/ch_14_canonical_p09.json U6 — "conceptual bridge to the space-travel speaking task", that unit's own task. (Its REAL breach, the closing sentence naming a later sitting, WAS repaired under v1.7.)

GROUP B — the meta-leak disclaimer regex spanning a semicolon into an unrelated clause (2). Founder: no preference expressed; left as authored on the same reasoning as Group A. The pattern's window is [^.]{0,70}, which crosses clause boundaries to reach OUR vocabulary in a sentence that was never about it.
  • vii/ch_02_canonical.json U9 — "closes within its own minutes without requiring prepared specimens; the homework folk-song task…": the disclaimer's object is MATERIALS.
  • vii/ch_06_canonical.json U7 — "without requiring revision time the unit does not have": the object is TIME, and the sentence is a scheduling judgement about this unit's own budget.

GROUP C — content the scanner cannot tell from scheduling (2). Flagged by Claude at W2 rather than repaired, because striking either would falsify chapter content (runbook trap 4).
  • vii/ch_02_canonical_p06.json U1 [forward] "foreshadow" — the pre-reading pictures foreshadow the poem's spider metaphor, and the poem is READ IN THAT SAME UNIT. The pattern has no same-unit exemption.
  • vii/ch_03_canonical_p07.json U3 [calendar] "tomorrow" — Helen Keller's own argument ("use their eyes as if tomorrow they might be blind"), paraphrased from p.33. The word is the ESSAY'S. A calendar hit inside quotation marks drops to advisory; this close paraphrase misses the exemption by its punctuation alone.

WHAT THIS WAIVER DOES NOT COVER. It is scoped to these 8 strings in these 7 files. It is not a standing exemption for the four patterns, and it does not travel to another stage: english·preparatory and english·secondary must rule on their own hits with their own evidence. The upstream remedy, if the rate persists, is at the scanner — a forward object required on the bridge pattern, a clause boundary on the disclaimer window, a same-unit exemption, a wider quoted-content test — and that is a free change under §9. It was NOT taken here because four patterns narrowed on one stage's evidence is how a gate stops catching things.

F1.comment:
S10 · classes vi/vii/viii · 2026-08-15. ENUMERATED, NOT SAMPLED. borrowed_seams.py swept all 46 chapters over X in [floor−2, top+2]; self-fills are excluded by definition (the serving plan's own priors, nothing foreign to read), leaving 44 cross-canonical borrowed seams — vi 9 · vii 15 · viii 20. The largest F1 in the campaign (S11 read 21, S5 read 30) and still a FULL read, so there is no sample and no rate to defend.

METHOD, stated because it differs from earlier stages. Dossiers were built by RE-SERVING each seam (genon/out/f1_seam_dossiers.py) rather than by inferring the borrowed unit from the lender's last period — correct only for the synthesis modes and wrong for every fill/*. Each dossier is asymmetric on purpose: the host prefix as unit TITLES (all the borrowed unit is entitled to assume) against the borrowed unit's full assumption surface — notes, MATERIALS, every band, homework. ARV-D-119's lesson: the dependency arrives through materials, not the prose. Read against the SHORTEST prefix in every case. Three readers took one grade each against a fixed rubric; every non-CLEAN rating was then verified against the source file, and the JUMPY was traced into the lender canonical to confirm its provenance.

RESULT: 38 CLEAN · 5 SERVICEABLE · 1 JUMPY. All five SERVICEABLE are join REDUNDANCY — the host prefix's last unit and the borrowed unit working the same textbook pages back to back (vi ch7, vii ch7, vii ch10 X=2, viii ch2, viii ch4) — no continuity break in any of them. Every MATERIALS line across all 44 was checked individually: not one lists an artefact another unit produces. The units carrying an explicit portability sentence in NOTES ("not a continuation of any earlier draft", "no written artefact from an earlier sitting is needed or assumed") were without exception clean — the V-series discipline is visibly landing in authored text, and that sentence is a usable certification signal.

THE ONE JUMPY — viii ch 01 X=6, and it is ARV-D-136 recurring. The class receives p05's five units plus the TOP's synthesis U8. Band 0: "Students draft their narrative essay in full (p.15–16) using the outline they formed — introduction, body with a turning point, and a conclusion that draws a lesson." The outline is made in the top's U7 ("draft an outline (opening sentence, two or three body points, closing lesson)") — a sitting this class never had. The unit is TRUE in its home plan at X=8 and false the moment it is borrowed: anchoring is not teaching (e11 / ARV-D-023).
It is worse than a missing artefact. The prefix's last sitting is U5 "Narrative Essays and a Limerick of Their Own" — the class has already written the essay AND the limericks — and the borrowed unit then asks them to draft the essay and introduces limericks as new ("Teacher introduces limericks from 'Let us explore' (p.16): reads the sample aloud, pointing out the AABBA rhyme scheme"). Two consecutive sittings doing the same two tasks, the second pretending the first did not happen.
Same shape as english·IX ch 7: a TOP synthesis that touches the writing spine. Not repairable in place — the fix is that U8 must stop doing the writing spine, which is a teaching change, and repair_register.py exists precisely to refuse laundering those as text hygiene. S11's remedy was a re-author of the top at ₹28.74 with both compacts staying verbatim against the new registry.

KNOWN LIMITATION, RECORDED RATHER THAN GATED (founder ruling 2026-08-15). The reading surfaced a defect CLASS the certifier cannot see, and the ruling is to record it, not to build a check that fingers it. Six borrowed units name a prior ACTIVITY rather than content, and are true only because THIS prefix happens to contain it:
  • vi ch7 "the leaf presentations" (prefix U3) · vi ch9 "whether modal verbs appeared in both" (U6) · vi ch11 "their own playtime paragraphs" (U5)
  • vii ch5 X=8 "using at least one phrasal verb" (U6) — and ch5's OWN X=5 prefix drops that spine entirely
  • vii ch14 "the gratitude note they wrote" (U3) — directly under a NOTES line claiming "no particular earlier activity or written piece is assumed to exist"
  • viii ch4 X=6 "their oral presentations … using their chosen theme from the Let us speak task" (U3)
All rated CLEAN or SERVICEABLE because they are true HERE. They are clean by luck, not by construction. Nothing in the pipeline can catch them: the register bans FORWARD references, and v1.10 legalised backward ones deliberately — a backward activity reference is legal prose that happens to be false for some prefixes. The shape to watch if it is ever taken up: a possessive activity reference in a borrowed unit, verified against the host prefix's actual units. Not scheduled. Recorded so the next stage's F1 reads for it by eye.

Dossiers: genon/out/f1_english_middle/f1_{vi,vii,viii}.txt.

RULING ON THE JUMPY — ACCEPTED AS AUTHORED (founder, 2026-08-15). No re-author, no repair, no constitution change. The defect stands on disk and is recorded here rather than fixed, on the same principle as the register waiver above: a decision on the record beats a silent correction.

What is being accepted, stated at full strength so nobody re-derives it as smaller than it is. This is NOT a scanner artefact like the 8 waived register hits — those are invisible to a teacher. This one is visible in the room: a Class VIII teacher serving viii ch 01 at X=6 gives her class "Narrative Essays and a Limerick of Their Own" as sitting 5, then in sitting 6 asks them to draft the same narrative essay from an outline they were never asked to make, and introduces the limerick form as though it were new. It is the only accepted defect in this stage that a real class can hit. Scope is exactly one serve of one chapter — X=6 on a [8, 5] library; X=8 (identity) and X=5 are unaffected, and the other 43 seams are clean.

Why accepting is defensible here. The remedy is a re-author (~₹30), and regenerating is a lottery (founder, 2026-08-02) — the S11/ARV-D-136 precedent came back clean but nothing guarantees a second draw does, and a fresh top would void this chapter's W1 register repair and could arrive with new hits of its own. Against that: one serve, of one chapter, in a stage of 46. The cost of the ruling is that it must not be forgotten, which is what this entry is for.

What this ruling does NOT license. It is scoped to viii ch 01. The underlying shape — a TOP canonical whose synthesis unit touches the WRITING spine — is now the second sighting (english·IX ch 7 was the first, and was re-authored). Two stages, two chapters, one cause. If a third appears at S9 (english·preparatory), the finding is no longer a per-chapter defect but a property of how english LP constitutions build the closing unit, and the remedy moves upstream to Rule 1's closing-unit exception rather than to another ₹30 re-author. The english·preparatory F1 should read its synthesis units for the writing spine FIRST, before anything else.

F2.comment:
S10 · classes vi/vii/viii · 2026-08-15. THE RESOLVER GATE PASSED FIRST, and it was the thing that could have wasted the whole exercise: 46/46 chapters resolve to exactly ONE textbook PDF, and all 46 carry _source_unit.unit_chapter_number — so the split mapping is real, not a silent fallback to the plan's own number. english·middle is the stage whose record originally said the resolver could find the book for NO english chapter (ARV-D-155); S11 fixed it and this run is middle's proof. A wrong book scores ~0% and reads as a clean pass, which is the most expensive way for this check to fail — so the count was verified BEFORE the scan, not after.

TEST 1 — verbatim reproduction. 121 canonicals · 471,898 teacher-facing words · 126 runs ≥10 words · 1,540 matched words = 0.33%. Longest single run 24 words. Against english·secondary's 2.51% and longest-126, this stage is an order of magnitude cleaner. copyright_scan.py --book-only throughout, so the figure is against the PROTECTED WORK alone and never against Aruvi's own summary.

And most of the shortlist is not quotation at all. Of the 31 runs ≥14 words: ~12 are textbook EXERCISE APPARATUS — the "24-word longest match" is fifteen separate contractions (i'll it's don't i'm i'd he's…) from a grammar drill, plus idiom lists, distance-word lists, verb lists, a list of Indian women's names, and fill-in sentence frames. Four are the textbook's own comprehension questions restated as the teacher's task; four are format templates (diary headers, a notice); ~11 are genuine short narrative quotations, all attributed in their own sentence and none over 16 words. The n-gram normaliser strips apostrophes and joins adjacent list items, which is what inflates a drill list into a "24-word run" — worth knowing before the next stage reads its own shortlist.

TEST 2 — third-party material: 0 URLs · 0 external-image instructions · 0 brand names (the two brand hits were the verb "zoom in"). TEST 3 — attribution: clean.

THE ONE FINDING — verse reproduced in MCQ OPTIONS, and it is a GAP in the poem-locator rule, not a breach of it. vi/ch_05_canonical_p09.json item Q-RFC-B-1 (A Friend's Prayer): the stem asks "Which line from the poem most clearly expresses this idea?" and three of four options are couplets copied verbatim — "I'll try all that a friend can do / To make their wishes come true.", "Let me use my heart to see, / To realise what friends can be.", "May my friendships always be / The most important thing to me." 41 words of published NCERT verse in one item, inside a canonical — the one artefact class that reaches the cloud, which is F2's whole concern.
The 2026-08-12 amendment closed the STIMULUS (Read lines N–M on p.PP, beginning "<incipit>", 8-word cap, lines copied into no field) and says nothing about OPTIONS. This item's question FORM structurally requires reproducing lines to work at all. Measured across the stage: 1 of 1,462 items (231 option-bearing) — a narrow gap, not a systemic one.

RULING (founder, 2026-08-15): ACCEPT the item as authored, AND CLOSE THE GAP AT S9. The item stands. The poem-locator rule is extended to OPTIONS at english·preparatory's P2 — where it is free, because no S9 library exists yet and its 39 chapters are unbought. No english stage carries a signed GATE, so §9 re-opens nothing today; done later it would cost a re-author per affected library. This is the same "do it while it is free" reasoning that put the original poem-locator amendment into all three english assessment constitutions on 2026-08-12 ahead of their P-preps.
OWED AT S9's P2, and it must not be lost: extend the poem-locator prohibition to cover OPTION text and any other item field that can carry a line, not just the stimulus. The "which line from the poem" question form should be re-expressed as a locator ("Which of the following ideas does the poem express in lines 5–6?") so the option text carries paraphrase, not verse.

NOT DEFECTS, ruled and recorded so they are not re-litigated. viii ch 8 quotes four imperative lines from The Magic Brush across three canonicals — but that unit TEACHES falling intonation on those lines, each is 3–5 words, and each is attributed ("the poem's own commands"). You cannot teach the intonation without saying the line. vi ch 8's closing two-line stanza ("I don't know how the world is made / And neither do my neighbours") is attributed as "the poem's final stanza" and was already cleared by that chapter's own C14 on 2026-08-13.

W1.comment:
S11 · classes iii/iv/v · 2026-08-15. 39 chapters, 38 top canonicals, ₹375.43, 38/38 ok (III ch 11 correctly skipped — the 2026-08-13 pilot was already installed with its full ladder 12/10/7).

THE FIRST ENGLISH LIBRARY EVER AUTHORED UNDER THE PAIR RULE AT PREPARATORY (assessment v1.5). It held, and was asserted by measurement rather than by eye: 186 of 188 cells carry exactly 2 items; 0 pairs disagree on source_lo; and unit_ref / period_ref / period_number / phase_ref appear on ZERO items — the Rule 8A prohibition verified across the whole corpus, not sampled. Density 0.87 items/unit against english·secondary's pre-amendment 0.35. The two 4-item cells (III ch 3 A|oracy, III ch 15 B|word_work) are TWO correct pairs sharing one (section × spine) address — the cell key is coarser than source_lo — not a rule breach.

C5 check 11 caught a defect class nothing else was looking for. It first read 37/39, with V ch 8 and V ch 9 reporting "no section list readable". The cause was not a missing marker: both chapter summaries were UNPARSEABLE JSON — 12 and 4 unescaped " inside quoted dialogue ("I sold only the well, not the water."; "Bangles, crystal bangles!"), each duplicated across tasks_verbatim and a question_bank stem. Generation never noticed, because prompt_assembly.read_file embeds the summary as raw TEXT — so the plans are sound and every anchor check passes. Only JSON-parsing consumers went blind, and check 11 advised rather than failed, so it would have entered the tracker as "unreadable" rather than "broken". Repaired to \" (the convention every other summary already uses), verified as pure escaping — strip backslashes from backup and repaired file and the diff is 0 lines, +12 and +4 bytes exactly. 39/39 PASS after. A JSON-parse assertion belongs in the chapter pipeline; two of 39 shipped broken and nothing caught it.

FAIL census: 17 register ban hits across 14 of 39 files — 1 per 2.8 files, dead on the runbook's expected 1-in-3. Families: clock 8 · forward 6 · meta-leak 2 · calendar 1. The clock family has a preparatory-specific shape worth carrying: every hit is a duration inside a READING or DISCUSSION instruction ("re-read silently for two minutes"), never the "for the remaining time" boilerplate the middle-stage sets struck — at classes III–V the model bounds a task because young children need it bounded.

16 repairs declared and applied (repair_register.py v1.8, free, all old→new by assertion). 1 struck: III ch 13 U2 foreshadows — narrative structure inside the story, both warning and trouble read in the same unit; founder ruling ignore, handle as it arises. One edit REPLACES rather than deletes (IV ch 6 U11 "do tomorrow" → "start doing").

Two engine findings this wave produced. (1) 2 STARVED assessment cells — cell_resolver's dispersion guard is M≥N, and everything failing it fell to the shared-span branch, collapsing every item onto the closing unit while the earlier sittings that teach the cell showed no Assess tab. Fixed by _backfill() (founder: back-fill to close, do not touch the constitution), 132 carrier tests green. W2.comment:
Compacts landed 2026-08-15. 68 requests, ₹718.21, 68/68 ok, 0 re-bought; library complete went to 39/39 PASS — 109 canonicals on disk (39 tops + 70 compacts).

ONE FILE WAS QUARANTINED, AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE FINDING. IV ch 3 p07 failed first-visit order follows the registry. Its cell order is registry positions [0, 2, 3, 4] — strictly ascending. Nothing is taught early. It failed because build_library.py:421 treats a GAP in the frontier (r[0] > seen_hi + 1) as a skipped section, so dropping a middle cell trips the ORDER check. The same file produced the batch's only OMITS line — the check built precisely to report drops as "reported, not gated — rule at the human gate", above a comment saying a compact legitimately teaches less. The two checks contradict each other, and the ORDER message misdiagnoses.

Recurrence was measured before re-authoring, not assumed. Every other compact on disk teaches all 5 cells at every size — 17 of 17 other 7-period compacts, and the 5-period ones too — so 7 periods is not a squeeze. The brief is sound and identical in shape to the one that produced the passing p09. The latent cause: the compact brief never says every registry cell must be TAUGHT — only that references be verbatim and first appear in registry order. The model broke no instruction it was given. Re-authored for ₹7.63: 7 units, all 5 cells including oracy, positions [0,1,2,3,4] ascending AND gapless, 0 register hits. The quarantined copy is kept as the cost record and carries 0 register hits, so runbook trap 1 does not bite.

FAIL census: 32 ban hits across 24 of 70 compacts — 1 per 2.9 files, statistically identical to W1's 1-per-2.8. Families: clock 19 · forward 9 · completion 2 · meta-leak 2.

CLOCK ROSE FROM 8-of-17 TO 19-of-32 BETWEEN WAVES, same shape both times. A shorter plan makes every band feel tighter, so the model reaches for a duration more often. This is a BRIEF problem, not a model problem, and the next preparatory stage should say so upfront rather than pay for 27 repairs twice.

COMPLETION APPEARED FOR THE FIRST TIME AT THIS STAGE — and it can only ever appear on compacts. Both hits are in a compact's CLOSING unit ("built across the chapter"). A top's closing unit is the mandated synthesis, which the completion ban EXEMPTS by design; a compact is FORBIDDEN a synthesis anchor, so its last unit does the same summing-up job with none of the licence. Expect this family on every compact wave; it will never show on a top.

META-LEAK HELD AT 2 — on 70 files against W1's 2 on 38, i.e. 0.9 per 1000 units. Third corpus confirming the corrected variant_plans._serving_block().

29 repairs declared and applied (v1.9); 3 struck (see WAIVER). One REPLACES rather than deletes (V ch 6 p08 U1 — deleting the sentence would lose "unhurried", the actual instruction).

The _backfill fix earned its keep here: 18 cells would have collapsed onto their closing unit under the old rule, against 2 in W1 — exactly as predicted for shorter plans. Library-wide assessment coverage 808/972 units = 83.1%.

F1.comment:
S11 · english·preparatory · 2026-08-15. ZERO JUMPY across 22 borrowed seams. Founder ruling: accept and close.

ENUMERATED, NOT SAMPLED — so there is no sample size to defend, per the step's own standing instruction. borrowed_seams.py english iii iv v swept every X in [floor−2 … top+2] at the class-standard 40 min across all 39 chapters:
  • 358 serves swept
  • 187 produced no borrow at all (identity / truncation / surrender)
  • 149 SELF-FILLS excluded — the Xth slot filled from the plan being served, so the borrowed unit's priors are that plan's OWN earlier units. No foreign prior, nothing to read. This is 87% of all borrows, which is the e14 SELF-FIRST tie-break working exactly as designed.
  • 22 cross-canonical seams — every one read in FULL, X−1 and X back to back as a teacher meets them on two consecutive days. Dump preserved at genon/out/f1_english_preparatory_seams.txt (103k chars, 1,171 lines).

RATINGS: CLEAN 12 · SERVICEABLE 10 · JUMPY 0.

TWO CONSTRAINTS HELD PERFECTLY. (1) Zero positional references in all 22 borrowed units — not one "last unit", "next lesson", "as we saw in the previous sitting". (2) The self-guard clause is doing real work: ten borrowed units carry an explicit one ("by name and concept rather than by reference to any earlier activity"; "no specific earlier activity needs to have occurred"), and every unit carrying one rated CLEAN bar two.

ALL TEN SERVICEABLES ARE ONE CONSTRUCTION, and it lives in the TEACHER NOTE, not the bands: a "this synthesis draws on…" list that opens with content strands and slides into a named activity — "the food-basket sort" (iii ch 13) · "the Spellathon" and "the noun sorting" (v ch 07) · "the outdoor-play discussion" (iii ch 07) · "the clue-word writing from the park activity" (iii ch 09) · "the 'difficult side' writing theme explored earlier" (v ch 09). Because it is framing copy rather than an instruction it never blocks a teacher — it only tells her the class did something it may not have. The remedy is ONE authoring rule, upstream in the brief, not ten repairs: in the draws-on list, name the IDEA, never the TASK. Carried to the next stage rather than repaired here (founder).

THE ONE CASE THAT WAS FIRST RATED JUMPY, AND WHY IT WAS DOWNGRADED — the founder's read, and it is the methodological point of this step. iv ch 1 X=9: the served 10p plan gives U1–U8 and the borrowed 12p synthesis REPLACES the 10p plan's own U9, which is "Craft — Creating a Symbol of Togetherness". The borrowed unit's note says "the three strands of the chapter (poem, word work, craft)" and its closing riddle answers "the paper figure" — so the text points at the very lesson the serve arithmetic removed (units 1–8 contain zero occurrences of paper / fold / craft / figure). Claude rated this JUMPY. Founder: the PHASES do not require the activity to have happened — corroborated on three independent checks: materials lists only Textbook pp. 1–8, notebooks, blackboard with no artefact (a genuine dependency would appear there); band 2 reads "one thing they made or talked about", and the disjunction gives every class a legal path; and band 4's riddle is teacher-posed with the answers supplied, so a missing third answer deflates but never halts. The defect is ASSERTION, not DEPENDENCY — text stating something false for this serve, not an instruction a teacher cannot carry out — which is SERVICEABLE by the rubric. Worth keeping the distinction: a unit that NAMES a prior activity is not the same failure as one that NEEDS it, and only the second is what killed the earlier architectures. One nuance recorded against the eventual fix: iv ch 1 is the only case where the leaked list-item reached a CLASS-FACING line (the riddle clue "I show togetherness when you unfold me"), not merely the teacher's note. Accepted as authored, unrepaired, founder 2026-08-15.

ONE NON-JUMPINESS FINDING, ACCEPTED: a REPETITION risk no check looks for. english iv ch 12 carries a fort-jigsaw craft in all three canonicals — 10p U9 "Fact Paragraph and Fort Puzzle" · 8p U8 "Fort Jigsaw Puzzle: Make and Play" · 6p U6 "Fort Jigsaw Craft". At X=9 the 10p plan borrows the 8p's jigsaw unit, so a class can meet the same craft as both its own U9 and the borrowed U10. Not a continuity breach and not in F1's remit — the serve is structurally correct — but nothing in certification tests whether a borrowed unit DUPLICATES one the prefix already taught. Recorded as a standing gap; accepted for this stage.

S11 · english·preparatory · 2026-08-15. Founder ruling: ACCEPTED, F2 CLOSED for this stage — "they are short and within inverted commas", on the same reasoning as the extract-analysis precedent (a full paragraph quoted word-for-word was left standing because the analysis would have been incomplete without it).

FIRST ENGLISH STAGE EVER MEASURED AGAINST THE CORRECT TEXTBOOKS. The copyright review records that copyright_scan.py "cannot find the book for ANY English chapter" — its PDF resolver assumed plan chapter number == PDF number, which the split breaks, and at preparatory it was worse than nothing (III has 12 unit-PDFs against 17 split chapters, so the numbering spaces COLLIDE and split ch 11 resolved to a DIFFERENT chapter's book, scoring ~0% and reading as a clean pass). That resolver was fixed at S9 via _source_unit.unit_chapter_number, and this is the first stage to run under the fix. Verified before use: III ch 11 now resolves to chapter 07 - The Big Laddoo.pdf, III ch 17 to chapter 12 - Chandrayaan.pdf. S10's english·middle figures were obtained by pointing at the PDF by hand; these were not.

TEST 1 — verbatim reproduction. 109 canonicals, 243,371 teacher-facing words, shingled n=8 against the 39 chapter PDFs:
maths·middleenglish·middleenglish·prep
book-matched words1.15%1.64%1.59%
longest run18w14w32w
runs in assessment items—044
369 runs total (325 LP · 44 item), 254 distinct strings. The aggregate is in line with two subjects that carry no F2 finding; the two outliers are the longest run and the item count.

TEST 2 — third-party material: CLEAN. 0 URLs, 0 brand mentions, 0 external images across all 109 files.

TEST 3 — attribution: CLEAN. 1,126 of 1,128 in-class tasks carry a (p.NN)/pp. locator = 99.8%.

THE POEM RULE, MEASURED BY READING — because an 8-gram scan is blind to it by construction. Measured against each summary's own poem_text: 79 hits across 30 plans in 14 poem chapters; worst single file III ch 7 top at 8 of 11 distinct lines (73%), then IV ch 7 top 41%, IV ch 7 p09 35%, III ch 15 top 44%, IV ch 1 top 40%. Field split: band text 60 · teacher_notes 19 · homework 0. Full coordinates, every line quoted, at genon/out/f2_english_preparatory_lp_poem_coordinates.txt.

WHY THE ASSESSMENT CAP DID NOT COVER THIS, and it is structural rather than a model failure. The poem cap exists in exactly ONE place — assessment Rule 3, scoped by name to four ASSESSMENT fields (item_stem, visual_stimulus, suggested_answer, rubric). The english LP constitutions carry no equivalent rule (grepped for reproduc/verbatim/copy/ incipit/copyright: the only hit governs task_text, not verse). And the LP is HANDED the poem — poem_text is a declared input and Rule 160 directs "poem → read-aloud + repeated/choral reading". The split in the evidence follows the split in the rules exactly: 101 poem lines in LP fields against 11 in assessment items (~9:1). The 2026-08-12 poem-locator amendment (ARV-D-138) landed in all three english ASSESSMENT constitutions and in none of the LP constitutions.

WHY IT PRESENTS WORSE HERE THAN AT MIDDLE. The conduit did not widen — the denominator shrank. Preparatory poems run 36–132 words against middle's 17 lines, so identical behaviour consumes a far larger fraction of the work.

THE RULING, AND WHAT IT RESTS ON. Claude first reported this as a probable F2 breach and recommended against closing. The founder read the instances and ruled otherwise, and the reading supports the ruling: every poem-line instance is QUOTED AND FUNCTIONAL — inside inverted commas, naming the lines the teacher must read, chant or point to, with a maximum of 3 lines (~12 words) in any single string. Representative: "highlights the paired lines: 'We run and skip / We jump and sway / We slide and swing.' Students repeat each pair twice"; "the poem says 'win or lose, we always share' — what does sharing a loss feel like?". There is no instance of a poem dumped as text for its own sake. Claude's earlier hypothesis of "distributed accumulation with no framing purpose" was advanced BEFORE reading the strings and is withdrawn on the record.

TWO MEASUREMENT CORRECTIONS, recorded so the numbers are not over-trusted. (1) The first ranking counted REFRAINS once per occurrence, producing impossibilities (III ch 5 read "24 of 14 lines") and inflating IV ch 1 to "100%". Re-run on DISTINCT lines: III ch 5 falls from worst to 11%, IV ch 1 to 40%, corpus worst case from ~100% to 73%. (2) The 44 assessment-item runs are NOT poem lines — reading them shows story facts in MCQ options and riddles in visual_stimulus ("thirty white horses on a red hill…", IV ch 4); poem lines in items number 11, across 4 files. The constitutional firewall bent, it did not break.

ONE FINDING CARRIED FORWARD, NOT ACTED ON (founder: close, it's fine). The corpus's longest run — 32 words, III ch 8 p09 U3 band[2] — is the poem My Top reproduced ENTIRE, inline, labelled "transcript": "teacher recites the poem 'My Top' (Textbook p. 51, transcript: 'My Top. Red and green, … Along with it, I jump around.')". It differs from every other instance in two ways worth keeping on the record even under an accept ruling: it is 100% of the work rather than an extract of a longer one (proportion-of-the-whole being the usual operative test), and it arrives through a permission the constitution grants explicitly — the oracy carve-out licensing the generator to read transcript_text. Note the poem is not in poem_text at all (ch 8's section is typed prose), so this is a SECOND conduit, independent of the poem-line one. 19 of 39 preparatory chapters carry a transcript_text, so it recurs by design. Accepted here; the natural remedy if it is ever taken up is one line mirroring assessment Rule 3 — a transcript is LOCATED, never TRANSCRIBED.

defects.title: Stale serve cache: in-place repairs do not invalidate already-served plans
defects.evidence: C6 run 2026-08-03. The X=8 request returned ch_03_50m8_e12_c20260803142658.json - a cache entry written at 17:58, i.e. BEFORE the 18:07 register repair and BEFORE the 19:28 option normalization. Scanned now, that served plan carries 1 REGISTER BAN (p10 U2's 'previewing the climate change thread', the breach repaired at 18:07) and 5 UNARRANGED MCQs. Every other row served fresh and is clean: 50m9, 50m11, 50m13, 50m6, 60m4-50m6, 45m10 all scan 0 bans / 0 unarranged. | CONFIRMED BY THE FOUNDER: the 21:02 clean re-serve only happened because he DELETED the cached file first. A repeat request alone does not re-derive - the cache hit short-circuits before serving.
defects.notes: ROOT CAUSE: the cache key is {matrix}_e{engine}_c{canonical ledger_ts}. Repair tools (repair_anchors, repair_register, normalize_options) change canonical CONTENT in place without touching the ledger timestamp or the engine version, so the key is unchanged and the stale derived plan is served forever. This is the gap between certification and serving: build_library certifies the LIBRARY clean while the teacher-facing path serves pre-repair bytes. It will recur at every stage that repairs anything. OPTIONS: (a) add a content fingerprint of the source canonicals to the cache key - old files stay valid for whoever holds them but every new serve is fresh; (b) purge the chapter's derived ch_NN_*_e*_c*.json whenever a repair or normalize stage runs - simplest, but breaks My Lessons links for plans teachers already hold; (c) key on max(genon_canonical.repairs[].at). Founder call needed. Whatever is chosen, the ch 3 derived plans served before 19:37 need re-serving. | FIXED 2026-08-03 in api/data.py canonical_version(): the repair set now joins the cache key. Any genon_canonical.repairs[] entry appends r{count}{sha1[:4]}, so a repair MINTS A NEW ENTRY instead of being served from an old one - ch 3's keys are now c20260803141938r45661 (standard, 4 repairs), c20260803142658r307eb (p10, 3), c20260803143426r31fa7 (p07, 3). Chosen deliberately over purging: the derived plans a teacher already holds keep their filenames and their My Lessons links, exactly the promise canonical_version's own docstring makes about regeneration - the repaired version is offered as a new file, never substituted underneath her. This is the same failure handoff_rev was added for, one step later; the docstring anticipated it and the repair tools outran it. Test added: tests/test_genon_plan_key.py::test_repairs_rekey (a repair re-keys, a second repair re-keys again, keys stable, ledger run still readable in the key). test_genon_serve + test_genon_duration_order still green. No GENON_ENGINE_VERSION bump - served BYTES are unchanged, only the key. RECHECK OWED: one serve through the API to confirm the new filename is written and the old ch_03_50m8_e12_c20260803142658.json is left untouched for whoever holds it. | CLOSED at C10 (2026-08-03): the recheck ran against the live API - X=8 after the repairs wrote ch_03_50m8_e13_c20260803142658r307eb.json with cached false, the old e12 file untouched, and the immediate repeat returned cached true with mtime frozen. | RE-OPENED AND RE-FIXED 2026-08-04 (founder): the repair fingerprint in the cache key is REVERTED - it hung an unreadable hash tail off every served filename. The invariant moved to genon/purge_derived.py: a canonical change deletes the chapter's derived plans (ch_NN_<matrix>_e*_c*.json only - never a canonical, never another chapter), called automatically from repair_register, repair_anchors and normalize_options. Names are plain again (ch_03_50m8_e13_c20260803142658.json) and the next request rebuilds in ~11 ms. Accepted cost: a teacher holding a purged plan loses it and re-prepares; the plans listing walks the directory, so her dangling register key is skipped rather than erroring (30 such keys exist today across kumar1/2/3, My Lessons unaffected). test_genon_plan_key::test_repairs_do_not_rekey pins both halves (key stable across repairs; purge pattern never matches a canonical). (1) Unit DROPPED (below floor, X=6): the unit is rendered on screen as self-study, so its items should RIDE WITH IT - anchor them to the dropped unit and show them in its block. (2) Unit simply NOT SERVED (a prefix shorter than the chosen canonical, X=8/9/11): the item's SECTION is still taught by some served unit. Checked on X=8 - all seven orphans' chapter_sections ('Elements of Weather and Climate', 'Punjab Floods 2025', 'Climate Change / Punjab Floods') ARE served elsewhere in that plan, so a fallback from unit-anchor to SECTION-anchor would recover all seven and restore the exact counts. defects.title: Item type reverts to what the section's testable content can bear; the LO, not the tag or the format, is what overstates — CLOSED, no action
defects.detail:
MEMORY item 9's contract for assessment/science/secondary is 'check demand-tag drives format'. Rule 5: 'Application -> SCR (correct multi-step chain; the steps are the object, so selection cannot reveal them)'. TOP S6 and S9, and p10 S9, each carry exactly ONE item — an MCQ tagged Application. Rule 5's anchor-MCQ allowance does not cover them: it permits an MCQ ALONGSIDE an extended item on a rich section, and these sections have no second item. p07 is clean, so the constitution does hold at the floor count. Note the substantive cost the rule is protecting: an Application item is meant to expose the multi-step chain, and a four-option MCQ cannot.
SECOND, SEPARATE OBSERVATION — a genuine TENSION INSIDE THE CONSTITUTION, not a model failure. Rule 4 says cognitive_demand is classified PER SECTION and 'record the result as cognitive_demand on EVERY question for that section'. Rule 5 says a rich section MAY carry more than one item and MAY MIX TYPES — but format follows demand, so mixing types within a section REQUIRES mixing demands, which Rule 4 forbids. The TOP does exactly this on both its doubled sections: S3 carries MCQ@Analysis + SCR@Application, S10 carries SCR@Application + ECR@Analysis. Either reading is defensible from the text. Needs a founder ruling on which rule yields, and the loser amended — it will recur at every stage that allows a second item.

★ FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-06 — ACCEPTED, NO ACTION, and the diagnosis is re-pointed. Reading the three items against the constitution's own RATIONALE rather than its table: Rule 5 justifies Application->SCR because 'the steps are the object, so selection cannot reveal them'. That rationale does NOT bite on one-step arithmetic. TOP S6 is '²³₁₁Na — how many neutrons?' (23-11=12, a single subtraction); TOP S9 and p10 S9 are 'config 2,8,2 -> valency and pathway', one inference from the outer shell. An MCQ reveals those completely. So the FORMAT is defensible in all three cases and is STABLE across the library — every canonical chose MCQ for valency and for symbols.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNSTABLE IS THE TAG, and Rule 4's reading guide cannot separate the candidates: 'determine' sits in the Application list, 'explain (one-step)' and 'classify' in Understanding, and valency-from-configuration answers to both. The proof is that TOP's Application item and p07's Understanding item are NEARLY THE SAME QUESTION — same element (magnesium), same configuration (2,8,2), same ask. Only the label moved. Founder's reading: the chapter's content is strictly numerical and definitional, so it resists SCR, and the pressure surfaces as tag creep rather than format failure.
CORRECTION TO C4'S OWN EVIDENCE, recorded for honesty: 8.4 Symbols was cited as the same section tagged differently (TOP Application, p10 Recall). It is not — the two canonicals assessed DIFFERENT CONTENT from that section. TOP asks the neutron arithmetic; p10 asks why iron is Fe and not Ir (IUPAC/Latin convention). Each tag matches its own question. The genuine same-task drift is 8.8 Valency alone.
COMPLIANCE IN CONTEXT: 26 of 29 items match the hinge exactly, and all 3 exceptions are one-step MCQs the rationale exempts. No action; carried as a known property of this stage. If it is ever revisited, the amendment belongs in RULE 4's spectrum (pin the tag to the section, or sharpen the verb lists), NOT in Rule 5's format table.

★ RE-READ 2026-08-06 AT FOUNDER'S REQUEST — READ THE LOs, AND THE ACCEPTANCE ABOVE DOES NOT SURVIVE IT. Claude's 'one-step, so the SCR rationale does not bite' defence was wrong for valency, and the p07 case is the opposite of what it looked like.
TOP 8.8 implied_lo: 'Students can PREDICT the combining capacity of an atom by APPLYING the octet rule to its electronic configuration and DISTINGUISHING between electron loss, gain, and sharing pathways.' Rule 4's guide puts 'apply' in Application and 'distinguish' in Analysis, so the tag is if anything CONSERVATIVE. And the task is not one step: the handoff's activity_summary and U10's own band 28-40 spell out a four-stage chain students are told to record — 'configuration -> valence electron count -> action (lose/gain/share) -> valency'. That is precisely the case Rule 5's rationale describes: 'the steps are the object, so selection cannot reveal them'. The MCQ conceals the chain. THE MISMATCH IS REAL. p10 8.8 is the same ('determine an atom's valency by applying the octet rule').
p07 8.8 IS THE WORSE CASE, NOT THE COMPLIANT ONE. Its own implied_lo reads 'Students can DETERMINE the combining capacity ... by reasoning from its electron configuration', and its activity_summary says students 'APPLY the same reasoning to novel elements' — both squarely Application on Rule 4's list. It is tagged UNDERSTANDING. So the tag was lowered to fit the format the model wanted, which breaks Rule 4's own requirement that the tag 'MUST be derived from and consistent with the section's implied_lo'. It did not fall into line; it was filed down. This failure mode is INVISIBLE to any format check, because tag and format agree with each other while both disagree with the LO.
TOP 8.4 SYMBOLS IS A THIRD, MILDER CASE. Its LO — 'apply a rule-governed symbolic notation system to ENCODE AND DECODE quantitative information' — and its task ('practise reading and writing standard nuclide notation to determine proton, electron, and neutron counts') justify Application. Here the item is not mis-FORMATTED so much as under-sampled: a single subtraction (23-11) stands in for encode-and-decode. An SCR would have matched.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE C4 NUMBER: '26 of 29 match the hinge' overstated compliance. p07 S6 passes the hinge only because its tag was moved, so on Rule 4's consistency test it fails too.
WHAT IS NOW PROPOSED, and it is cheap: the loose joint is that NOTHING CHECKS THE TAG AGAINST THE LO. That is mechanically checkable — Rule 4 already publishes the verb->band table, so the certifier can flag any item whose implied_lo's strongest verb outranks its cognitive_demand. It would have caught all three cases here and needs no model call. Founder decision: (a) add the tag-vs-LO gate and re-accept the items, (b) regenerate, or (c) accept knowingly with the corrected reasoning on the record.

★ FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-06 — CLOSED AT S3, NO ACTION, AND THE ROOT CAUSE IS PLACED UPSTREAM OF BOTH EARLIER READINGS.
The founder's diagnosis: LO -> demand tag is STABLE and reads correctly against the summary slice, exceptions aside. What moves is the QUESTION TYPE, and it moves because of what the section actually offers to test. Valency is the clean example — the section's testable content is a short rule application, so however the LO is worded the item reverts to what the content can bear, which is an MCQ. On this reading the overstatement sits in the LEARNING OUTCOME: 'predict ... by applying the octet rule ... and distinguishing between electron loss, gain and sharing pathways' promises more operational breadth than the section supplies. The tag then faithfully follows the overstated LO, and the item honestly follows the content — so the mismatch is a symptom, not the disease.
WHY NOT FORCE THE HINGE: mandating SCR wherever the tag says Application would produce a padded multi-step question on content that has one real step. That trades a visible mismatch for an invisible one — a worse question that passes the gate. The tag-vs-LO certifier gate Claude proposed is DECLINED for the same reason: it would police the tag against the LO while leaving the LO itself unexamined, which is the wrong end.
CARRIED, NOT ACTIONED: if this is real it is an LP RULE 6 (LO derivation) question, not an assessment Rule 4 or Rule 5 one, and it should show up as a pattern rather than a case — LOs routinely outrunning their sections' testable content. Cheap future test at other stages: where an item's type falls below its tag, read the LO against the summary slice and ask which of the two overstated. One chapter cannot answer it.
STATUS: closed. C4 passes with this defect closed rather than accepted-open.

defects.title: Served science.secondary plans lost their assessment container - every question printed under every sitting

FIX: route the filter through the seam, and put the WRAPPER BACK - the science port reads it to decide the plan is secondary, so returning a bare list would have re-created ARV-D-060 inside the export. VERIFIED: 30/30 200, zero tracebacks, anchors in the exported view resolve 1..6 / 1..7 / 1..12 (a middle-stage join would have orphaned them), SS unchanged, suite unchanged (test_genon_carriers, test_genon_serve, test_science_port, test_link_resolver-adjacent all pass; the 4 red tests are pre-existing missing-fixture/env: english/iv and science-middle saved plans cleared from disk, httpx2 absent, test_api's 'expected at least one saved science plan'). C12 was blocked by this and is now unblocked.

defects.title: Assessment anchoring is recomputed at display time through a plan-local mediator (section number) instead of reading the unit identity the engine already stamped - FIXED e16
defects.evidence: PRE-FIX on a clean HEAD: SS·IX X=9 and SS·VIII X=12 (real cross-plan synthesis borrows) served 1 and 2 questions on a borrowed sitting with ZERO handoff rows for it - coverage stopped at sitting 8/11. POST-FIX: 4 rows each, handoff spans every sitting. Anchor half proven by tests/test_borrowed_anchor.py, which fails against HEAD and against serve-fixed-but-old-port.
defects.notes:
RAISED TO S1 BY THE FOUNDER 2026-08-06, and the remedy changed with it. My first remedy - restore the lender's handoff row alongside the borrowed unit - was the WRONG fix: it repairs the mediator instead of removing it. Founder's objection, and it is correct: the section is a MEDIATING VARIABLE the platform does not control. The LLM is free to cut and merge sections against the time it is given, so `section_number` means something different in every canonical of the same chapter (measured on ch 8: p12 S3 = 8.2.2 gold foil, p07 S3 = 8.2.3 Bohr; S2-S7 all disagree), and some subjects have no numbered sections at all, only descriptions. Anything joined through it at render time is joined through a key whose meaning is plan-local.

THE PROPERTY THAT SHOULD HOLD, in the founder's words: if p07 U7 is filled with p12 U11, the question indexed to p12 U11 must be brought along - and stay attached to it. Unit identity, carried, not recomputed.

THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY AGREES; THE DISPLAY DOES NOT. genon stamps the true answer onto every served item - compile.py::_anchor_items writes `unit_ref`, serve.py writes `period_ref = [sitting]`, INCLUDING for a borrowed unit (serve.py:566-573). Verified on disk this run: every item in every served science.ix plan carries a correct period_ref. But the science port throws that stamp away and recomputes: subject.py:315, `linked = period_index.get(int(gnum), [])`, joining section_number through the CHOSEN plan's coverage_handoff. Same at english/subject.py:299 and mathematics/subject.py:248,290 (their own mediators - spine/section codes). Social Sciences and TWAU do the right thing already - `stamp(meta, as_list(it.get('period_ref')), lo)`, the item names its own unit - which is exactly why neither ever met this defect.

REMEDY (proposed, not yet built): DERIVE ONCE, STAMP, READ THE STAMP. One precedence rule in the shared link_resolver - if the item carries a platform-stamped period_ref/unit_ref, that IS the anchor; only when it does not (an un-served library file, where the plan is self-consistent and the derivation is safe) run the subject's join. Subject-agnostic, so all three carrier families get it, and it makes the other four subjects behave the way SS and TWAU already do. The mediator survives only as the one-time derivation it was meant to be. SECOND HALF, do not miss it: the view also GROUPS by the mediator (science/subject.py:300-307 keys groups on section_number and takes the label from the first item to claim that number), so a borrowed item would be absorbed into a wrong-labelled group even once its anchor is right - group on the item's own section_label, or on the resolved unit.

FOUNDER ON THE CACHE COST: not an issue. Non-canonical variants are not kept permanently; re-verification is to re-run SS.secondary, SS.middle and science.secondary on the plans that carry a borrowed unit, only to confirm the fix went through cleanly.

Still LATENT on ch 8 - the sole cross-plan borrow is X=8's rescue of the TOP's synthesis unit, which carries no questions, so nothing crosses today. S1 is about what the mechanism does the first time a borrowed unit carries a question: attach it to the wrong lesson, or to none, silently.

--- FIXED 2026-08-06 (founder authorised the engine change; cache churn accepted). AND IT WAS NOT LATENT. ---

THE HALF THAT WAS ALREADY LIVE, on two CERTIFIED stages. Re-serving the real corpus turned up
two genuine cross-plan borrows that DO carry questions: SS·IX ch 3 X=9 (chosen p10, closes on
p12's synthesis unit - 1 question on the borrowed sitting) and SS·VIII ch 3 X=12 (chosen p13,
closes on p16's synthesis - 2 questions). Measured against a clean HEAD checkout, PRE-FIX:
handoff rows for the borrowed sitting = 0, and the plan's coverage stopped at sitting 8 and 11
respectively while questions were being asked on sitting 9 and 12. POST-FIX: 4 rows each, the
handoff spans every sitting. So both SS stages have been serving a closing sitting that asks
questions the plan claims no learning outcome for - exactly the identity serve.py's own
dropped-unit comment says must never break. No teacher SAW a misplaced question in SS (SS is
item-self-sufficient: its items carry period_ref and its port has always read it), and the LP
never displays LOs, so this was invisible on screen and would surface only in a coverage audit
- but it was real, it was shipped, and it is now closed. The ANCHOR half remains latent on the
current corpus: science·secondary is the only handoff-bridged stage certified so far and its one
cross-plan borrow carries no items.

WHAT WAS BUILT (4 files, engine bumped e15 -> e16):
1. aruvi_core/link_resolver.py - `platform_anchor(item)`: the platform's own stamp
   (period_ref, then unit_ref) beats every subject join. Documented with the measured drift.
2. The three joining ports now read it first and fall back to their own mediator only for an
   UN-SERVED library file: science/subject.py:315, english/subject.py:299 (the positional
   pairing counter still advances, so a stamped item cannot shift its siblings),
   mathematics/subject.py:248 and :290. social_sciences and the_world_around_us were already
   correct and are untouched - they are the reference behaviour this makes universal.
3. science/subject.py grouping now keys on the item's OWN section_label, not on the mediating
   number (the heading half of the defect).
4. serve.py carries a borrowed SERVED unit's handoff row, remapped to the fill sitting, with an
   `_order` beyond the host's rows so it reads last. Safe verbatim because the engine handoff is
   label-keyed (carriers.to_engine_handoff chose that key for this exact reason).

VERIFICATION.
* NEW TEST tests/test_borrowed_anchor.py - the case the corpus withholds: a science·secondary-
  shaped library whose borrowed unit CARRIES two questions and whose lender numbers them 6,
  where the host's section 6 is a different section on a SERVED sitting. It is discriminating:
  against a clean HEAD it fails at the missing handoff row; with serve fixed but the old port it
  fails with the borrowed questions filed under '8.6 Mass Number' AND the host's own mass-number
  question dragged onto sitting 8 (handoff_period_index is a dict - a number-keyed join clobbers
  in BOTH directions, which is the sharpest argument for removing the mediator rather than
  repairing it).
* NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE ON THE REAL CORPUS: every science·ix ch 8 plan and canonical re-rendered
  through the port before and after - anchors and group labels byte-identical (diff empty).
* Suite: 20/24 pass, the same 4 pre-existing missing-fixture/env failures as before the change.
* Re-served at e16 and re-checked: science·ix ch 8 (6 requests, anchors unchanged, 18/18 exports
  200), SS·IX ch 3 (X=11, 9, 8, 6) and SS·VIII ch 3 (X=15, 12, 11, 9) - all 200, views carry no
  orphaned item, 6/6 SS exports 200. Old e15 files untouched on disk beside the new e16 ones.

defects.title: The engine version stamped INTO every served plan (e15) has drifted from the one that keys its filename (e16) — the second time, at the line that predicts it
defects.evidence: aruvi_core/genon/serve.py:765 writes "engine": "serve v2.2 / e15 (…)" while api/data.py:370 sets GENON_ENGINE_VERSION = "16".
