defects.title: My Lessons drew the lesson TWICE during a re-prepare, and the proposed card's duration line used a different separator from the finished card
defects.evidence: web/app/components/MyLessonPlans.jsx. (1) <ProposedCard> was rendered unconditionally above the plan list with no check for whether the run would land on a card ALREADY in it. The proposed card is deliberately worded to read identically to the finished card ('she should not see the wording change under her'), so the teacher saw the same lesson twice — same title, same length — until the response arrived and the duplicate vanished. Founder reported it from the app during C6. NOT an edge case: any RE-PREPARE hits it, and so does EVERY IDENTITY SERVE (X equal to a canonical's own count returns that canonical's filename and writes no new file, so its card is already on screen) — it would have fired on all four of C6's kumar1 rows. (2) Found while fixing (1), not yet hit: ProposedCard joined rows with ' + ' where api/data.py duration_label() joins with ' · '. Identical on a single row; on kumar3's mixed matrix it would have read '60 min × 4 + 45 min × 6' against '60 min × 4 · 45 min × 6'.
defects.notes: FIX: matrixLabel() extracted and exported in the SERVER's phrasing so the two renderings cannot drift again — and it doubles as the dedupe key, since the served filename derives from chapter + matrix. On a chapter+label match the proposed card is not drawn; the EXISTING card is marked busy instead (aria-busy + .sc-proposed + the same .sc-prep markup), keeping the progress feedback where she is already looking rather than deleting it. Empty-state guard moved to the new flag so a first-ever plan still shows its card. VERIFIED STATICALLY ONLY (CLAUDE.md §11 — the sandbox cannot run next dev): braces/parens balanced, default export intact, ' + ' join gone, <ProposedCard> rendered exactly once; the dedupe logic extracted and unit-tested over 7 cases (empty list · new length on a present chapter · re-prepare · identity · identity mid-list · same length on a DIFFERENT chapter · mixed matrix) — all pass. LIVE RECHECK IS THE FOUNDER'S: reload the app, re-prepare an existing plan, expect ONE card carrying a progress bar. Founder ruling 2026-08-07: fix now rather than after C6 — display-only, does not touch the serve path under test. testing.md C12 gains the mixed-matrix label check.

defects.title: The borrowed synthesis dragged the LENDER's whole final-stage assessment into the variant, and grew a phantom extra stage holding one sitting
defects.evidence: Founder, from the app during C6. Measured on X=9 (p08 + the top's synthesis): the served plan carried 18 items where p08 authored 14, and its coverage_handoff listed SIX stages — a stage 6 whose only sitting was the borrowed synthesis. The 4 extra items were the TOP's stage-6 set, testing 'explain cyclone formation as a self-reinforcing pressure system and evaluate preparedness' — a stage whose earlier units (the top's 10 and 11) the variant's class was never taught. Same on X=11.
defects.notes:
ROOT CAUSE, and it reverses a ruling made earlier the same day. C9.2's standing rule — 'a borrowed unit brings its own items' — presupposes UNIT-level anchoring, which is true of the ten section-axis stages. Under science·middle's STAGE-level anchoring a unit has NO items of its own: it inherits its whole stage's set. So the generic lender-import paths in serve_plan (items, then the coverage_handoff row) did exactly what they were written to do and produced something incoherent. The 2026-08-07 ruling recorded at P2 ('the synthesis carries items and travels with them') stands for the section-axis stages and is WRONG here; the distinction was not visible until a stage-anchored library was served.

FIX (founder's design): the borrowed synthesis is imported as the LAST UNIT OF THE HOST'S LAST STAGE with NO questions linked to it. The variant has already met its own per-stage minimums (assessment v1.5) so it needs no more items, and the lender's stage keeps its questions where they belong — in the top. Implementation: select_whole_plan marks the fill `silent` (suppresses BOTH lender imports) and `adopt_group` (the unit takes the host's grouping-field values). Which fields those are is asked of the plugin — carriers.group_fields / Subject.genon_group_fields — so the engine still never learns a subject's name; science·middle declares ('progression_stage','stage_label'), everyone else the empty tuple. The unit's own content (title, bands, notes, materials) is untouched.

VERIFIED across the full band [5,14]: every served plan's item count now equals its BASE canonical's exactly, no served plan carries a stage its base plan lacked, the synthesis sitting joins the host's last stage, and NO item anchors to it. assessment_items_unserved is 0 throughout. The three authored unit-granularity libraries serve with identical modes — SS·IX, SS·VIII and science·IX untouched. New regression test test_borrowed_synthesis_brings_nothing_but_itself; the older test that asserted the reversed ruling was updated and now cites this defect. Suite 20 passed / 5 baseline failures.

SECOND OBSERVATION, folded in: the phantom stage also made the plan READ wrong — a sixth stage for what is just the closing sitting of the fifth. Fixed by the same adoption.

defects.title: A newly prepared plan never entered My Lessons until the teacher changed subject or class — and the ARV-D-066 fix had moved the progress bar below the fold
defects.evidence:
Founder, from the app during C6: 'when a new LP variant is generated, it does not appear at all with progress bar. only when i refresh by changing subject or class, it comes back.' TWO causes, one pre-existing and one introduced hours earlier.

(1) NO REFETCH — pre-existing, and the reason the finished plan never appeared. The plans effect in MyLessonPlans.jsx keys on [key, sSlug, gSlug]; preparing a lesson changes NONE of them, so the list was never re-read. Only a subject/class switch changed `key` and pulled the new plan in. Invisible until now because a RE-prepare lands on a card already in the list — the gap only shows on a genuinely NEW plan, which is every new variant of a chapter she already has, i.e. most of C6.

(2) THE PROGRESS BAR WENT BELOW THE FOLD — introduced by the ARV-D-066 fix the same day. That fix stopped drawing a duplicate proposed card and marked the EXISTING card busy instead. Correct, but the proposed card had always been drawn FIRST, where she is looking; the real card sits wherever chapter order puts it, and with seven cards for ch 6 that is often off-screen. Suppressing a duplicate is right; silently moving the only progress indicator out of view is not, and it read as 'no progress bar at all'.
defects.notes:
FIX (1): `preparing` going non-null -> null IS the completion signal (page.jsx clears it in both onPrepared and onPrepareError). A ref-guarded edge detector bumps `plansNonce`, which joins the fetch effect's deps. Declared ABOVE that effect on purpose — the dep array is evaluated during render, so a later `const` sits in the temporal dead zone and throws; I hit exactly that and moved it.

FIX (2): the busy card is HOISTED to the head of the list while it runs, so the indicator is back where the proposed card would have been. Same rule the list already follows ('the plan she just acted on comes first'), so it needed no new concept.

VERIFIED: the ordering logic was extracted and exercised over five cases — new variant (proposed card shown, no reorder), re-prepare/identity mid-list (hoisted to head, busy), identity on the LAST card (the below-the-fold case, hoisted), identity already first (no needless reorder), and not-preparing (list intact). Static checks: braces/parens balanced, single declaration, declared-before-use confirmed by index, map walks `ordered`. STATIC ONLY per CLAUDE.md §11.

LIVE RECHECK IS THE FOUNDER'S, and it is now two things: prepare a NEW length -> a proposed card appears immediately AND the finished plan lands in the list without touching the wheels; re-prepare an EXISTING length -> ONE card, hoisted to the top, carrying the progress bar.

STANDING LESSON: ARV-D-066 was verified against its own symptom (no duplicate) and not against what the surface was FOR (she can see progress). A fix that satisfies the defect and defeats the feature is not a fix — the check is 'what was this element doing that I have now stopped it doing?'

defects.evidence: See docs/testing_artefacts/c3_mathematics_ix_ch04.md — the rule table quotes the evidence for every row and section C lists the defects.

ACCEPTED by founder 2026-08-09, not remedied. Guides that refer to an option
by its letter ('confirm option A') in 4 places across the two files; STEP 6's label-reference
guard reads options[] only, not the guide, and caught 1 of 4.

Founder reasoning, recorded because it sets a precedent: the post-hoc re-ordering in STEP 6 is
itself what makes a letter reference fragile, and the answer is not to write yet another
constitutional rule telling the model not to mention options - the rule surface is already the
thing under strain, and naming option positions at all keeps position salient to a model that
should never reason about it (the same argument that struck the arrangement sentence at
assessment v1.7). The occurrence is rare and a teacher reading a guide that says 'option A'
beside an item whose correct answer is marked C will resolve it correctly. Accepted as a known,
bounded cosmetic defect.

NOT accepted, and to be kept separate: std item 7's guide names the WRONG option as correct on
the merits ('confirm option A' where C is correct on re-derivation). That is a content error
wearing a letter reference, not an instance of this defect. It rides with the item-level
content debt and is unaffected by this ruling.

defects.title: science IX ch 8 p07 item 4(b): the model's self-correction shipped inside the STUDENT-FACING stem, and the key resolved the part to the atom it was given

violation, it is a wrecked sentence, and a reader checking rules does not see it. A regex over
the text fields catches it in milliseconds at zero cost and nothing runs one (see the C5

defects.title: served plans rendered an EMPTY pedagogical approach line on 8 of 11 stages — the canonicals were correct throughout, only the artefact the teacher receives was wrong
defects.evidence:
FOUND 2026-08-09 at S4's C6, on kumar2's and kumar3's served plans. Every ch 4
canonical carries pedagogical_method on all 15/12/9 units and C4's item 7 measured 0 empty
through the real port. Every SERVED plan measured 100% empty.

MECHANISM, two links in one chain:
 . compile.py's _MODELLED listed all five approach key names, which is what EXCLUDES a key
   from unit["extra"]. So serve._period_from_unit spliced none of them back.
 . the only approach key the served period then carried was the NORMALIZED
   pedagogical_approaches, computed by carriers.unit_approaches - which read three of the
   five names and returned [] for maths, english and TWAU. Its docstring claimed
   pedagogical_approach covered "Science, Maths"; maths emits pedagogical_method.
Each subject port reads the key ITS OWN constitution emits, so only social_sciences - whose
authored key happens to share the normalized name - rendered anything.

MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX (served, through each subject's real port):
  mathematics/ix ch4  X=13  EMPTY 13/13      science/ix   ch8 X=13  EMPTY 12/12
  mathematics/ix ch4  X=8   EMPTY  8/8       science/viii ch6 X=11  EMPTY 11/11
  social_sciences/ix  ch3   X=11  EMPTY 0/11 (unaffected)
Scope by key: maths (pedagogical_method) x2 stages · science (pedagogical_approach) x2 ·
english (pedagogical_methods) x3 · TWAU (dominant_mode) x1 = EIGHT stages. SS x2 unaffected;
maths-preparatory has no source field and is legitimately empty (MEMORY item 7).

SEVERITY: this is CLAUDE.md 3(b)'s single canonical "how do I run this?" line, and it was
missing from every served plan on a CERTIFIED stage - science-middle carries a signed human
GATE. Filed against science/middle and science/secondary as well as this stage.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: C1-C5 read canonicals and reports. No step before C6 reads a served
plan, and C6 is described in the template as the first step that "tests the path a teacher
actually takes". It did exactly that on its first outing.

FIX (2026-08-09): the approach keys are no longer modelled, so each subject's own key rides
in extra verbatim and is spliced back - no port change and no subject branching, which is
what extra exists for. carriers.unit_approaches now reads all five names (english's dict
shape included) and its docstring is corrected. VERIFIED: 0 empty on all six served plans
across three subjects; tests/test_genon_approach_survives_serve.py added, locking BOTH the
unit-level key reading AND the end-to-end compile->serve->port property - the second is the
one that would have caught this, since the ports never read the normalized key.

ENGINE 17 -> 18 (served bytes change for maths, science, english, TWAU). Per testing.md 9 an
engine change is corpus-wide and cheap: --certify-only re-run on all five chapters with a
library, reports diffed line by line against the previous run - ZERO diff lines on every one,
all five still DETERMINISTIC CHECKS ALL PASS, serve sweeps identical. So no stage loses
certification. All five genon suites green. Every _e17_ plan file is stale by construction
and stays on disk as C10.3 evidence.
defects.resolution: Fixed in aruvi_core/genon/compile.py (_MODELLED) + carriers.py (unit_approaches); GENON_ENGINE_VERSION 17 -> 18; regression test tests/test_genon_approach_survives_serve.py.

defects.title: a failed prepare tells the teacher NOTHING on the ordinary path — the proposed card flashes and vanishes, and the message is set on a screen she is no longer looking at
defects.evidence:
FOUND 2026-08-10, on the phone, while setting up the C13 mobile demo. The founder
broke ch 4's canonical, asked for 14 periods, and reported: 'something seemed to flash for a
micro sec but nothing readable .. it goes back to my lessons'. That is exactly what the code does.

THE CHAIN, traced end to end:
 1. onPreparing(descriptor) -> page.jsx:279-284 setEditFlow('lessonplans') + setTab('myplans'),
    which UNMOUNTS PrepareLesson and lands her in My Lessons with the proposed card drawn.
 2. the POST fails.
 3. onPrepareError() -> page.jsx:288 is exactly `() => setPreparingCard(null)`. The card is
    pulled. THAT IS THE FLASH.
 4. setError('Couldn't build the lesson plan right now. Try again in a moment.') sets state on
    PrepareLesson, WHICH IS UNMOUNTED. The string is never rendered.
 5. MyLessonPlans has no error surface at all — no error rendering anywhere in the component.
Net: tap -> land in My Lessons -> a card appears and disappears -> nothing. No lesson, no
explanation. She would reasonably conclude she mis-tapped.

THE CODE ANTICIPATED THIS AND STOPPED HALF WAY. The comment on the catch reads: 'She may already
be in My Lessons watching the proposed card — the failure has to reach HER, not this screen, so
it goes back up the same way it went down.' The intent is right; onPrepareError only pulls the
card and never delivers the message.

PATH-DEPENDENT, and the common path is the broken one: on the SECTION-ATTACH path onPreparing
returns false (page.jsx:278, `if (!desc || prepareReturn) return false`), so she stays on the
Prepare screen and does see the generic line. It is the ordinary My Classes / My Lessons route
that is silent.

WHY NO C-STEP CAUGHT IT: C13 tests the API's response bodies and they are correct and readable
(6/6). Nothing in the campaign reads the SCREEN on a failure path. This is the C6/C13 seam —
C6 tests the happy path a teacher takes, C13 tests the API's unhappy path, and neither tests the
teacher's unhappy path.

REMEDY (not applied — founder to rule on the wording): onPrepareError already RECEIVES the
descriptor and throws it away. Keep a failed marker in the shell and render it in My Lessons as a
line she can read — ideally on the card that was about to become her lesson, since that is where
her attention already is.
defects.resolution:
CLOSED 2026-08-10, verified on the phone by the founder. A failed prepare no longer
vanishes: the proposed card STAYS, its bar stops, the dashed 'not yet' border goes solid, and
the last line becomes the reason with a Dismiss she controls. onPrepareError now carries the
message with the descriptor instead of discarding it — which is what the original comment
('the failure has to reach HER, not this screen') asked for and never did.
Card height was wrong on the first pass and is fixed: the failed line is ONE ROW at every
width, because .sc-prep's <=420px column stacking exists to protect the progress BAR and there
is no bar here. The note is clamped to two lines so a long 4xx sentence cannot grow the card
either, with the full text in `title`.
Also fixed in the same pass, found because the founder pressed Prepare on a chapter with no
canonical and got NOTHING: the chapter step had no {error} block at all — the only one sits
inside the 'preview' step, which is why the retired stand-in path used to navigate there just
to be seen. The message now renders beside the button she pressed, with the picker still in
front of her, and clears when she moves the chapter wheel so it cannot accuse the wrong
chapter.

defects.title: postJSON discards the server's `detail`, so every failure collapses to one generic line — and that line tells her to retry things that can never succeed
defects.evidence:
web/app/lib/format.js:96 — `if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${r.status}`)`. The
response BODY is never read, so the server's teacher-worded detail is thrown away at the
transport layer, before any component sees it. Only Allocate.jsx reads body.detail, and it uses
its own fetch rather than postJSON.

CONSEQUENCE: the four messages C13 certified never reach her. 'No underlying chapter yet.',
'Period count implausibly large.', and the 500 that names the broken item all render as the same
sentence: 'Couldn't build the lesson plan right now. Try again in a moment.'

AND THAT SENTENCE IS WRONG IN A SPECIFIC WAY: 'Try again in a moment' is true for a transient
failure and FALSE for both cases she can actually reach — an unauthored chapter and an
impossible period count are permanent until someone acts. We send her to retry a thing that
cannot work.

SCOPE NOTE: the 404 is unreachable from the UI anyway. genonAvailable is computed from
/genon/{s}/{g}/chapters (chapters WITH a library) and the picker itself is built from the
SYLLABUS (/subjects/{s}/{g}/chapters, i.e. the mappings folder), so the app never asks the genon
path for a chapter we have not authored. The reachable cases are the 400 (period count) and the
500 (corrupt canonical).

REMEDY (not applied): have postJSON read `detail` off the body and attach it to the thrown Error;
show it when present, keep the generic line as the fallback. Safe by construction — the API
strings are already teacher-worded, which is precisely what C13 check 1 polices ('canonical' is
our word, not hers). Pairs with ARV-D-087: 087 is why she sees nothing, 088 is what she would
see once there is somewhere to say it.
defects.resolution:
CLOSED 2026-08-10. postJSON now reads the body and attaches `detail` to the thrown
error, so a 4xx reaches her in the API's own words. Scoped to 4xx DELIBERATELY: those strings
are already written for her (C13 check 1 polices exactly that — 'canonical' is our word, not
hers), while a 5xx detail is engine talk ('Canonical cannot be compiled: assessment item #4
NUM / C-3.1 …') and must never be shown. A 5xx therefore keeps the generic sentence.
Verified live: 31 periods on ch 4 now reads 'More than 30 periods is too many for one chapter.'
on the failed card, where it previously read 'try again in a moment' — advice that could never
have worked.

defects.title: p10's closing unit is a whole-chapter consolidation wearing a 7.4/7.5 label, after both runs closed — LP v3.6 Rule 1, and it cannot be repaired by reordering
defects.evidence:
ch_07_canonical_p10.json U10 'Bringing It Together: Altitudes, Types, and Extended Problems'. Anchors section 7.4 AND section 7.5 (adjacent, so the two-section anchor is itself legal under Rule 1) but sits AFTER both runs closed - 7.4 at U7, 7.5 at U8-U9 - which v3.6's contiguity sentence forbids. Because an item anchors at its section's LAST unit, U10 becomes the last unit of both and captures 4 of the 10 items (two 7.5 recall, two 7.4 apply) while U7, U8 and U9 - which actually taught those sections - carry none.

THREE THINGS MAKE IT MORE THAN A CONTIGUITY SLIP:
(a) THE ANCHOR DOES NOT MATCH THE CONTENT. Both its in-class items are E-9 and E-11, SECTION 7.2, and its first two bands are 7.2 material (circle-intersection, equilateral existence). Its own teacher note says it draws on 7.2, 7.3 and 7.4. This is the S4 section 3.3 consolidation-label pattern, worse here because the ITEMS come from a different section than the anchor.
(b) IT IS A SYNTHESIS UNIT IN ALL BUT THE FLAG. Architecture v2.0 reserves the whole-chapter consolidation to the STANDARD canonical and the compact brief forbids it in terms; this unit obeys the letter (no 'synthesis': true, so the reserved-token gate passes) and breaks the intent.
(c) IT CANNOT BE REPAIRED BY REORDERING, unlike the top's U11. Its band 3 uses 7.5's classification vocabulary (scalene, obtuse, classify), so it depends on U8/U9 and has no earlier home. A re-author (~Rs 35) is the only fix.
defects.decision:
ACCEPTED by founder 2026-08-10, C1 closed. The certifier reports ALL PASS - nothing in the current gate set tests contiguity, which is precisely the gap. p07 is clean (contiguous, 5/5 sections, 7 items across 5 units) and the top was repaired by declared unit-order permutation. Carried to C5/C8 and the human gate.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-10 at C9 (founder's question): the constitution's own SURPLUS bullet. Rule 2 told the model that where the budget exceeds what the sections need, 'the surplus is spent by DEEPENING sections' — which frames spare units as things to PLACE, separate from teaching, and a unit with no run to belong to lands at the end. U10 is that frame made concrete. Only maths MIDDLE carried such a provision (grep: middle 1, preparatory 0, secondary 0); maths IX's Rule 7 has a bare permission and produces zero revisits. The bullet is DELETED at LP v3.8 — its permission was already in the bullet above and its prohibition is already Rule 1. Relaxation-only, no re-author.
defects.carried: THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING, NOT THE INSTANCE. Three occurrences in ONE chapter: the top's three revisits under v3.5, the top's U11 after v3.6 landed, and now p10's U10. Prose has failed to suppress it three times, including twice against text that forbids it in terms. Same shape as the option-order lesson (prose could not carry a sort, so it became STEP 6) and the register (banned in terms by v1.10, breached nine times, so it became a machine gate). OWED AND FREE: a certifier check that no section appears in two non-contiguous runs, gated by a plugin-declared fact (genon_sections_are_contiguous) so it never touches SS or TWAU - SS VIII ch 3 revisits twice and SS IX ch 3 once under constitutions that never forbade it, and gating them would re-open certified stages over a rule they were never held to.

defects.title: extract_determinate.py read only the SECONDARY shape, so C3's maths sub-check returned ZERO items on maths·middle — a silent pass on an unexamined library
defects.evidence:
genon/extract_determinate.py. (a) iter_items() knew two containers — {…,'questions':[]} and a FLAT assessment_items list — but not the GROUP-NESTED one maths middle and preparatory use ([{section_code, items:[…]}]). It yielded GROUP dicts, which carry no answer and no stem, so nothing matched. (b) The field read was `item['expected_answer']` / `item['method_one_line']` / `item['question_text']` — the secondary hybrid's TOP-LEVEL shape. The library actually carries 29. Third recurrence of the container-shape class after the science `questions` wrapper (S3) and carriers.raw_item_list (S7·P5.5); first one where the failure was SILENT rather than a crash.
defects.decision: FIXED 2026-08-10 before C3 ran. iter_items detects the group container by SHAPE (an element that is a dict carrying an `items` list), never by subject; the field read falls back through teacher_guide. Verified both ways: maths·VII 0 → 29 items, maths·IX unchanged at 19 items / 25 checks.

defects.title: STEP 6 relabelled MCQ options without remapping teacher_guide.what_each_option_reveals — the correct answer carried a distractor's diagnostic
defects.evidence:
genon/normalize_options.py remapped the label-keyed guide only at guide[QUESTION_TYPE].what_each_option_reveals — the constitution-family path used by science, social_sciences, TWAU and maths SECONDARY. Mathematics MIDDLE and PREPARATORY keep it at teacher_guide.what_each_option_reveals, so their diagnostics never moved when the options were sorted and relabelled.

ch 7 top item 2 (hypotenuse): is_correct=B, and B's diagnostic read 'Same misconception as A — the student picks the other adjacent side', while the correct-answer text sat on C. p10 item 2 was shifted the same way. A missing diagnostic is a gap; this is a CONFIDENT WRONG ONE printed against the answer the class got right — hence S1.

CERTIFIED STAGES ARE NOT AFFECTED by this half: science and maths secondary both keep reveals under guide[MCQ] and were remapped correctly (verified by reading the installed files).

Fourth recurrence of the container-shape class: science's `questions` wrapper (S3), carriers.raw_item_list (S7 P5.5), extract_determinate.py (S7 C3, ARV-D-090), this.
defects.decision: FIXED AT SOURCE + REPAIRED IN PLACE, 2026-08-10. (a) normalize_options.py now remaps BOTH paths, found by shape, never by subject; negative-tested on a synthetic 4-option permutation and the constitution-family path proven unchanged. (b) Re-running STEP 6 could NOT undo the damage — the options are already sorted so its remap is the identity, and the inverting permutation is returned by normalize_item but deliberately never written to the artefact (founder 2026-08-04). So genon/repair_option_reveals.py applies DECLARED (old->new) label pairs, read off each diagnostic against the option it names, applied only if the mapping is a bijection and the resulting key set equals the non-correct labels. Recorded in genon_canonical.repairs[]. (c) Assessment v3.4/v1.2 make the key set machine-checkable, so this cannot recur silently.

defects.title: Two inclusivity notes in the CERTIFIED maths IX ch 4 library name an option by a letter that STEP 6 has since moved
defects.evidence:
Corpus sweep 2026-08-10 (S7 C3): exactly 7 answer/guide fields anywhere in the installed corpus name an option by letter in prose. THREE are stale — one in maths VII (repaired under ARV-D-092) and TWO in maths IX ch 4, which is CERTIFIED:
  ch_04_canonical.json item 2 (correct B): 'verify the identity by substituting small integers for x and y IN OPTION A' — option A is 3x^2-24xy+4y^2, a distractor. You do not verify an identity against a wrong form; written when the answer was A.
  ch_04_canonical.json item 7 (correct C): 'expand the full sum symbolically and CONFIRM OPTION A' — option A is a distractor.

The other four are CORRECT AS WRITTEN and are the reason this cannot be automated: ch_04_p12 says 'verify option A by expanding (2x-3)^2' and option A IS 4x^2-9=(2x-3)^2 — the task is to disprove it; science VIII p07 says 'rewrite option D so it is correct' and D IS the wrong hardness claim.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is not the mapping bug: an answer key exists in TWO representations. STRUCTURAL (is_correct, label-keyed dicts) travels with a sort. PROSE (a letter inside a sentence) cannot be rewritten by any sort without rewriting meaning. A9 at v1.7 already established the principle — an option may not refer to another option BY LABEL, 'because options are ordered downstream and a label reference would be falsified' — but A9 was scoped to options and never to the answer or guide fields.
defects.decision: OPEN — founder's call, and it is a defect against a CERTIFIED stage, so it is raised here rather than absorbed by S7. Three options, increasing scope: (1) repair the two notes in place (they name a distractor that is no longer at that letter); (2) add a certifier check listing every label-reference in a prose field and failing when the named label is not is_correct AND the prose does not quote that option's content — the four legitimate cases pass that test, the three stale ones do not; (3) widen A9 across all eleven constitutions from 'no option may name another option's label' to 'no field may name an option's label — name its content instead', which prevents rather than detects.

defects.title: LP Rule 1 and the schema cap a unit at 1–2 adjacent sections, but v2.0 MANDATES a synthesis unit spanning all of them — a rule/brief collision, not a generation defect
defects.evidence: ch_07_canonical unit 12 carries FIVE textbook_segments (section 7.1…7.5) with synthesis: true, against Rule 1's 'one or at most two adjacent sections' and the schema's '// 1-2 entries'. The model did exactly what the platform brief told it to. Contiguity itself is clean after the unit-order repair: runs 7.1(1)·7.2(2,3,4)·7.3(5-8)·7.4(9)·7.5(10,11)·synthesis(12), zero revisits; p07 contiguous as authored.
defects.decision: CLOSED 2026-08-10 by LP v3.7. Founder's correction: this is not a synthesis carve-out, it is Rule 1 and Rule 2 capping the same many-to-many relation from opposite directions, and v3.6 widened only Rule 2 (one SECTION over many PERIODS). Rule 1 governs one PERIOD over many SECTIONS and still named a number. It now reads 'A period anchors to as many ADJACENT sections as its content warrants' — Rule 2's own wording from the other side — and the schema's '1-2 entries' cap goes with it. The synthesis unit is NOT named: the mandate is V-series and testing.md section 3 keeps it out of constitutions; 'as its content warrants' covers it. RELAXATION-ONLY, so no re-author: the installed library becomes compliant rather than breaching.

defects.title: The LP header block (core_cg, core_competencies, adjunct_competencies, periods_allocated, dissolution_test) is absent from EVERY authored canonical, across certified stages too
defects.evidence: LP Rule 7 mandates a chapter header table. Absent from ch_07_canonical and ch_07_canonical_p07 — and not a save-path artefact: the raw model output ch_07_20260810_184152_raw.txt lacks them, and so do CERTIFIED social_sciences/ix/ch_03 (S1) and mathematics/ix/ch_04 (S4). The assessment envelope likewise omits its mandated 'stage' key everywhere.
defects.decision:
WON'T FIX — founder, 2026-08-10. The LP header block is absent from SECONDARY too, so it is not a middle-stage defect and not a regression; it is a rule no stage has ever satisfied.

AND MIDDLE CANNOT SATISFY IT EVEN IF ASKED. The competency data reaches an assessment through the COVERAGE HANDOFF, and the two stages' handoffs differ in kind. Verified 2026-08-10: maths IX's handoff entries carry c_code and co_central (keys: c_code, co_central, implied_lo, period_duration_minutes, period_numbers, section_context, section_number, section_ref, section_title, total_sections) and its items carry `competency`. Maths VII's goal entries carry only anchor_book_ref, anchor_description, anchor_id, goal, section_ref, section_title — no competency channel exists at all, and its items carry none. Middle's LP Rule 8 is the reason: 'Competencies do not drive LP … never in periods, time bands, or teacher_notes.'

So the header block is a secondary-shaped requirement sitting in a middle-stage file. Striking it from Rule 7 is the honest fix, but it is a corpus-wide question and is deferred, not done.

defects.title: register_scan reports 0 ban hits on a file carrying a real ban-2 breach — U11 claims intuition 'built throughout the chapter'

defects.title: the synthesis flag did not survive the serve, so every SERVED closing unit was labelled 'Equilateral Triangles (Revisit)'

SELF-INFLICTED AND WORTH RECORDING AS SUCH: this exact residue was DISCLOSED the same day as harmless — 'the synthesis boolean does not survive serving… nothing downstream reads it'. It stopped being true within hours, because is_synthesis had just become what the group label reads. defects.title: at X=5 a unit is neither served nor declared dropped — it simply vanishes

But the teacher is handed 7.5's material for self-study with a note, and loses half of 7.3's teaching with no note and no material. The contract is FIRST-EXPOSURE coverage: a section is 'covered' once a unit first deals it, so a second unit on an already-dealt section is surplus, not a drop, and does not enter dropped_units. Recorded as the contract rather than a defect. The residue a future reader should still know: below the floor a teacher is handed the material for a section that was never reached, and silently loses a second unit on a section that was — so 'covered' in the note means introduced, not taught in full.

defects.title: every synthesis borrow repeats the SAME textbook exercise the sitting before it just did — the composition creates it, no canonical is wrong

(b) CERTIFIER (free, deterministic) — assert the synthesis unit's book_refs are disjoint from every other unit's, which catches it at C1 rather than at C8 by eye. Note the tie-break is NOT the culprit here: the lender is correct in every case (the standard owns the synthesis), so hardening lender selection would fix nothing.
defects.notes:
ACCEPTED, NOT A DEFECT (founder, 2026-08-11): 'but then p12 (canonical) also shows it in two places. naturally, synthesis will have to cite content that had occurred before. no problems.' THE REFRAME, which is the durable part: the 12-unit canonical ALREADY uses Figure it Out Q4 p.170 twice, at u10 and u12. A synthesis unit's function is to draw earlier work together, and doing that means citing work already done - a closing unit that referenced nothing prior would not be a synthesis. So re-use of an earlier exercise in the closer is the DESIGN, present in the authored plan itself, not something the serve manufactures. What the serve changes is only the SPACING: the canonical has one unit between the two uses, the X=11 and X=9 serves have none, because the borrow displaces the unit that sat between. defects.title: a DROPPED unit's items keep the lender's unit number, so they anchor outside the served plan and are not flagged unscheduled
defects.evidence:
C9 checks 1, 3(c) and 4, on the below-floor serves. X=5 (5 sittings) carries an item anchored to unit 6; X=6 (6 sittings) to unit 7. C9 3(c) is explicit: a dropped unit's items must be anchored 'to the dropped unit's sitting number in THIS plan, never the lender's own numbering'. And neither is flagged `unscheduled: true` — Q-A-1 on both — which C9 3(d) makes load-bearing: EXPORTS omit exactly the flagged items. Unflagged means the export prints questions about a unit the class never had. That is ARV-D-037's failure, which e13 was written to end.

Independent of the p10 re-author: these rows use p07 and are unchanged by it.
defects.decision: NOT A DEFECT — founder, 2026-08-10, and MY CHECK WAS WRONG, not the engine. I asserted that every anchor falls within 1..len(served sittings). A dropped unit is RENUMBERED as the plan's continuation (p07's u7 becomes 6 at X=5), so an item pointing at 6 points exactly at the unit the teacher is holding — which is what C9 3(c) asks for ('the dropped unit's sitting number in THIS plan'), not the lender's numbering leaking through. On the flag, the founder's reading governs: 'if she chooses to accommodate the dropped unit and teach, she can as well use the assessment.' The `unscheduled` flag's only consumer is the export, which omits flagged items — so flagging would strip exactly the question she needs. The check is corrected on both counts.

defects.title: C9 check 2 is UNSATISFIABLE on this stage — the synthesis unit can hold no assessment item, so a Case-1 borrow brings none
defects.evidence:
Founder, reading the served plans: 'synthesis of tops has no assessment item'. Verified on the authored top: 12 units, 12 handoff entries, 12 items, and U12 (the synthesis) holds ZERO. Nothing is lost in the borrow — there was never anything to lend.

CAUSE, and it is partly the platform's own fix. On maths·middle an item reaches a unit only by matching its section_ref to a period's textbook_segments. The synthesis unit names EVERY section, so with it in the index it became the last unit of all five and swallowed all twelve items (ARV-D-092's symptom: units 1-11 showing no assessment at all). carriers.items_by_period_field therefore EXCLUDES it — correctly — and the consequence is that it can hold no item, ever, on this stage. The handoff confirms there is no lost data: all 12 entries name a real section (7.5, 7.5, 7.2, 7.3, 7.3, 7.1, 7.2, 7.2, 7.3, 7.3, 7.4, 7.5) and NONE names the synthesis.

This is S4 §3.2's prediction — 'C9.2 is unsatisfiable on precisely the Case-1 synthesis borrow C8 exists to inspect' — confirmed on a MEDIATED-anchor stage, where it was raised for DERIVED-anchor stages only. The sharpest face of it is X=9: nine sittings, all five sections taught, the note reads 'Every section is covered; the closing sitting draws the chapter together' — and that sitting has nothing to assess while 7.5 has nothing either.
defects.decision:
ACCEPTED AS DESIGN — founder, 2026-08-10, after establishing the scope precisely. The exclusion is NARROW: `is_synthesis` is true only for a unit carrying `"synthesis": true` or the reserved token, so it catches the TOP's closing synthesis and nothing else. A COMPACT's composite unit is not flagged synthesis and takes items normally — the old p10's composite held 5 of 11, which is the empirical proof. So the only unit in the system that cannot hold an item is the one unit that tests nothing of its own, and that is coherent.

Founder's framing, worth keeping: the p10 problem was never that composites exist — it was the BRIEF pushing consolidation to the end 'not naturally but through the brief prompt'. With that pressure removed p10 came out contiguous. Where a natural flow does consolidate a few sections in a compact, that unit may carry items, and those items may be lost to variants served from a shorter prefix — the risk accepted at ARV-D-106.

Implemented at two sites, both via carriers.is_synthesis: genon/carriers.py::items_by_period_field (the index that stamps unit_ref) and subjects/mathematics/subject.py::_middle_assess (the display join). Two, so a canonical read from disk and the same plan served anchor identically.

defects.title: a section whose run is cut mid-way loses its assessment silently — taught, but no item and no note
defects.evidence:
X=8 and X=9 teach all five sections; 7.5 is assessed in neither. Its three items anchor at p10's U10, the last unit of 7.5's run, and both serves stop at U8. `assessment_items_unserved` reads 3 — provenance, not teacher-facing — and the only note X=9 shows is the reassuring one.

MEASURABLY BETTER THAN BEFORE, and worth recording as the brief fix's dividend: under the old composite p10 BOTH 7.4 and 7.5 were unassessed at X=8 and only 6 of 10 items survived. The contiguous p10 gives 7.4 its own closing unit, so it is now assessed and 7 items survive. The residue is structural, not a defect in the new plan: anchoring at a section's LAST unit means whichever section the prefix cut falls inside loses its assessment.
defects.decision:
ACCEPTED RISK — founder, 2026-08-10: 'if we are going to link items to last of the sittings which is our approach, we must live with the reality that borrowed units may lose assessment items. it is fine.'

THE GENERAL FORM, established at C9 and worth carrying: §0.4 borrows the unit that FIRST deals the next-due section, while items anchor at that section's LAST unit. So a borrowed unit carries items ONLY when its section happens to be a single-unit run. At X=8 the borrow takes p10's u8 (7.5's first unit) while 7.5's items sit on u10. This is not a ch-7 quirk and not a defect in any plan — it is the arithmetic of the anchoring rule meeting the borrow rule, and it follows the 2026-08-05 ruling that an item tests its section's whole goal and so becomes available only when the section completes.

defects.title: C10 checks 2 and 3 cannot both be evidenced: the purge check 2 requires deletes the earlier-engine files check 3 asks to see
defects.evidence:
C10.3 asks that 'every earlier-engine file for this chapter is still on disk untouched beside the current ones'. C10.2(b) requires that after any in-place repair the chapter's derived plans are GONE, via genon/purge_derived.py, which runs from repair_register, repair_anchors and normalize_options.

Observed at S7: the seven _e18_ served plans were deliberately preserved as C10.3 evidence when the engine moved 18 -> 19. The p10 re-author then ran normalize_options, which called purge_derived, and all seven were removed. Zero _e18_ files remain. Both checks did exactly what they say.

The two are not reconcilable as written: a purge scoped to 'derived plans for that chapter' cannot spare files from a superseded engine version, because the pattern it matches (ch_NN_<matrix>_e<NN>_c<version>.json) covers every engine.
defects.decision: OPEN — a TEMPLATE question, not a product defect. Nothing was ever rewritten in place, which is what check 3 exists to protect: the engine version is IN the filename, so an overwrite is impossible by construction and provable from the naming scheme alone. Two ways to settle it: (a) restate check 3's evidence as 'no served file is ever rewritten in place — proved by the engine token in the name', which costs nothing and is what the check actually means; or (b) scope purge_derived to spare files whose engine token is not current, which keeps the artefacts but leaves stale plans nothing will ever serve. (a) is cheaper and truer. Raised against cross because it is testing.md's wording, not S7's.

defects.title: Rule 10's 10-word inline-quotation cap is breached by 85% of band quotations (median 18.5, max 39)
defects.evidence:
mathematics-middle LP Rule 10 mandates: book_ref ("description up to 10 words.... ") — the inline quotation is the stage's textbook-reference convention, unlike maths-secondary which mandates a bare locator. Measured over the three installed canonicals of maths/vii ch 7: 88 band quotations, 75 of them (85%) over the 10-word cap, median 18.5 words, maximum 39 ('Altitudes Using Paper Folding: cut out a paper triangle, fix one side as the base, and fold so the crease is the altitude from the top vertex to the base. Justify why the...', p10 u7 band2). Homework descriptions run to 38 words on the same pattern.

WHY IT IS RAISED AT C14 RATHER THAN LEFT TO C3. The cap IS the short-quotation guarantee for this stage. C14's own verdict is PASS — the longest run shared with the textbook is 18 words, 16 for prose, 1.15% of the chapter — but that holds only because ch 7's summary condenses its source. The cap is what makes the guarantee independent of how closely any given summary tracks its book; at an 85% breach rate the guarantee is doing no work, and a chapter whose summary quotes more faithfully would land the same breach on NCERT's own sentences.

Authored under LP v3.6. Rule 10 was untouched by the v3.4-v3.8 amendments (which moved Rules 1, 2, 5 and the surplus bullet), so this is not a stale-rule breach.
defects.decision: OPEN — for the founder. Three questions, in order: (a) is the 10-word cap the right number for a stage whose exercises are measurement sets, where '(a) 3 cm, 75 deg, 7 cm; (b) 6 cm, 25 deg, 3 cm; (c) 3 cm, 120 deg, 8 cm' is 18 tokens and cannot be shortened without destroying the exercise? (b) if the cap stands, it needs a certifier check — nothing measures quotation length today, which is why an 85% breach reached a paid artefact and was found by measurement rather than by the pipeline; (c) if the cap is relaxed for data, it must stay tight for prose, since prose is the whole copyright exposure. Remedy either way is free: a repair pass over the band text, or an amended Rule 10 — never a regeneration.

defects.title: Assessment Rule 6's inclusivity cap (<=25 words) is breached by 76% of the standard's items and 52% of p08's
defects.evidence: Standard: 22 of 29 verified items over the cap, median 30, mean 29.2, max 36, and only 7 at or under 25. p08: 16 of 31, median 26, max 39. THE WRITING IS NOT PADDED - the longest, Q-B-5 (36 words): 'Support: guide the child to check each shape one property at a time (sides? corners? opposite sides equal?); stretch: ask the child to draw a shape that has 4 straight sides but is NOT a rectangle.' That is two distinct, useful teaching moves. Rule 6 demands BOTH a support AND a stretch, fitted to the intent, in one sentence of 25 words; the compliant examples (Q-B-10, 19 words) are good but noticeably thinner. The evidence points at the RULE, the same finding S4 recorded against activity_title/section_context and S7 against the method cap.
defects.notes: ACCEPTED, no change (founder, 2026-08-11). The <=25-word inclusivity cap stays as written and the overruns are not repaired. The field is teacher-facing guidance, not a contract, and a 30-word support-plus-stretch costs nothing downstream. | PRIOR ANALYSIS RETAINED: RECOMMENDED REMEDY: widen the cap to ~40 words (relaxation-only under section 9, so free and no re-author). Do NOT drop the both-support-and-stretch requirement - that is what makes the field useful. Note p08 is materially tighter than the standard (52% vs 76%, median 26 vs 30), so the pressure is not uniform.

defects.notes: ACCEPTED, no change (founder, 2026-08-11). LP Rule 7's header table stays in all eleven constitutions and NO canonical is required to emit it. THE STANDING DISPOSITION, which applies to the batch sweep as well as to this chapter: the platform sources competencies, core_cg and dissolution_test from the MAPPING, so the omission is inert; when batch outputs are reviewed this is to be ignored exactly as it is ignored now. Do NOT re-raise it at S9-S11's C3. | PRIOR ANALYSIS RETAINED: WHY IT COST NOTHING, which is also why it went unnoticed: every consumer reads the competencies from the MAPPING json, not from the plan - export_lesson_pdf.targeted_competencies(mapping, descriptions) and report_competency.build_report both take the mapping. The LP copy would be duplicated data that nothing reads and that could DRIFT from its source. RECOMMENDED REMEDY: strike the emission mandate from Rule 7 in all eleven LP constitutions (relaxation-only - it removes an obligation - hence free and no re-author), replacing it with a line saying the platform supplies these from the mapping and the plan must not restate them. The alternative - making 330 chapters carry it - buys nothing and creates a drift surface. FOUNDER CALL; it touches every stage, including certified ones.

defects.title: Assessment Rule 9's intent->type map has no override sentence, unlike its LP twin, so 8 sensible items read as breaches
defects.evidence: Rule 9 lists 'reason -> SCR' with no alternative, but 8 of 29 standard items and 8 of 31 p08 items take MCQ or NUM on a reason intent (Q-B-1/3/4/6 MCQ; Q-B-7/8/11 NUM). defects.title: The `number_line:` tag is used for a NON-numeric pattern sequence, so it degrades to a table and leaks the internal tag to the teacher
defects.evidence: MEMORY item 14 added `number_line:` to prep + middle Rule 7 precisely so a real number line had somewhere legal to go. Its FIRST live exercise misuses it. Standard Q-C-4 emits 'number_line: line | curve | line | curve | line | curve | ... | ...' — the cells are WORDS, not numbers. Rule 7 requires 'each cell a number (labelled tick) or "..." (blank tick)' and 'endpoints must be numbers'. The engine is correct and defensive: `_nl_block` rejects it (needs >=3 cells, >=2 numeric, every cell numeric-or-placeholder), `_maths_number_line` returns None, and typing falls through to the shared classifier, which returns TABLE. CONSEQUENCE: the renderer boxes a repeating-pattern sequence as a one-row table AND the stimulus `content` still carries the literal prefix, so the internal tag 'number_line:' is printed to the teacher. Item Q-C-4 itself is a fine pattern question ('A line pattern goes: short straight line, curve, short straight line...'); only the stimulus typing is wrong. p08 and p11 emit no visual_stimulus at all, so this is 1 of 1 uses.
defects.notes: FIXED 2026-08-11, four layers, founder-directed ('do all four .. also back fill Q-C-4 to represent it in number line'). (1) `_nl_block` validates structure not cell type, so word labels are legal; (2) a failed tag strips itself and falls to PROSE, so the token can never render; (3) build_library.py DECLARED-TYPE GATE reports any tag that does not resolve — verified to fire on a broken artefact and to pass on the real one; (4) Rule 7 widened to a TICK LINE in prep v1.4 and middle v3.5, relaxation-only, no re-author. THE BACK-FILL NEEDED NO FILE EDIT: Q-C-4's stimulus was already the right content, and the engine fix alone makes it resolve — it now reaches LessonView's ANumberLine branch with ticks ['line','curve','line','curve','line','curve','',''] and the two '...' as blank ticks the child fills. Certification re-run: 'every declared stimulus type resolves (0 mis-tagged)' on all three files. | PRIOR: ACCEPTED (founder, 2026-08-11): 'ignore number_line being used for non-numerals. It is a better representation in Q-C-4.' The pattern sequence stays tagged as it is, Rule 7 is NOT tightened, and the item is not repaired. | ONE MECHANICAL CONSEQUENCE RECORDED SO IT IS NOT LOST, because it works against the ruling's own intent: the engine does not render this as a number line. `_nl_block` requires >=3 cells with >=2 NUMERIC and every cell numeric-or-placeholder, so word cells are rejected, `_maths_number_line` returns None, and typing falls back to TABLE. The teacher therefore sees a one-row TABLE whose first cell reads literally 'number_line: line' - the internal tag printed on screen and in the PDF export; nothing strips it (LessonView.jsx:466 and export_assessment_pdf.py:210 both branch on type=='number_line', which this is not). So the better representation the ruling prefers is not the one delivered. TWO SEPARABLE FOLLOW-UPS, both small, neither done: (a) to actually GET the tick-line rendering for word labels, relax `_nl_block` to accept non-numeric tick labels - a two-line engine change, no constitution moves, and it would make the artefact match the ruling; (b) regardless of (a), the TABLE fallback should strip a recognised tag from `content` before rendering, so an internal token can never reach a teacher. (b) is free and wanted under any reading. | PRIOR ANALYSIS RETAINED: TWO CANDIDATE REMEDIES, both cheap, founder's call: (a) tighten Rule 7 to say the tag is for NUMBER lines only and a non-numeric sequence must be plain prose in the prompt (constitution, relaxation-neutral); or (b) give the pattern case its own legal home, since a repeating-shape sequence is a reasonable prep-maths stimulus and currently has nowhere to go — which is the same gap that produced item 14 in the first place. SEPARATELY AND REGARDLESS: the TABLE fallback should strip a recognised-but-invalid tag from `content` before rendering, so an internal token can never reach a teacher. That third fix is free, is not a constitution matter, and is worth doing even if (a) or (b) is declined. ALSO A C3 MISS, owned: C3's R7 line passed this file after checking only 'no SVG/img' and 'tag present', never the cell contract the rule states.

defects.title: The served coverage note prints an INTERNAL section code to the teacher — 'S8 could not be scheduled'
defects.evidence: X=6 (below floor) serves: 'Time budget short of the chapter's full span: S8 could not be scheduled — the material is included for you to share as guided self-study or homework.' LP Rule 6 forbids this in terms: 'Section codes (S1, S2, …) are also internal references. They MUST NOT appear in any prose the teacher reads … use its title from section_titles (e.g. "the kilograms and grams section", not "S2").' The generated plan obeys that rule everywhere — C3 measured zero S-codes in any band or teacher_note across both files. THE LEAK IS THE PLATFORM'S, not the model's: serve.py:835-840 joins `fill['uncovered_sections']`, which holds raw ANCHOR strings, straight into a teacher-facing sentence. On stages whose anchor is a readable reference ('section 7.3') the result is merely terse; on preparatory the anchor is a bare code and the sentence is close to meaningless — the teacher is told 'S8' when she needs 'Comparing and composing shapes'. It is also the WORST place to be unreadable: this note is the only thing telling her which material her class will not be taught.
defects.notes: ACCEPTED, no change (founder, 2026-08-11). AND THE PREMISE IS CORRECTED BY OBSERVATION: the founder reports the note does not appear on screen at all - not during generation and not after. The code path exists (PrepareLesson.jsx:340/408 and FirstRun.jsx:439/596 both read resp.coverage_note), but it did not render in the live run, so the 'S8' string never reached a teacher. The wording defect is therefore MOOT in practice rather than merely tolerated, and no fix is made. WHAT THIS LEAVES, recorded as an observation and NOT re-argued: a teacher served below the floor is currently told nothing about the section that could not be scheduled - the dropped units still show as self-study, but the sentence naming what is missing does not display. If that is ever revisited, fix the wording at the same time; the section titles are already on the period as section_titles[]. | PRIOR ANALYSIS RETAINED: SCOPE: every stage, but only visible where the anchor is not human-readable — preparatory maths (S1..Sn) certainly, English's spine codes probably. It fires only on below-floor / uncovered serves, which is why six prior stages' C7s did not meet it: this is the campaign's FIRST below-floor serve with a genuinely uncovered section. FIX: resolve anchors to titles before composing the note. The titles are already to hand — the summary's sections[].title, and the period's own section_titles[] carries them verbatim. A one-place change in serve.py's note composition, no constitution involved, no re-author. The same substitution should be applied to the `overlap_sections` runway sentence (serve.py:829-834), which joins the same raw anchors.

defects.title: register_scan does not read dropped_units, so a below-floor serve under-reports its own register
defects.evidence: X=6 scans MECHANICALLY CLEAN (0 ban hits) while the plan it describes hands the teacher two DROPPED units as guided self-study, and dropped U8 carries a ban-2 completion breach — '…curved, triangle, rectangle, square, circle — that has been built across the chapter.' Scanning that unit on its own returns the hit immediately, so the text is reachable; `scan_plan` simply never walks `result.dropped_units`. Dropped units are teacher-facing BY DESIGN (e09: rendered online via view.dropped_lp, omitted from exports), so their prose is exactly as live as a served unit's.
defects.notes: ACCEPTED, no change (founder, 2026-08-11). register_scan continues not to walk dropped_units. The consequence stands and is recorded rather than fixed: a below-floor serve reports its register cleaner than it is, because the self-study text handed to the teacher is never scanned. On this chapter that hides exactly one hit, itself already accepted as ARV-D-112, so nothing new is concealed today. | PRIOR ANALYSIS RETAINED: This is the same failure SHAPE the existing 'register scan reached the band text' guard was written to prevent — a plan reporting clean because a surface was skipped rather than checked. FIX: walk dropped_units in scan_plan alongside periods, tagging the unit so a hit reads as 'dropped U8'. Free, no constitution. NOTE the interaction with ARV-D-112: once dropped units are scanned, X=6 will report the hit it should have reported today — the accepted-defect count goes up by exposure, not by any new breach.

defects.title: Assessment THINS in the middle of the serve band — X=12/13 give 20 items where X=11 gives 33, and two taught sections carry none
defects.evidence: Founder-spotted at C8, then measured across the whole band. Items served per X: 6->31, 7->22, 8->31, 9->31, 10->25, 11->33, 12->20, 13->20, 14->30, 15/16->30. A teacher on 13 periods therefore receives FEWER questions than one on 8, 9, 10 or 11, and X=12/13 are the thinnest serves in the entire band. SECTIONS TAUGHT BUT CARRYING NO QUESTION AT ALL: S8 at X=7 and X=10; S7 AND S8 at X=12 and X=13. At X=13 the plan teaches S8 across three sittings, tells the teacher 'Every section is covered', and gives her nothing to assess it with. CAUSE - two correct rules colliding, neither wrong alone: (a) items anchor at their section's LAST unit (founder 2026-08-05: an item tests the whole section, so it becomes available only once the section completes); (b) an X-1+1 serve replaces the base's LAST unit with the borrowed one. So the section whose run reaches the end of the plan always loses its entire assessment. On the top, S8 runs units 10-13 with all 10 items on U13, and U13 is exactly what the synthesis borrow displaces. The concentration was already visible at C3 (10 of 30 items on one unit) and flagged there; this is that finding arriving. NOTE THE IRONY: X=6, the BELOW-FLOOR serve that actually drops teaching content, is the only non-identity serve that keeps every question - dropped units carry their items with them. The mid-band serves have no such channel.
defects.notes: ACCEPTED (founder, 2026-08-11): 'i will grudgingly accept it as this is finally the logic we have set up knowing the shortcomings.' TWO REMEDIES WERE PROPOSED AND BOTH WERE REJECTED ON ARCHITECTURE, correctly, and the reasons are the durable part of this record: (1) RE-ANCHOR AT SERVE TIME - rejected because it BYPASSES THE 8-RULE TABLE. The item->unit link is DERIVED from the declared join (section_ref -> section_refs[]); re-anchoring is the platform inventing a link the join does not give, in direct breach of P5.5's 'genon does not invent linkage', and it risks presenting questions for material not taught in the sitting they land on. (2) ROUTE THE LOST ITEMS THROUGH dropped_units - rejected because dropping is an LP-SITTING mechanism belonging to the lending/borrowing arithmetic, not an assessment channel. Coupling the two would entangle assessment with the borrow architecture, which is the class of entanglement that killed the two previous engines. NOT A DEFECT AGAINST ANY RULE: every item resolves correctly through row 5, nothing mis-anchors, and C9's checks pass. This is a priced consequence of the design, now measured for the first time. STANDING NOTE FOR S9-S11 AND THE SWEEP: this recurs at EVERY stage, and its severity scales with how concentrated the tail section's items are - a chapter whose last section runs long and anchors many items will thin hardest in the middle of its band. Measure it per chapter rather than rediscover it.

defects.title: Rule 6's 10-word inline-quotation cap breached by 52% of quotations — ARV-D-108's twin at preparatory
defects.evidence: LP Rule 6 mandates band narration as book_ref ("description up to 10 words.... "). Across the library's 120 quotations: 62 over the cap (52%), median 11 words, max 28. PER FILE the spread is the interesting part - standard 18/45 (40%, median 9, max 19), p08 15/33 (45%, median 10, max 17), and p11 29/42 (69%, median 14, max 28). p11 is the outlier twice over: it breaches hardest AND it emits ZERO of the mandated '....' truncation markers, where the standard used 20 and p08 used 16. So p11's run did not merely overshoot the cap, it ignored the truncation convention entirely. THIS IS ARV-D-108's TWIN: maths middle measured 75 of 88 (85%) against the same 10-word cap in its Rule 10. Two stages of the same subject, same rule, same failure - which makes it a family property rather than a per-stage accident.
defects.notes: ACCEPTED (founder, 2026-08-11), same disposition as ARV-D-108 at maths middle. The cap stands unamended, the quotations are not truncated, and no library re-authors. | THE WORKED EVIDENCE, kept because it is what makes the risk legible: THE SAME TASK, quoted by two canonicals of the SAME chapter, at opposite ends of the cap. Standard u13 -> 'Tangram p.63 ("Use the pieces from the tangram puzzle....")' = 7 words, truncated. p11 u11 -> 'Tangram p.63 ("Use the pieces from the tangram puzzle given in the end of the book. Can you create these shapes using some of the pieces?")' = 24 words, the book's instruction whole. Nothing in the pipeline decides which of those a teacher gets. At 7 words it is a LOCATOR; at 24 it is the task REPRODUCED. That is the entire distance between pointing at the book and copying it, and it is currently left to the model's mood on the day. | PREFERRED REMEDY IF EVER REVISITED: the deterministic truncation post-step, not a widened cap - the rule already describes '.... if truncated', and the standard and p08 did it unaided 36 times between them, so the convention works when it is followed. A post-step makes it always followed at Rs 0. SEPARATE FROM THE COPYRIGHT QUESTION, and that separation matters: C14's copyright verdict is CLEAN on its own terms (26.8% of the chapter reached, longest verbatim run 24 words, every quotation attributed). The cap is a STYLE rule about how much book text rides inline in a band, not a legal one. But it is the conduit the copyright guarantee runs through - S7's C14 recorded that ch 7's copyright pass 'holds only because the summary paraphrases, so the guarantee is doing no work', and the same caveat applies here. REMEDY OPTIONS, none taken: (a) accept, as ARV-D-108 was; (b) widen the cap to what generation actually produces (~15 words) - relaxation-only, free, and it would make the rule true; (c) leave the cap and add a deterministic post-step that truncates over-long quotations at the word boundary and appends '....', which is what the rule already describes and what the standard and p08 did unaided 36 times between them.

defects.title: the synthesis unit was filed under the section it names, so the teacher never read 'Synthesis' — ARV-D-101's shape on a third stage
