defects.title: the standard's last two units are a PAIR (prepare the posters, then present them), so the X-1+1 form drops the preparation and keeps the presentation
defects.evidence:
Top U15 'Cultural Fair - Research and Prepare' MAKES the charts; U16 (the mandated synthesis) presents them - materials ['Group posters and charts prepared previously'], visual_aids 'Group-created posters and charts', opening band 'Groups set up their posters'.

X=15 serves top U1-U14 + the synthesis and DROPS U15: the teacher reaches her last sitting needing posters no unit in her plan ever made.
X=14 serves p13's U1-U13 + the borrowed synthesis, and p13's own U13 is 'Cultural Fair - Research and Presentation' - so the Cultural Fair runs TWICE, back to back.

The certifier passes both. The register's three bans are clock quantity / forward reference / calendar time, and 'prepared previously' is a BACKWARD reference, which the register explicitly legalises. Per-unit independence lives only in the top brief ('MATERIALS, OPENING MOVES AND HOMEWORK ARE PER-UNIT. No unit may require that another unit was taught... in order to run') and NOTHING TESTS IT. Same family as ARV-D-023 (anchoring is not teaching) and ARV-D-103 (the synthesis borrow repeats the sitting before it).

The model wrote the rule and then broke it: U16's own teacher_facilitation_note says 'Name the content, not any particular earlier activity.'
defects.notes: Two candidate fixes, founder's call. (a) BRIEF: forbid a unit whose materials or opening move name an artefact another unit produces - cheap, iterates at failure speed, does not enter a constitution, triggers only a --certify-only re-run for future chapters but a re-author (~Rs 38) for this one. (b) CERTIFIER: a free gate scanning the synthesis unit's materials/visual_aids/opening band for artefact dependence ('prepared previously', 'their posters', 'from the last'). (b) catches it everywhere for nothing and should land regardless; (a) is what stops it being authored.
defects.decision:
PARTIALLY FIXED 2026-08-11 by founder-declared ONE-OFF unit permutation on the TOP canonical alone: U14 <-> U15, so 'Cultural Fair - Research and Prepare' moves inside the X=15 prefix. Applied by genon/repair_unit_order.py (order [1..13,15,14,16]), which gained an item-self-sufficient path for TWAU's flat handoff + flat period_ref[] items - units, handoff entries and items travel together, asserted by an item/unit accounting invariant; backup at ch_05_canonical.json.bak_pre_unit_order; recorded in genon_canonical.repairs[]. Re-certified free: deterministic ALL PASS, sweep unchanged, register still 0 hits, one item per unit 1..16, anchors / registry / first-visit order / Rule 3's mode cap all unmoved (the pair share a section, so nothing structural travels).

X=15 now OK. X=14 IS STILL BROKEN and is why this is not closed: it serves the prefix of 13 and drops BOTH units whatever their order. Fixing it needs the poster unit at position <=13 - a three-unit move [1..12,15,13,14,16] - which is a bigger structural claim than a swap of two neighbours and is the founder's call. The general fix is unchanged and still owed: a brief line forbidding a unit whose materials or opening move name an artefact another unit produces, plus a free certifier gate scanning the synthesis unit for artefact dependence. Reordering rescues one X per chapter by hand; only the brief stops it being authored.

★ CLOSED 2026-08-12 — the general fix landed. variant_plans.py gains an explicit ARTEFACT rule in BOTH briefs: 'NO UNIT MAY DEPEND ON A PHYSICAL ARTEFACT ANOTHER UNIT PRODUCES. If a unit needs a poster, chart, model, collection or draft to exist, it must make it itself within its own minutes, or the material must be something any classroom already has... Where the chapter genuinely wants a make-then-present pair, put BOTH acts inside ONE unit.'

WHY A NEW LINE WAS NEEDED WHEN 'MATERIALS ARE PER-UNIT' WAS ALREADY THERE: it was obeyed in the letter. Nothing in ch 5 said 'as we did last time'. The dependency arrived through the PROPS — a materials list is not prose, so the register's three bans never reach it, and 'no unit may require that another unit was taught' reads to a model as a rule about REFERENCES rather than about THINGS. The new line says the quiet part and names the escape hatch (put both acts in one unit).

The plan-granularity brief gets its own wording: the REFERENCE ban is correctly relaxed there (every unit of a canonical is served with every other) but the ARTEFACT rule is not a reference rule and survives the relaxation — the closer of a K-unit arc is borrowed into a K+1 serve, where the unit that would have made its props is not guaranteed present.

X=14 ON THIS CHAPTER IS NOT RETROSPECTIVELY FIXED and is not worth Rs 38 to re-author: the brief governs what is authored NEXT, and ch 5's remaining exposure is one X in an eleven-wide band, on a chapter whose closer is otherwise sound. Carried to the human gate as a declared residue.

defects.title: one item carries question_type 'HI' - a dominant_mode code, outside the closed taxonomy - and its question_text is null
defects.evidence:
ch_05_canonical.json, the item anchored to U11 ('Headgear from Every Region', dominant_mode HI). question_type = 'HI', which breaches assessment Rule 3 PROHIBITION 1 and A1 PROHIBITION 1 ({MCQ, SCR, ECR, OPEN_TASK} is closed). CAUSE IS VISIBLE IN THE CONSTITUTION: Rule 3's guidance table puts dominant_mode in the LEFT column and the type in the right ('HI / CG-6 inquiry steps... | SCR') and the model copied the left.

The item is otherwise a correct SCR - guide.SCR present, three expected_elements, options [], task/scaffold '' - so the SHAPE is right and only the label is wrong. But question_text is null, which breaches A1's 'Populate every field on every item; fields not applicable MUST be present as empty arrays [] or empty strings "" - never omitted'. null is neither, and for an SCR the stem IS the question: as authored there is nothing to ask.

Nothing in the pipeline reads either. The certifier checks structure, STEP 6 checks option order; no gate reads question_type against the taxonomy or checks that a non-OPEN_TASK item has a stem. Same class as ARV-D-084 (a wrong answer shipped verified:true) - the pipeline does not look at the field.
defects.notes: Two free gates at --certify-only time, both worth having for every stage: (1) question_type must be in the subject's declared taxonomy; (2) a non-OPEN_TASK item must carry a non-empty question_text, and an OPEN_TASK must carry ''. Repairing this one item in place is deterministic for the type ('HI' -> 'SCR', which its own guide key already declares) but NOT for the stem - the question has to be written, so this needs either a hand repair or a re-author.
defects.decision:
BACKFILLED 2026-08-12, founder-directed, on the TOP canonical. Both halves repaired through genon/repair_c3.py's DECLARED path; backup backup/c3_repair/20260812_093828/; recorded in genon_canonical.repairs[]; derived plans purged; re-certified free, deterministic ALL PASS.

(a) question_type 'HI' -> 'SCR'. NOT A GUESS: the item's own guide is keyed SCR, it carries three expected_elements and an empty options[] - the SCR shape in every particular - so the file already declared what it was and the repair makes the label agree with it.
(b) question_text null -> an authored stem, written to the item's OWN three expected_elements, one clause each: 'Name one traditional headgear worn in a particular region of India. In two or three sentences, explain why that headgear suits the region it comes from, and what it tells us about the people who wear it.' Grounded in the anchored section (Diversity Everywhere: saafa/pagri from Rajasthan, topi from Himachal Pradesh, Textbook p. 87) and in its unit's activity (U11 'Headgear from Every Region'). No element added that the guide did not already expect, none left unasked; the Rule 7 regional-variation annotation already covered the answer's spread and is untouched.

VERIFIED ACROSS THE WHOLE LIBRARY AFTER THE REPAIR: 39 items, zero off-taxonomy, zero guide-key mismatches, zero missing stems, zero non-empty OPEN_TASK stems, zero NULLs. TOP types now MCQ 4 / SCR 6 / OPEN_TASK 4 / ECR 2.

THE TWO FREE GATES REMAIN OWED and are the real fix - question_type must be in the subject's declared taxonomy, and a non-OPEN_TASK item must carry a non-empty question_text. Both run at --certify-only for Rs 0. This backfill repaired one instance; nothing yet stops the next.

defects.title: section_context breaches its cap AGAIN at 10-25 - live output runs 13-35, so the number is still wrong after being widened the same day
defects.evidence: LP v1.4 widened Rule 5's cap from 10-15 to 10-25 at P-prep on measured corpus evidence (3 saved plans, 24 periods, 14 above 15, range 10-28). The library authored UNDER v1.4 breaches the new bound too: top 20-31 (7 of 16 over), p13 13-35 (2 of 13), p10 18-32 (3 of 10) - 12 of 39 units over 25. The lower bound is still never approached.
defects.notes: S4's standing lesson, twice over: 'a limit stated as a number is the kind of rule live generation most often disproves.' The P-prep amendment was right to look and still landed on a number the generator does not respect. Options: widen to ~35, or DROP the upper bound and state the intent in kind (the v1.4 sentence already says 'name every object the period actually used... do not drop an object to fit a length', which is the rule doing the real work). Relaxation-only either way, so no library re-authors.
defects.decision:
FIXED 2026-08-12 by DROPPING the number, not raising it — LP v1.4 -> v1.5, exactly as the acceptance note said to if revisited. Third setting of this cap, second live disproof (<=v1.2 10-15, breached by 14/24 corpus periods; v1.4 10-25, breached by 12/39 generated units).

section_context is a LABEL, not prose: it names the objects a unit drew from and the assessment reads it to ground its question. Length is a property of the UNIT'S CONTENT, not of good writing, so a cap forces a choice between naming what was used and hitting a number — and on a dense unit the only way to satisfy it is to DROP an object, degrading the assessment's grounding to protect nothing. v1.4 already forbade that in prose, so the number and the sentence were in contradiction.

REPLACED BY THE RULE IN KIND: a LIST of what the period handled, not a sentence about it — name every object used, name nothing that was not, no commentary, length follows content. Both surfaces moved (rule + schema comment). RELAXATION-ONLY: one MUST NOT added, restating v1.4's own do-not-drop instruction, and the edit script asserts the delta is exactly +1. No library re-authors.

TRANSFERABLE RULE for S9-S11 and the pre-warm: when a constitution states a number about the LENGTH OF A FIELD WHOSE LENGTH IS SET BY CONTENT, the number is the defect. Widening buys one run. Ask what the field is FOR — if the answer is 'so something downstream can read it', the honest constraint is completeness, not size.

defects.title: a repair_c3.py pass declared GENERIC is mathematics-only, and proposed writing maths text into nine TWAU guides
defects.evidence:
repair_c3.py splits its passes into GENERIC ('derive the correct value from an AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE... intended to run over the whole corpus at the mass pre-warm. Adding a chapter costs nothing.') and DECLARED (per-chapter, hand-written). pass_open_task_substitution (ARV-D-082) sits in the GENERIC list. Its authority is MATHEMATICS' Rule 8 open-task menu, and the constant it appends says so in words: 'The teacher may substitute any other format from the Mathematics open-task menu.'

Run on the_world_around_us v ch 5 for an unrelated declared repair, it proposed NINE edits across the library (4 top / 3 p13 / 2 p10), appending that sentence to OPEN_TASK guides on a stage whose Rule 8 is EXECUTABILITY BOUNDARY and which has no open-task menu at all. Not a harmless no-op: it writes a false statement about a non-existent rule, in another subject's vocabulary, into a certified artefact - and the pass is declared corpus-safe, so at the mass pre-warm it would have reached every non-maths OPEN_TASK guide in the corpus.

FOUND BY ACCIDENT. S5 ran the tool only to backfill ARV-D-120; the dry-run line 'WOULD REPAIR ... ARV-D-082 x4' is the whole warning there was.
defects.decision:
FIXED 2026-08-12. The pass gates on ctx['subject'] == 'mathematics' and returns [] elsewhere; subject/grade/chapter now ride in ctx so a pass whose authority is one subject's constitution can declare that fact. Verified both ways: TWAU dry-run drops to ARV-D-120 only, maths IX ch 4 is unchanged (already repaired, nothing to do, no regression).

THE OTHER FOUR PASSES WERE AUDITED AND ARE SAFE ON TWAU BY ACCIDENT, NOT BY DESIGN - recorded in the docstring so the next stage checks authority rather than behaviour: pass_method_label keys on `pedagogical_method`, a field TWAU has no equivalent of; pass_strip_internal_ids matches WE-N/E-N, which TWAU never emits (its ids are T-N); pass_verbatim_descriptions reads enumerated_worked_examples/enumerated_exercises, absent from TWAU summaries. Only pass_guide_shape is genuinely subject-agnostic.
defects.carried: THE GENERAL LESSON, owed to S9-S11 and to the mass pre-warm: 'generic' in this tool has meant 'happened not to fire on the one subject it was written for'. Before the corpus-wide run, re-read each pass and ask what CONSTITUTION its correct value comes from - if the answer names a subject, it is not generic. English is the next family and shares none of maths' vocabulary.

defects.title: no certifier gate reads question_type against the taxonomy, or checks that a non-OPEN_TASK item has a stem
defects.evidence:
S5's ARV-D-120 shipped a certified library carrying question_type 'HI' (a dominant_mode code, outside every subject's closed taxonomy) on an item whose question_text was null. Both passed certification, STEP 6 and generate_canonical.validate. The certifier checks STRUCTURE, STEP 6 checks option ORDER, and nothing reads either field's VALUE - the same shape as ARV-D-084, where a wrong maths answer shipped with verified:true.

The cause of the type error is visible in the constitution and will recur: assessment Rule 3's guidance table puts dominant_mode in the LEFT column and the question type in the right, so a model that copies the wrong column emits a plausible-looking value.
defects.notes: Two gates, both free at --certify-only, both subject-agnostic if they read the taxonomy from the subject rather than a constant: (1) every item's question_type must be a member of that subject-stage's declared type set; (2) a non-OPEN_TASK item must carry a non-empty question_text, and an OPEN_TASK must carry '' (the schemas specify both directions). Neither needs a constitution change. S5's backfill repaired one instance; nothing yet stops the next, and every remaining stage authors items under a rule with the same table shape.
defects.decision:
BUILT 2026-08-12, founder-directed, BEFORE the defect fixes it guards — three gates in build_library.py::certify, all free at --certify-only.

(1) KNOWN-TYPE GATE. Every question_type must be in KNOWN_ITEM_TYPES — the union of every type the corpus actually uses, from a census over all saved plans plus the backup corpus (MCQ, SCR, ECR, NUM, OPEN_TASK, SOURCE_INTERPRETATION, FILL_IN, MATCH, TRUE_FALSE, ORAL_PROMPT, WRITING_TASK, PROJECT, EXTRACT_ANALYSIS). Deliberately the UNION across eleven stages rather than one stage's closed set: the gate quarantines, so it must never fire on a legal value. It still catches the real failure mode exactly, because a value copied out of another enumeration is not an assessment type in ANY constitution. The failure message names the cause — 'check the type-selection TABLE: its left column is another enumeration'.
(2) STEM GATE, both directions. A non-OPEN_TASK item must carry a non-empty question_text; an OPEN_TASK must carry exactly '' with its prompt in `task`.
(3) SINGLETON ADVISORY, never a gate: a question_type used by exactly one item in the whole library.

PROVEN BOTH WAYS. On the real S5 library: ALL PASS, 48 checks, quarantine clean. On a scratch copy with the exact pre-repair defect re-injected (question_type 'HI', question_text None): BOTH gates FAIL by name — "unit [11]: question_type 'HI' is not an assessment type at all" and "unit [11]: HI has question_text None — there is nothing to ask" — plus the singleton advisory, and the top's failure takes its library to quarantine per founder doctrine.

ONE MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING. The first cut derived the legal set from EACH FILE'S OWN frequencies and failed p10 on its single legitimate ECR, quarantining a good canonical. A rare-but-legal value and an illegal one are indistinguishable to a frequency test — which is why the gate now uses a corpus census and the frequency signal is advisory only. A gate that quarantines must not guess.

defects.title: p10 U3 cross-references a unit BY POSITION where content-naming was shorter — 'already encountered in the previous unit'
defects.evidence:
ch_05_canonical_p10.json U3, band 20-32: '...the Ashoka Chakra on the flag, already encountered in THE PREVIOUS UNIT of work on the tricolour, is noted as a recurring symbol.' Also reaches the served X=8 and X=9 plans.

NOT A BAN: v1.10 legalised backward reference, and register_scan correctly reports it as ADVISORY [positional], not a hit. It is a breach of this stage's own VOCABULARY clause, which says 'Cross-reference another unit by the CONTENT it built, NEVER by its position' (added at P1, standing in LP v1.5), and of the register's closing best-practice sentence.

The claim is TRUE in every serve — p10's U1-U2 teach the tricolour and the prefix is always preserved — so nothing is falsified and serving is unaffected. Content-naming was not merely available but SHORTER: 'already encountered in the tricolour work' says it in fewer words.
defects.notes: S4 because it costs nothing at serve time. Repairable in place for Rs 0 via genon/repair_register.py's declared path (one string), which would also purge the two derived plans that carry it. Alternatively accept: the machine surfaced it as advisory exactly as designed, and a human ruling that a true backward reference may stay is a legitimate outcome. Founder's call.

defects.title: already-certified libraries carry live BAN hits from register_scan patterns added AFTER they certified — nothing re-runs the gate over the corpus
defects.evidence:
C7's corpus-wide sweep (2026-08-12, 25 certified library files) reports 5 live BAN hits, none on the stage being tested:
  maths/iii ch 5 canonical + p08 + p11 — 'built/developed across the chapter' x3 [completion] — recorded, ARV-D-112 ACCEPTED
  maths/vii ch 7 canonical U11 — 'the geometric intuition built throughout the chapter' [completion] — recorded, ARV-D-100 OPEN
  maths/vii ch 7 p10 U4 — '...foreshadows the angle-sum property that follows in this section.' [forward] — **NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE**

The last is caught by the `foreshadow` pattern, which was added AFTER that library certified. That is the general shape: register_scan gains patterns at each stage's C7 (S6 added seven, S7 added the completion-by-paraphrase family, S5 added the artefact set today), and the already-certified corpus is never re-run against them. A library certified in August under July's pattern set is not certified under today's.

It only surfaced now because C7's (c) step happened to need a corpus-wide false-positive check for an unrelated change.
defects.notes: THE FIX IS ALREADY FREE. `--certify-only` is idempotent and costs Rs 0; a loop over the corpus after any register_scan pattern addition turns this from an accident into a standing check. At 25 files it takes seconds, and it would have caught the p10/U4 hit on the day the pattern landed. Worth wiring into the pattern-addition ritual C7 already mandates ('added with a dated note') — add 'and re-run the corpus'. Separately: decide whether ARV-D-100's string, still open, is repaired or accepted like its ARV-D-112 siblings.

defects.title: a BORROWED unit back-references content its home plan taught in a unit the serving prefix never reached — ARV-D-023's mirror, on the backward side
defects.evidence:
X=8 (base p10, prefix U1-U7, borrowed p10's U9). The last sitting, "India's Achievements: Then and Now", band 22-34 reads: 'Students connect this to what they observed earlier about REGIONAL DANCE FORMS SPREAD ACROSS THE MAP.'

The dance map is p10's U8 ('Mapping Dance Forms of India'). At X=8 the prefix stops at U7 (Headgear) and U8 is precisely the unit the X-1+1 form skips to make room for the borrow. THE CLASS NEVER SAW IT. Verified by scan: at X=8 the only unit mentioning dance IS the borrowed one; at X=9 and X=10 U8 is served and the same sentence is TRUE.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. The register LEGALISED backward reference at v1.10, correctly — but on the implicit assumption that 'earlier' means 'earlier in this plan'. That holds for a prefix, which is contiguous from U1. It does NOT hold for the Xth slot: the borrowed unit comes from a different POSITION in its home plan, and the units between the prefix's end and that unit's home position are exactly what the borrow skips. register_scan reports it as clean because it is neither forward reference nor completion claim; C5's first-visit and coverage checks pass because the SECTION ('Diversity Everywhere') IS covered at X=8, by the headgear unit. Section coverage is not content coverage.

This is ARV-D-023 ('anchoring is not teaching') seen from the other end: there a forward-safe unit assumed lessons the class never had; here a backward-safe one does.
defects.notes:
NOT A SELECTION ERROR — the deterministic remedies C8 names all check out. The lender DOES first-deal the next-due section (p10 U9 is the first unit of 'Spirit of Togetherness'), so the choice set is right and the tie-break is right. The fault is in the borrowed unit's own PROSE, so the remedy is the BRIEF, exactly as C8's third option says.

THE PRECISE RULE, and it must be precise or it forbids what the register welcomes: a unit may back-reference content from an EARLIER SECTION (registry order guarantees earlier sections are covered before it), but MUST NOT back-reference the content of a specific sibling unit within a multi-unit section run — any of those siblings may be the one the borrow skips. Here 'what they observed about India's diversity' would have been safe; 'regional dance forms spread across the map' names one unit's activity inside a 2-unit run.

SCOPE: affects X=8 only on this chapter (at X>=9 the sentence is true). Cheap to detect once stated — it is a sibling of the artefact rule landed the same day, and the same brief paragraph can carry both.

defects.title: the item-shape gate reads `question_text` only, so it FALSE-FAILED and quarantined a clean english library — english's constitution names the field `item_stem`
defects.evidence:
First certification of english IX ch 7 (report 20260812_143130) returned 'every non-OPEN_TASK item carries a stem (6 without)' on ALL THREE canonicals — 18 items, every one of them reported as having nothing to ask — and quarantined the whole library ('top canonical failed — the entire library is quarantined with it').

Every one of those items carries a populated stem. English's assessment constitution names the field **`item_stem`** at all three stages (its JSON schema block, and the corpus agrees: 82 occurrences of `item_stem` across saved english plans). The gate — added the same morning at S5's C3 as ARV-D-123 — reads `question_text`, on a comment asserting that 'every schema in the corpus says the same two things': a census that missed english.

WHAT MAKES IT S2 RATHER THAN S3: the gate QUARANTINES. A false positive here does not annoy a reader, it moves a paid library off disk and reports it as a fix worklist. Had this landed one stage earlier the same run would have read as 'the model omitted every stem', which is a re-generation (~Rs 80) chasing a defect that does not exist.

FIX (2026-08-12): `build_library.item_stem()` reads the stem under either name and the report names the field the item actually carries. `_STEM_FIELDS = ('question_text', 'item_stem')` is the whole inventory, verified by census over every saved plan and canonical on disk; the prototype-era maths `prompt` (471 occurrences, no canonical) is recorded in the comment and deliberately not read. Quarantine restored, re-certified on the free path: ALL PASS.

THE GENERAL LESSON, third instance in this campaign after the carrier seam and the handoff shapes: a check that names a FIELD is a check that branches on subject, whether or not it says so. The platform's own answer already existed — `carriers.period_section_codes` and `unit_approaches` read the same fact under five names each — and a new gate should reach for it rather than assume.

defects.title: the FLOOR canonical breaches LP Rule 5's 'minimum 3 bands' on 4 of its 10 units, and nothing deterministic looks at band COUNT
defects.evidence:
english LP Rule 5: 'Each period's time bands sum EXACTLY to period_duration_minutes; minimum 3 bands.' Measured on the certified library:
  ch_07_canonical.json    (17 units) — 0 breaches (54 bands, min 3)
  ch_07_canonical_p14.json (14 units) — 0 breaches (57 bands)
  ch_07_canonical_p10.json (10 units) — **4 breaches**: U2, U4, U5 and U8 carry TWO bands each ('0–25/25–50', '0–15/15–50', '0–20/20–50', '0–20/20–50').
TILING IS CLEAN everywhere — every unit tiles 0..50 with no gap or overlap — so this is the count alone.

It appears only on the FLOOR canonical, which is where the S8 lesson says a stated number gets tested: at 10 periods a whole (section × spine) cell lands in one unit and the model writes it as two long moves. Whether that is a defect or a rule that should relax is a C3 read and a founder call — the same shape as S4's word counts (relaxed) and S7's consecutive-method cap (relaxed with an exception).

WHAT IS NOT ARGUABLE: nothing tests it. The certifier checks the register, the anchors, coverage, stimulus tags, item shape and MCQ order; band COUNT and band TILING are checked nowhere, though `normalize.phase_tiling_issues` already exists and would give both for free on every stage. Owed as a certifier check, in the same list as S7/S8's un-built 'no section appears in two non-contiguous runs'.

ACCEPTED AS AUTHORED — founder ruling 2026-08-12, at C3. No repair, no re-author, no constitution change. The finding stays on the register so the RATE stays visible across the remaining stages; it does not gate C3 and does not re-open anything.

defects.title: the mandated SYNTHESIS unit depends on a physical artefact another unit produced — and it is the unit the serve engine borrows
defects.evidence:
ch_07_canonical.json U17 (the closing synthesis):
  materials: "Students' draft article (notebooks or draft sheets)"
  band [30–50]: 'Students COMPLETE the draft article "Our Inspiring Elderly" (Paragraphs 3 and 4 …)'
The draft is produced at U15: 'Students draft Paragraphs 1 and 2 independently.'

The standard-canonical brief forbids exactly this: 'NO UNIT MAY DEPEND ON A PHYSICAL ARTEFACT ANOTHER UNIT PRODUCES … A unit that lists "prepared previously", "their charts from earlier" or "the models they built" in `materials` is asking for a sitting that may not have happened.' U17 is the CASE-1 BORROW: a teacher on X=11 receives p10's ten units plus this one, and p10's writing unit (U9) asks for the WHOLE four-paragraph article in a single sitting — so the borrowed closer tells that class to finish paragraphs they either never started or already finished.

TWO THINGS MAKE IT PRECISE. (1) The model half-obeyed: the band hedges ('Those who have already completed the draft review it …') and the teacher note says outright 'Students need not have covered every task to participate: the chapter's content is now the shared ground.' The prose understood the independence requirement; `materials` did not. (2) `register_scan` CANNOT catch it — this is a BACKWARD dependency, which the register explicitly permits since v1.10; the artefact rule lives only in the brief and nothing enforces it.

Same family as ARV-D-023 (e11, found at S1's C7): a borrowed unit assuming a sitting the host class never had. Flagged for C8, which inspects this transition directly. The cheap fix is a certifier check over `materials` and the opening band for artefact language — free, subject-agnostic, and the third such check now owed alongside band-count/tiling (ARV-D-128) and the non-contiguous-section check inherited from S7/S8.

ACCEPTED AS AUTHORED — founder ruling 2026-08-12, at C3. No repair, no re-author, no constitution change. The finding stays on the register so the RATE stays visible across the remaining stages; it does not gate C3 and does not re-open anything.

CLOSED 2026-08-12 — superseded by the ARV-D-136 re-author. This row was the C3 (authoring) reading of the same unit and was ACCEPTED as authored; the artefact it describes no longer exists on disk. The `materials` line and the 'complete the draft' band are both gone from the re-authored U17.

defects.title: assessment Rule 12's `total_items` was never emitted, and the two canonicals disagree on the SHAPE of `period_schedule`
defects.evidence:
(a) Rule 12 requires the assessment header to carry `total_items`. Neither file emits it. Nothing reads it — the count is derivable and the platform derives it — so this is a constitution/artefact mismatch rather than a functional defect: either the model should emit it or Rule 12 should drop it.

(b) A1 says 'exactly ONE row {period_duration_minutes, period_count}'. The standard emits `[{...}]` (a list of one); the p10 compact emits `{...}` (a bare dict). Same chapter, same library, two shapes — from the same prompt. Nothing downstream breaks (the serve path reads `genon.matrix` / `served_matrix`, and the display reads `period_rows_snapshot`), which is exactly why it would survive unnoticed until something did read it.

Both are cheap to close and neither justifies a re-author on its own; fold them into whatever pass repairs ARV-D-130/131.

defects.title: a fill serve withholds items correctly but declares nothing — the handoff still asserts all six cells while the paper ships four
defects.evidence:
X=12 (english IX ch 7, variant p14): LP covers all six cells, assessment carries FOUR items. X=13: five. Neither serve declares anything — `section_coverage_note` is None, `dropped_units` is empty, and the six-spine `coverage_handoff` rides in full, so the artefact asserts complete coverage.

MECHANISM, exact. An item anchors at its cell's LAST unit (founder ruling 2026-08-05: an item tests the cell's whole `implied_lo`, so it becomes available only when the cell completes). p14's last-unit map is RFC 6 · VG 8 · LIS 9 · SPK 10 · WRT 12 · BYT 14. At X=12 the serve is p14's first 11 units plus one borrowed unit, so units 12 and 14 are not served — WRT's and BYT's items are filtered out while both cells ARE taught (the prefix contains their first units, and the borrowed unit first-deals BYT).

`genon.assessment_items_unserved: 2` is the engine's own record of it, and it lives in the PROVENANCE block that no teacher and no export reads.

WHY ENGLISH IS THE STAGE THAT SURFACES IT: assessment Rule 2 gives english exactly ONE item per (section × spine) cell — six per chapter — so two lost items is 33% of the paper. SS·secondary, with 18 items over 9 sections, loses the same way and it reads as a couple of missing questions. The mechanism is subject-agnostic; only the visibility is english's.

NOT the below-floor drop (ARV-D-135 is that, and it is declared). This is INSIDE the band, at counts a teacher routinely asks for, with nothing said.

The shape of a fix is a founder call and there are at least three: anchor the item at the cell's FIRST served unit when its last is not served; or keep the anchoring rule and DECLARE the loss in `section_coverage_note` the way a dropped section is declared; or refuse a fill whose prefix truncates a cell mid-run. The first changes what an item means, the second changes only what the teacher is told.

DOWNGRADED S2 -> S3 AT C9 (2026-08-12), and re-diagnosed. The ABSENCE is specified behaviour — C9 check 3(b): 'an item whose unit is not in the plan is not in the plan', with the count reported in `assessment_items_unserved`, which it is. It is also pedagogically right: p14 teaches Writing across U11 AND U12, X=12 stops before U12, so the class drafted the article but never did the revision sitting — and an item tests the cell's WHOLE implied_lo (founder, 2026-08-05). Withholding is the anchoring doctrine working.

WHAT SURVIVES: the served plan says two different things. `coverage_handoff` carries all six cells — asserting complete coverage — while the paper ships four, and the only record of the difference is a provenance field. There is no `section_coverage_note`, because nothing was dropped in the LP sense. That is a DECLARATION gap, not a mis-anchoring: contract drift a teacher notices only by counting. Remedy is one sentence in the channel the below-floor case already uses, not a change to anchoring.

defects.title: WITHDRAWN at C9 — the below-floor item IS flagged `unscheduled` and its sitting number is the dropped unit's own; this is check 3(c), not a defect
defects.evidence:
X=9 (below the floor of 10). The LP half is exactly right: BYT is dropped, `section_coverage_note` names it ("Time budget short of the chapter's full span: A|beyond_text could not be scheduled"), and `result.dropped_units` carries the lost unit verbatim, flagged `unscheduled: true`.

The assessment half is not. `Q-BT-A-1` is still in the paper, carrying `period_ref: [10]` — sitting 10 of a NINE-sitting plan. `genon.assessment_items_unscheduled: 1` records it in provenance; the item itself is neither removed nor marked, so a teacher who prints this assessment asks her class a question on the one thing the plan has just told her she has no time to teach.

The inverse of ARV-D-134 and the same seam: the item's unit is resolved once, at authoring time, against a plan the teacher may only partly receive. Here the platform already KNOWS (it dropped the unit and said so), which is what makes this the cheaper half to fix: whatever channel declares a dropped section can drop or flag the item that tests it.

WITHDRAWN 2026-08-12 AT C9. The item carries `unscheduled: true` and `period_ref: [10]`, where sitting 10 is the dropped unit's number in THIS plan — `result.dropped_units` carries it verbatim. C9 check 3(c) requires exactly that shape, and e13 (ARV-D-037, S1) established it after the opposite behaviour printed 7 of 20 questions about units a class never had. My C6 read printed `period_ref` without printing the `unscheduled` key beside it. Recorded rather than deleted: the misreading is the useful part — when the engine has a documented state for a case, read the state before rating the output.

defects.title: the borrowed SYNTHESIS unit continues a piece of student work another unit began — coherent in the standard, wrong in both plans that borrow it
defects.evidence:
C8 rated six transitions; the four self-fills are clean and BOTH Case-1 synthesis borrows (X=11 host p10, X=15 host p14) are jumpy, for one reason.

The borrowed unit (the standard's U17) spends its last band — 20 of 50 minutes — on "Students COMPLETE THE DRAFT ARTICLE 'Our Inspiring Elderly' (Paragraphs 3 and 4)", with `materials: ["Students' draft article (notebooks or draft sheets)"]`.

In its own plan that is coherent: U15 drafts Paragraphs 1 and 2, U17 completes 3 and 4. BOTH COMPACTS WRITE THE WHOLE ARTICLE IN ONE SITTING — p10's U9 ("plan and draft their article … they write the title at the top and their name and grade below it", then peer-exchange and revise) and p14's U11 ("write their four-paragraph article independently"). So a borrowing class arrives with a FINISHED article and is instructed to write the two paragraphs it completed two sittings earlier. The hedge "Those who have already completed the draft review it" was written for a few fast finishers and here describes the entire class.

The unit is coherent in exactly one of the three plans it can appear in — its own — which is the ARV-D-025 profile (a closing unit importing the lending plan's priors) arriving through student WORK rather than through prose.

WHAT MAKES IT S2: it is 40% of a sitting, it is teacher-facing, and it lands on the one unit the engine is guaranteed to move between plans.

defects.title: re-authoring a canonical does not purge the derived plans that BORROWED from it — the cache key names the chosen variant, never the lender
defects.evidence:
Measured on this chapter immediately after the ARV-D-136 re-author of the top:
  X=11 -> key ch_07_50m11_e19_c20260812142824 (p10's version) — file ON DISK, and it still contains 'complete the draft article'
  X=15 -> key ch_07_50m15_e19_c20260812142352 (p14's version) — same
  X=16 -> key moved to c20260812154258 (the top IS its chosen variant) — safe

So the two serves ARV-D-136 was raised about, and which cost Rs 28.74 to fix, are the two that would still be handed to a teacher unfixed — `api/main.py` returns the cached file and discards the correct plan it just computed.

ROOT CAUSE. `purge_derived` is wired into every REPAIR tool (normalize_options, repair_register, repair_anchors, repair_leaked_deliberation, repair_item_type) and into no GENERATOR. `canonical_version()`'s docstring — 'regenerating the canonical therefore produces a NEW key' — holds only for the chosen variant; a served plan can carry a unit BORROWED from another canonical, and the key does not name the lender. Re-author the lender and the content changes while the key stands still. This is ARV-D-034's family (stale bytes served because the key did not move) on the one path the 2026-08-04 fix did not cover.

REMEDY, founder call: (1) call `purge_derived` from `generate_canonical`'s install path, exactly as every repair tool does — consistent with the doctrine, and the cost is already accepted in writing ('a teacher holding a purged plan loses that file and re-prepares'); or (2) name the lender in the key (`c<chosen>` + `b<lender>`), which re-keys only borrow-bearing plans but hangs a second token off the filename, the very thing reverted on 2026-08-04 for readability.

IMMEDIATE, for this chapter: delete ch_07_50m11_e19_c20260812142824.json, ch_07_50m15_e19_c20260812142352.json and ch_07_50m16_e19_c20260812141916.json. The other four served plans carry no borrowed unit from the top and are unaffected.

CLOSED 2026-08-12. `purge_derived` is now called from `generate_canonical.install_canonical` — every regeneration invalidates the chapter's derived plans, as every repair tool already did. Regression test in `tests/test_genon_plan_key.py` (asserts the call, its chapter and apply=True). The cache-hit half was then measured through the real endpoint: a repeat request returns `cached: true` in 4.2 ms with the file's mtime unchanged.

ONE ARTEFACT OF THIS DEFECT SURVIVES ON DISK and needs a manual delete — `ch_07_60m2-50m13_e19_c20260812142352.json`, kumar3's mixed week, which borrows unit 17 and still carries the old synthesis. defects.title: assessment Rule 9 licenses a 3–8 line verbatim extract from `poem_text`, which is the NCERT poem itself — F2's conduit, open on 8 of this class's 16 chapters

On a prose chapter the conduit is closed by construction.

ON A POEM IT IS OPEN. Rule 9's [SECONDARY DELTA] permits the extract block to be drawn from `poem_text`, and Rule 3 licenses 'a specific line, image, or phrase from poem_text'. `poem_text` is not a paraphrase — it is the poem. Measured on ch 2 'Bharat Our Land': the summary carries 16 poem lines and **13 appear verbatim in the NCERT chapter PDF**. A poem chapter's item would therefore place 3–8 lines of an NCERT-published poem into a CANONICAL, and canonicals are precisely what the copyright review's v1.1 ruling sends to the cloud.

This is F2 landing where `docs/NCERT_copyright_review.md` predicted it would: 'the verbatim conduit must be either closed (substitute a paraphrase + page ref) or licensed before English plans are served commercially.'

SCALE: 8 of the 16 chapters in english IX are poems (chs 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16), carrying 10-33 lines of poem_text each. Nothing in the ch 7 library is affected — the exposure is in the constitution, not the artefact — so this blocks no certification check, but it should be ruled on before the STAGE is certified, because certifying a stage is a statement about its constitution.

REMEDY, and it is one clause: poem sections already carry `poem_appreciation_summary`, Aruvi's own writing — the very thing that makes the prose path safe. Rule 9 becomes 'the extract block is drawn from `prose_summary` / `drama_summary` / `poem_appreciation_summary`; `poem_text` may be cited by line reference but never reproduced'. A P2 amendment, so §9 would re-author any poem-chapter library authored under the old text — none exists yet, which is why doing it now costs nothing.

CLOSED 2026-08-12 BY ASSESSMENT v1.5 — the poem locator. Rule 9 now carries two stimulus forms: the verbatim extract block, restricted to `prose_summary` / `drama_summary` (Aruvi's own prose, which is what makes reproducing it safe), and — the ONLY permitted form for a poem section — a LOCATOR: `Read lines N–M on p.PP, beginning "<incipit>".`, incipit capped at EIGHT WORDS, no ellipsis, no second fragment, and the poem's lines copied into no field at all. Rule 4's type definition, Rule 3's REQUIRED list and the schema comment carry the matching edits; the 'or inline' escape into `item_stem` is closed for poems.

THE APPRECIATION-SUMMARY ROUTE WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED as the primary fix: it is Aruvi's prose (zero verbatim runs in seven of eight chapters) but three chapters quote 4–6 word lines inside the commentary, so it narrows the conduit rather than closing it — and it costs the pedagogy, since an extract-analysis question on a poem is 'read these lines closely'. The locator keeps the reading and removes the reproduction.

Reading `poem_text` is deliberately still permitted (INPUTS §2, Rule 2(a), Rule 6) — the summary never leaves the machine. §9 re-authors nothing: ch 7 is prose and satisfies v1.5 unchanged, and no poem-chapter library exists.

defects.title: PrepareLesson suggested MORE periods than the chapter's top canonical holds — a per-chapter Math.round where the rest of the product apportions (40 of 340 chapters, 5 subjects)
defects.evidence:
FOUND BY THE FOUNDER on the ch 8 top canonical: the library is authored at 12 periods and the Prepare Lesson screen was offering 13.

TWO ROUNDING METHODS OVER THE SAME THREE NUMBERS. `genon/master_plan.py` computes `recommended_periods` by LARGEST REMAINDER, so a class's chapters sum to exactly its annual budget; `YearPlan.jsx` does the same client-side. `PrepareLesson.jsx::suggestionFor` instead re-derived its own figure as `Math.round(weight_c / Σweights × budget)`, independently per chapter. English VI ch 8: 16.5 / 182.5 × 140 = 12.658 → 13, where the master plan says 12 — eleven chapters were entitled to the +1 and ch 8's .658 remainder came twelfth. The screen's column summed to 142 against a 140 budget.

WHY IT IS S2 AND NOT COSMETIC: 13 > the 12-period TOP canonical, so a teacher accepting the default asked for more periods than the library holds and was served the serve engine's ABOVE-THE-TOP SURRENDER path — a surrendered plan, by default, on the pilot chapter of the stage being certified. Two screens also contradicted each other for the same teacher on the same chapter: YearPlan said 12, Prepare Lesson said 13.

SCOPE, measured across every master-plan combo: 39 of 323 non-placeholder chapters (12.1%) were offered a default different from the count their canonicals are authored at — english|V 4/10, mathematics|V 4/15, english|VIII 3/15, mathematics|VIII 3/14, science|IX 3/13, social_sciences|VII 3/12, social_sciences|IX 3/18. Not an english defect.

FIX (2026-08-13): `largestRemainder` moved out of YearPlan.jsx into `web/app/lib/format.js` as the single exported method, with the reasoning in its docstring; both screens import it. PrepareLesson now apportions the teacher's own budget across the chapter list in one `useMemo` and reads its suggestion out of that map. The design intent is preserved — the suggestion still keys off HER budget, never NCF and never the master plan's — and when her budget equals the calibrated one the result reproduces `recommended_periods` exactly. This screen FILTERS OUT the master plan's placeholder ('Book awaited') rows, so the apportionment appends one synthetic bucket carrying the syllabus weight they hold and discards it, which keeps the founder's 2026-07-25 rule (divide by the FULL syllabus, never the listed subset) without a second denominator.

MEASURED AFTER: disagreements with the authored count fall from 39/323 to 3/323 (0.9%), and english|VI ch 8 returns 12 with the column summing to exactly 140. The three residuals are all in the two combos that HAVE placeholder rows — mathematics|IX ch 6 (14 vs 15) and social_sciences|IX ch 3 and ch 5 (13 vs 12, 22 vs 21) — where 79.5 and 108.0 units of syllabus weight are hidden behind unpublished books and the synthetic bucket can only approximate their share. That is inherent to suggesting from a partial book list and resolves itself as the content lands; it is not the rounding defect.

STATIC VERIFICATION ONLY (§11 — the sandbox cannot run `next dev`): all three files babel-parse clean, the local copy is gone from YearPlan, both components import the shared helper, and the old expression is absent. A live check at C6 is owed.

ONE THING SEEN AND NOT FIXED: `api/main.py` computes `ncf_estimated_periods` with the same non-conserving `round(w / syllabus_total_weight * ncf_total)`. It is left alone deliberately — that field is a published-norm reference shown beside ours and 'drives nothing' (testing.md, 2026-07-26). Worth a look if it is ever promoted.

Filed because a rule that nothing enforces and nothing consumes should either be enforced or struck, and this is the first time anyone has looked at it. Likely true at the sibling english stages too; not swept.

RELATED READING NOTE, filed here so it is not rediscovered: Rule 6 / Rule 12 headers must be audited in the LEDGER file (`genon/out/canonical/`), NOT the installed saved plan. `build_library.py`'s install rewraps into the app's saved-plan shape and moves header fields onto the wrapper or drops them, so an auditor reading `result` concludes the header is missing when the model emitted it in full.

defects.title: p10's homework item carries only `task_brief` — no `spine`, no `task_index`, so it cannot be traced to a summary task
defects.evidence:
FOUND AT C4, which reads all three canonicals; C3 read the top and p07 and did not see it.

`ch_11_canonical_p10.json` u6 homework: keys are `['task_brief']` alone. The LP schema says `"homework": [ <same shape as tasks_in_class entry> ]`, i.e. `{spine, task_index, task_brief}`. The other three homework items in the library (top u5, top u8, p07 u4) all carry the full triple.

NOTHING BREAKS TODAY: `tasks_anchored[]` is LP-audit-only and the assessment generator does not read homework, so no downstream consumer misses the keys. What is lost is the traceability the pair exists for — a homework item with no `{spine, task_index}` cannot be resolved back to the summary task it came from, which is the difference between a homework line and a homework REFERENCE.

Its locator is present and correct (`(p.74)`), so item 11 is unaffected. Repairable in place; one item, one file.

defects.title: MEMORY item 8's FILL_IN answer contract ('numbered to its blank') is unsatisfiable on this content — 4 of 4 — and it traces to ARV-D-146
defects.evidence:
MEMORY item 8 is english·PREPARATORY's own item, on the checklist since 2026-07-13 with the note that there was 'in fact NO English-prep saved-plan corpus on disk to have even back-checked it against'. This is its first test ever.

THE MATCH HALF PASSES CLEANLY, 5 of 5 — structured `answer_key: [{left, right}]` of 4–6 pairs plus the short fallback string, table entirely in `visual_stimulus`, instruction-only stem.

THE FILL_IN HALF FAILS. The rule: `teacher_guide.suggested_answer` = 'each blank's answer NUMBERED TO ITS BLANK'. All four FILL_INs emit column-grouped or object-keyed prose instead:
  'That can be eaten: Apple, Orange, Grape. That cannot be eaten: Football, Globe, Coin.'
  'Typical results: paper — float (initially), stone — sink, leaf — float, …'

THERE IS NOTHING TO NUMBER, BECAUSE THESE ARE NOT CLOZE ITEMS — they are a two-column sorting table and a predict-and-record grid. The rule presumes a numbered cloze; the content has none.

SAME ROOT AS ARV-D-146. FILL_IN was chosen for `writing` slot 1 in 3 of 3 files (the slot table prescribes SCR) because this section's writing tasks ARE sorting and column-filling. The type choice then drags in FILL_IN's own answer contract, which the content cannot satisfy either. ONE DECISION, TWO RULE BREACHES: if `writing` slot 1 legitimately admits FILL_IN for sorting content, item 8 needs a SECOND permitted answer shape for non-cloze FILL_INs. Decide them together.

ADJACENT, NOT A BREACH, but recorded because the two files disagree: the top puts the word box in `item_stem` while p07 puts it inside `visual_stimulus`. Item 12's rule governs THE TABLE and neither file reproduces a table in a stem, so nothing is violated — but p07's is the better artefact, and it also gives real blank rows where the top gives a single '(write words here)' placeholder.

defects.title: MEMORY item 19's curly-quote format is not emitted at 2 of 3 english stages — the item's own 're-site, don't re-word' escalation fires
defects.evidence:
MEASURED ACROSS THE ENGLISH FAMILY:
  english III ch 11 (S9, this)   curly 0 / 0 / 0   straight-double 0 / 0 / 0
  english VI  ch 8  (S10)        curly 21          straight-double 0
  english IX  ch 7  (S11)        curly 0           straight-double 0
The model wrote 111 / 168 / 71 straight SINGLE quotes in the three S9 files instead.

THE AMENDMENT'S PURPOSE IS FULLY MET AND ITS FORMAT IS NOT. Zero straight DOUBLE quotes in any english library means the JSON escape hazard — the one that cost maths III ch 5 ₹40.72 and forced a hand recovery — cannot occur. But the mandated mark (U+201C/U+201D) is emitted at only one of the three stages.

ITEM 19 WROTE ITS OWN VERDICT IN ADVANCE: 'If it comes back with straight quotes anyway, the Format line is not where the model is taking its cue and the amendment needs RE-SITING, not re-wording.' It came back with straight quotes. The operative cue is 'do not put a double quote inside a JSON string', which the model obeys perfectly — not 'use the curly mark shown'.

MERGE-WORTHY WITH ARV-D-145, AND THAT IS THE POINT. ARV-D-145 found Rule 9's NARRATION FORMAT followed by 1 of 199 bands across three stages; this finds Rule 9's QUOTATION MARK ignored at two of three. They are THE SAME TWO LINES OF THE SAME RULE, measured independently. The conclusion is one conclusion: Rule 9's Format block is not load-bearing on generation, and anything relied on to be guaranteed by it should be re-sited into a line the model demonstrably reads.

NO §9 COST TO FIXING THE PREP COPY (no signed gate); english·middle and ·secondary are the expensive ones, as with ARV-D-145.

defects.title: serve.py's dropped-row RESTORE-AND-FLAG is a no-op on the whole english family — a below-floor plan's coverage_handoff claims a cell the plan declares dropped
defects.evidence:
FOUND AT S9's C9 on the X=6 below-floor serve; second instance of ARV-D-134's class (S11 · C9), and the first with a mechanical cause named.

WHAT IS WRONG. C9 3(c) requires a below-floor serve to carry the dropped units' items 'with their handoff rows restored and FLAGGED'. The ITEMS are correct — X=6 carries `Q-BEXT-B-1/2` flagged `unscheduled: true`, anchored to sitting 7, counted in `genon.assessment_items_unscheduled`. The HANDOFF ROW is not: the `beyond_text` contribution sits in the served `coverage_handoff` with keys `implied_lo · section_context · section_id · section_title · section_type · tasks_anchored` and no flag of any kind.

THE CAUSE, and it is not a deliberate skip. `serve.py:803-822` restores and flags by iterating `blk["los"]` and reading each row's `period_number`:
    for lo in blk.get("los", []):
        sit = dropped_lender_unit_to_sitting.get(int(lo.get("period_number", -1)))
        ... lo2["unscheduled"] = True
English's handoff is `_ENGLISH_SPINE_CELL` — a spine-keyed dict of `section_contributions[]` with NO `los` array and NO per-row unit number. The loop finds nothing, so BOTH THE FILTER AND THE FLAG ARE NO-OPS on english·preparatory, ·middle and ·secondary alike. It is the same shape-blindness `to_engine_handoff` was taught to fix for coverage filtering at S11, on the other half of the same code path.

CONSEQUENCE. The served plan states two different things: `coverage_handoff` says all five cells were taught; the plan teaches four and declares the fifth dropped in three other places (`section_coverage_note`, `result.dropped_units`, the two `unscheduled` items). Nothing renders wrong for the teacher today — the handoff is not teacher-facing and the screen anchors items to units — so this is a DECLARATION GAP, as S11 ruled ARV-D-134. What it costs is any consumer that reads the handoff to answer 'what was taught': the assessment generator would, if it were ever re-run on a served plan.

NOT FIRING TODAY BUT ONE CHAPTER AWAY. X=9's served handoff is byte-identical to its base's and happens to be ACCURATE — p10's unserved u10 anchored only tasks already anchored earlier, so no `tasks_anchored` entry advertises work the class never did. That is a property of this chapter. The same no-op filter would pass an INACCURATE handoff through unchanged on a chapter whose dropped unit carries a first anchor.

REMEDY. Teach the restore/flag path english's handoff shape, exactly as `to_engine_handoff` was taught it — the carrier seam already knows the shape (`_ENGLISH_SPINE_CELL`), so this is a shape adapter, not a new rule. No constitution moves; no library re-opens; §9 does not fire.

SCOPED `campaign` RATHER THAN `english/preparatory` because `serve.py` is shared and the blind spot is the english handoff shape, so S10 and S11 carry it too — neither was caught, because a below-floor serve is the only request that exercises the path.

defects.title: The genon repair toolchain ignores ARUVI_DATA_DIR — purge_derived / build_library / normalize_options address the repo tree while the API may serve another
defects.evidence:
FOUND AT S9's C10.2(b), the ordinary way: `purge_derived.py` was pointed at a copied content tree via `ARUVI_DATA_DIR` and purged the REPO tree instead. Its own error output names the paths it went to.

THE SEAM. `api/config.py` exposes `DATA_DIR` (env `ARUVI_DATA_DIR`), which testing.md §7 calls 'the single root that migrates to the cloud' and which the API reads for every library load. The genon toolchain does not use it:
    genon/purge_derived.py:41   CONTENT = REPO / 'data' / 'content' / 'saved_plans'
    genon/build_library.py:193  return REPO / 'data' / 'content' / 'saved_plans' / …
    genon/build_library.py:742  lib_dir = REPO / 'data' / 'content' / 'saved_plans' / …
    genon/normalize_options.py:209  d = REPO / 'data' / 'content' / 'saved_plans' / …
`repair_register.py` and `repair_anchors.py` inherit the same root through their `from purge_derived import purge`.

WHY IT MATTERS EVEN THOUGH NOTHING BREAKS TODAY. The failure it opens is ARV-D-034 exactly — a repair lands in place, the purge cleans a tree nobody is serving from, and the stale pre-repair plan keeps being served until someone deletes it by hand — reached by a different route. Today nothing overrides `ARUVI_DATA_DIR` outside the tests, and those point at the same tree, so the two roots coincide and the bug is invisible. It stops being invisible the moment a second checkout, a relocated content root, or the Phase-4 migration puts them apart, and §7's whole design is that `DATA_DIR` is the one place that moves.

REMEDY: read `api.config.DATA_DIR` (or a shared helper) instead of composing the path. One line per site, four sites. No constitution moves and no library re-opens.

OPERATIONAL COST ALREADY PAID, recorded so the size is honest: this step could not exercise the purge against its own sandbox copy and had to redirect `purge_derived.CONTENT` in-process — which is exactly what the env var should have done. The mechanism itself verified clean (8 of 8 derived removed, library untouched, regex refusing canonicals).

defects.title: copyright_scan resolved the WRONG BOOK for english (not merely no book) — S11's CERTIFIED C14 scored 0.00% against a different chapter; scanner fixed, S11's C14 must be re-run
defects.evidence:
FOUND AT S9's C14. The copyright review documents the resolver hole as 'the glob matches nothing on all 101 English chapters, so the book contributes ZERO words'. At two of the three english stages it is WORSE — it matches a DIFFERENT CHAPTER'S PDF, because english chapters were split out of textbook UNITS and the two numbering spaces collide:
  english III ch 11  ->  'chapter 11 - Chanda Mama Counts the Stars.pdf'   (correct: 'chapter 07 - The Big Laddoo.pdf')
  english IX  ch 7   ->  'chapter 07 - Carrier of Words.pdf'               (correct: 'chapter 04 - Vitamin-M.pdf')
  english VI  ch 8   ->  no match, as documented
  english VII/VIII ch 1 -> correct BY COINCIDENCE (first chapter of a unit)

A WRONG BOOK SCORES ~0% AND READS AS A CONFIDENT CLEAN PASS — the most expensive way for this check to fail. MEASURED ON S11's OWN CERTIFIED CANONICAL (english IX ch 7):
  vs 'Carrier of Words' (what it used) : 0 of 4,308 words = 0.00%, ZERO runs
  vs 'Vitamin-M' (the real chapter)    : 51 = 1.18%, 4 runs, LONGEST 20 WORDS
including a 13-word run of NARRATIVE PROSE in an ASSESSMENT ITEM's visual_stimulus — 'off he went twirling his walking stick jauntily leaving Ravi in a dilemma' — which S11 never saw, and which is exactly the class of match F2 is about.

TOOLING FIXED IN THIS PASS: the mapping was in the split summary all along (`_source_unit.unit_chapter_number`). The resolver reads it and falls back to the plan's own number, so the change is additive. Verified corpus-wide — all three english stages now resolve correctly (VI ch 8 -> 5,373 book words, EXACTLY the figure the copyright review obtained by hand), and mathematics, social_sciences, science and TWAU are unchanged.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN, and it is the reason this is S2: **S11's C14 result is not evidence and its C14 should be re-run against the correct book.** It is a CERTIFIED stage carrying a copyright verdict obtained from the wrong source. S10's C14 stands — the review records that its figures were obtained by pointing at the correct PDF by hand — but its tracker comment should note it was hand-resolved, not tool-resolved.

defects.title: One LP band restates a task_text verbatim (17 words) — LP Rule 3, and the largest lesson-plan-side book match in the library
defects.evidence:
LP Rule 3: 'Band activities reference tasks by `spine_section_name` + brief; they do not restate `task_text` or enumerate sub-items verbatim.'

Top canonical u3, band 1:
  "Let us think — teacher poses the first prompt: 'Have you seen a big laddoo? How big was it? Did you eat it all by yourself?' Children think for a moment, then share with a partner."

The quoted run is the textbook's own discussion question, restated word for word — 17 words, and the LARGEST lesson-plan-side book-matched run in the whole library. It propagates into 6 of the 11 scanned files because it rides in u3.

NOT A COPYRIGHT DEFECT: it sits inside quotation marks, its band names the subheading ('Let us think'), and the founder's ruling of 2026-08-13 (S10's C3) covers a short quoted lift that frames a question as reference rather than reproduction. It is filed as the RULE breach it is.

ISOLATED, NOT A PATTERN: one band of 133 across the three canonicals. Every other band references its task by subheading + brief as Rule 3 asks, and the four other 8-word book matches are prompt FRAGMENTS, which is the reference form. Repairable in place; no re-author needed.

defects.title: SS·IX ch 1 U13 teacher_notes carries a completion claim — ACCEPTED, not repaired
defects.evidence: ch_01_canonical.json U13 teacher_notes: "Having covered all four disciplines, this unit turns to the chapter's explicit normative argument: why this field matters." register_scan family COMPLETION; it is the only surviving ban hit in the whole social_sciences/ix library and it makes ch 01's certification report read FAILURES.
defects.notes: FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-13: accept the text, do not edit it. The reasoning is why it was never a clock/forward/calendar-style deletion in the first place — U13 of 15 sits after all four discipline sections in the STANDARD, where the sentence is simply TRUE. It is false only in a compact that drops a discipline, and a compact borrowing U13 borrows the note with it. So the open question was never 'is this text wrong' but 'is the completion ban about the TEXT or about the SERVE' — and the answer taken is the text stands. CONSEQUENCE, to be repeated wherever this stage is called clean: repair_register.py --apply still exits 1 on one surviving hit, and ch 01's report still says FAIL. SS·IX is 8 of 9 ALL PASS plus one accepted breach, and must never be written as 9 of 9.

defects.title: The serve contract was narrated into teacher-facing text in 35 places across four subjects
defects.evidence: e.g. TWAU iv ch 2 U17 BAND text: 'This surfaces the full conceptual map of the chapter without requiring any specific earlier activity to have occurred.' Also SS·IX ch 5 p17 U17 'across seventeen units' (a count SELECTION falsifies) and 'no prior artefact is needed'. Census: TWAU 20 · SS 6+3 · english 2 · maths 1; 12 in band text.
defects.notes: Found by F1 reading borrowed seams, not by any scanner. The brief says 'this unit must not assume another unit' and the model writes the instruction down instead of obeying it. All 35 repaired by genon/repair_meta_leak.py (declared old->new pairs, pure deletions bar 5 capitalisations); corpus now scans 0. register_scan.py gained a 4th ban family 'meta-leak' so the unauthored batches cannot reintroduce it. UPSTREAM FIX NOT DONE: a brief phrased as a prohibition hands the model a sentence to repeat — state self-containment as a property of the output, never as a rule to acknowledge.

defects.title: The item-stem gate did not know maths' own stem field and quarantined a paid library
defects.evidence: build_library._STEM_FIELDS = ('question_text','item_stem') with a comment asserting "`prompt` appears 471 times in the PROTOTYPE-era maths corpus and in NO CANONICAL". False: `prompt` is the stem field of mathematics·preparatory AND mathematics·middle. Census over every canonical on disk: question_text 1772 · prompt 123 · item_stem 96. The gate read 30-33 items per file as stemless and quarantined all three maths·iii ch 5 canonicals on a routine --certify-only.
defects.notes: Fixed by adding 'prompt' to _STEM_FIELDS; library restored and re-scanned per runbook trap 1 (the meta-leak repair survived in it). Stem failures 30 -> 1. The lesson is the one the old comment was reaching for and got backwards: a gate must tolerate the shapes that EXIST, and 'exists' is settled by a census covering every STAGE — maths is diverse within itself, so even a subject-level census would have missed it.

defects.title: maths·iii ch 5 Q-C-2 is an empty MCQ stub — a blank question on a teacher's screen
defects.evidence: ch_05_canonical.json item Q-C-2: prompt '', options [], visual_stimulus '', expected_answer '', method_one_line '', what_each_option_reveals {}, verified:false, and inclusivity literally reads '[Verification failed] Refer to the book task anchored to S5.' Only exercise.book_ref survives ('Let us Do Q1, p.55').
defects.notes: PRE-EXISTING, not introduced today — it was invisible because the stem gate's own bug (ARV-D-159) buried it among 29 false positives on the same file. Now the sole stem failure. It re-quarantines the whole ch 5 library on every --certify-only until it is resolved, so the chapter is unservable meanwhile. Not repairable by declaration (there is no text to delete — a stem must be authored), so this is a founder call: author the stem, drop the item, or re-author the file.

defects.title: meta-leak: the model narrates its own register compliance inside the artefact (10 hits / 40 files, new defect family)
defects.evidence: teacher_notes across 8 chapters, e.g. viii ch_11 U11 "…shows how the chapter's sections connect WITHOUT REQUIRING ANY EARLIER UNIT TO HAVE HAPPENED"; vii ch_10 U17 "…sets up the synthesis unit without requiring any specific prior activity to have occurred"; vi ch_07 U17, vi ch_09 U5, vi ch_10 U15, vii ch_06 U18, vii ch_10 U14/U18, viii ch_08 U5. viii ch_11 U11 is the sharp case: the same sentence carries a BACKWARD unit dependency ("as established in the earlier unit on Supreme Court jurisdiction") and then asserts it requires no earlier unit.
defects.notes: Not a teaching defect and not the 2026-08-02 lottery case — the constitution states the register and the model is OBEYING it, out loud, in prose addressed to the constitution rather than to the teacher. So this is brief-side: the next SS·middle constitution pass should say that self-containment is demonstrated by the unit working, never by asserting it. Same shape as the S4 finding (repair v1.4) where the model paraphrased the brief's own description of the synthesis unit. Repaired in place for this wave at the founder's instruction 2026-08-16; the row stays open against the brief, not the artefacts.

defects.title: register_scan clock ban fires on a narrated HISTORICAL duration — repairing it would falsify the history
defects.evidence: viii ch 9 U11: "Brigadier-General Dyer sealed the main exit and fired approximately 1,650 rounds FOR ABOUT TEN MINUTES" — the duration of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, not the pacing of a classroom activity.
defects.notes: CLOSED 2026-08-16 at the scanner, never in the text (runbook trap 4). The clock ban now requires a classroom actor in the sentence carrying the quantity. Kept deliberately crude: if a sentence mentions the class at all the ban still fires, so the gate can only release a sentence that is about somebody else entirely.

defects.title: repair_register.py: a second live ("social_sciences","viii") key silently shadowed the new batch set
defects.evidence: The 2026-08-04 VIII ch 3 pilot set sat at the live 2-tuple key. Adding the batch wave-1 set under the same key made it a duplicate in one dict literal; Python keeps the LAST, so --grade viii ran the already-applied pilot declarations and died on its own "declared text not found" guard.
defects.notes: Fixed by moving the pilot set to ("social_sciences","viii","APPLIED-20260804") — the pattern the file already uses for ix/APPLIED-20260803 and mathematics·IX v1.5. The guard caught it, which is the guard working; the key layout is what made it possible. Worth a one-line check in the tool that no 2-tuple key is declared twice.

defects.title: genon/master_plan.py rebuilt master_plan.json AT IMPORT, erasing every canonical_plan annotation portfolio-wide
defects.evidence: 2026-08-16 09:48. A verification script did `import master_plan` to reach the pure helper canonical_periods() for checking the W2 dry-run counts. The module's body ran, including `with open(master_plan.json,'w')`, regenerating the plan from the workbook. `canonical_plan` vanished from ALL 340 chapter rows across all five subjects — including RELEASED stages (TWAU·preparatory, SS·secondary). Surfaced as the W2 compact submit refusing all 40 SS·middle chapters with "Row is provisional — author and certify the standard canonical", which points at the standards rather than at the erasure.
defects.notes: Recovered free and exactly: `python3 genon/variant_plans.py` re-annotated 188 authored rows, and a field-by-field diff against git HEAD showed the ONLY remaining difference was the 40 SS·middle rows going provisional true→false — which is W1's own annotation, i.e. correct. Every count, budget and pin identical. FIX: the write and its prints now sit under `if __name__ == '__main__'`, so a rebuild is an explicit act and an import is inert (verified: artefact byte-identical after import, canonical_periods still callable). Standing lesson for the campaign: a module that mutates a data artefact at import will eventually be imported by something that only wanted a helper, and the damage shows up somewhere else entirely. Worth grepping the other genon scripts for module-level writes.

defects.title: 15 of 41 standards omit a real chapter-summary section from their registry (46 sections, 14 of the 15 in class VIII) — and C5 check 11's SS matcher cannot see it
defects.evidence: Found because six compacts were quarantined for anchoring sections the top registry lacks — every one of those anchors is a real summary heading (viii ch 8 'Ocean currents'/'Ocean trenches'/'Smaller water bodies'; ch 10 'Churches in India'/'Colonial Architecture'; ch 12 'Right to life'/'Right against exploitation'/'Right to constitutional remedies'; ch 7 'Factors of Production'/'People as a resource'). Check 11's advisory for viii ch 7 claims the summary does not name 'Introduction', 'Land (natural resources)', 'Labour (human resources)' — all three are verbatim headings — and it found 6 summary sections where there are 14, offering 'The section' and 'This section' as unmatched leads.
defects.notes: FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-16: the top's editorial selection IS the contract; a section the top folds in is in all likelihood integrated into the lesson anyway; the only concern is jump risk from compact-top anchor misalignment. So the 46 are accepted and the compacts were aligned to the registry (teaching untouched, only the section CLAIM withdrawn). What remains open is the GATE, not the content: check 11 is the mechanism meant to catch this at W1, before money is spent on compacts cut against short registries, and on SS it is not fit to be ruled on — which is what closing-checklist item 4 requires of it. Fixing the matcher is free and should precede the next SS batch.

defects.title: Two orphan units in viii ch 8 — resolved by re-anchoring to the parent section, not by re-authoring
defects.evidence: viii ch 8 p08 U3 ("Smaller water bodies and waterways") and p11 U3 ("Ocean currents / Ocean trenches") carried no registry anchor at all.
defects.notes: CLOSED 2026-08-16, and the closing is the lesson. Claude classified both as unfixable — drop the label and the unit is unplaceable, so re-author (~₹27) or rule accepted — and sent them to F1. The founder pointed at the registry, which already carries the parent section: 'The Blue of the Blue Planet, the Oceans' / 'The oceans'. Currents, trenches and smaller water bodies are that section's material, so the label is REPLACED rather than dropped. Both files then returned 0 unknown anchors, 0 order-breaks, 12/12 coverage, and viii ch 8 is ALL PASS. These eleven units were always ONE fix; they had been split into two categories on the accident of whether a valid anchor happened to sit alongside the stray.

defects.title: register_scan: a possessive apostrophe broke quote detection, so the "calendar hit inside quotes is advisory" rule protected almost nothing
defects.evidence: _QUOTED treated every ' as a delimiter, so in "residents' quality of life. Teacher asks: 'If you were appointed urban planner for your own town tomorrow…'" it paired residents' with the prompt's opening quote. Every span shifted by one and the quoted prompt fell OUTSIDE a quoted span — reported as a hard ban hit (SS·VIII ch 14 U10). Any band using a possessive before a quoted prompt lost its protection, which is most of them.
defects.notes: FIXED: an opening quote must now sit at a boundary (start, whitespace, : ( - —); closers are unrestricted. Verified corpus-wide in both directions — it cleared ch 14 AND exposed two hits the bug had been WRONGLY SUPPRESSING in released stages (SS·IX ch 4 U16, TWAU·V ch 10 U7), both hypotheticals, both now correctly advisory under the calendar narrowing below. Same change set: `tomorrow` and `this|next|last week|month` dropped from BAN to ADVISORY (every hit across all five stages was content — a definition of weather, a credit-timing question, an idiom, two hypotheticals; `(next|last) class` stays a ban because it names a SITTING), and the clock ban now fires only when the sentence carrying the quantity names a classroom actor, which closes ARV-D-162 without touching the Jallianwala text and without weakening the 58 real pacing hits.

tooling_notes.note:
C5 TOOLING GAP, added 2026-08-09 off ARV-D-084/085: certification has no check
for MODEL SELF-CORRECTION surviving into a shipped field. Two of 16 installed canonicals carry
one - maths IX ch4 top item 4 (method_one_line, teacher-facing) and science IX ch8 p07 item 4
(question_text, student-facing) - and a human rule-by-rule C3 caught the first and missed the
second, because it is not a rule violation. Markers observed: 'wait', 'let me re-check',
'let me verify', 'actually,', 'correction:'. A regex over question_text, expected_answer,
method_one_line, task, scaffold, expected_elements, look_for and the guide blocks costs
nothing and runs at --certify-only. Recommended to land beside register_scan.

C14 TOOLING, fixed in this pass (genon/copyright_scan.py). (1) load_source globbed only ch_NN_summary.txt; mathematics, english and the_world_around_us carry ch_NN_summary.json — SEVEN of the eleven stages — so the summary silently contributed zero words and the tool reported a confident clean against the PDF alone. Now reads both shapes; a --book-only flag keeps the textbook (the protected work) separable from Aruvi's summary (its own asset), because merging them turned an 18-word run into a 45-word one on this chapter. (2) lp_fields yields nothing on a served plan wrapped in a second {'result': ...} — serve_plan already returns the saved-plan envelope — so a scan of freshly-served plans reports clean on zero strings. Recommendation for the shared tool: print a per-plan field count and refuse a zero, as genon/out/stage_prep_mathematics_middle/c14_copyright_review.py now does.

doctrine_notes.title: read-after-write verification
doctrine_notes.note:
READ-AFTER-WRITE VERIFICATION — the founder's rule, implemented and proved
(2026-08-10). Recorded here because it is a standing pattern, not a defect fix, and because it
CORRECTS the reasoning that produced ARV-D-087/088.

THE RULE: an error requires a pre-state X, an action A, and an expected post-state Y known
UPFRONT. After A, pull Y' from the server. Error IF AND ONLY IF Y' != Y.
What it rules out, and what I had wrongly been treating as triggers: 'the request threw' is not
a criterion (a 200 can lie; a lost response can hide a write that landed), and 'the server is
unreachable' is NOT an error but a state in which THE CHECK CANNOT RUN — presuming failure
there would invent a fact. Three outcomes, never two: ok (silence) · mismatch (the only case
that speaks) · unverified (silence).

IMPLEMENTED: web/app/lib/verify.js — verifiedWrite({write, read, expect}). The write's own
rejection is swallowed on purpose; the READ is the arbiter. A comparator that throws returns
'unverified' rather than a false alarm.

AREA 1 (the teaching profile) IS LIVE AND TESTED ON THE PHONE. Y = the subjects[] she composed,
Y' = GET /readiness. On mismatch the view is RE-SYNCED to Y' before the message shows —
telling her it failed while leaving her edit on screen would recreate the divergence the check
exists to catch. Founder ran all three cases: A works -> silence; B (profile chmod 444, so the
write fails while the read still succeeds) -> the line fires AND the subject disappears;
C (API stopped) -> silence, correctly.

THE COMPARATOR IS THE WHOLE RISK and is tested as such: tests/test_verify_readiness.mjs, 17
checks, most asserting what must NOT fire (section order, subject order, grade case, duration
order, '7' vs 7, budget edits). A false alarm would teach her to ignore the real one.

KNOWN RESIDUAL, seen deliberately at case C: between an unverified write and her next refresh
the screen shows a state the server may not have. The doctrine forbids calling that an error.
Closing it would need a third state — 'not yet confirmed' — which is a design decision, not a
patch.

OWED, in the founder's numbering: area 2 (LP generation), 3 (archiving), 4 (attaching an LP to
a section card), 5 (mark complete) are the same call with a predicate instead of an equality —
their read endpoints all exist (/plans-prepared, /plan-archive, /section-state). AREA 6
(chapter notes) CANNOT be done: notes live only in localStorage under
chapter_notes_{subject}_{grade}_{chapter_title} and NO endpoint exists, so there is no Y' to
pull. Under the rule that correctly means no error may ever be raised for a note — and also
that her notes are one cache-clear from gone. That is an endpoint decision, not a message.
