doctrine_notes.title: read-after-write — areas 1-5 complete
doctrine_notes.note:
AREAS 1-5 ARE LIVE (2026-08-10). Area 6 is impossible and stays out.

1 PROFILE — all THREE live write sites, not the one first shipped: TeachingProfile.persist
  (settings gear + '+' portal), page.jsx onFirstRunComplete (THE ACTIVATION WRITE — it ended in
  an empty catch, so a lost profile looked exactly like successful setup until her next
  sign-in) and page.jsx onReadyComplete. On mismatch the shell re-syncs BOTH `readiness` AND
  `ready` from Y', because leaving ready=true over an empty profile would strand her in a shell
  with no classes and no explanation. MyClasses.jsx:97 is a fourth site but the component is
  DEAD CODE (imported nowhere) — left alone deliberately.
2 PREPARE — after the serve returns a filename, Y is knowable: 'that lesson is in MY prepared
  register'. Verified against GET /plans-prepared; a mismatch means the plan was built but
  never became hers, which she would otherwise meet as an unexplained absence in My Lessons.
  Reported through the SAME failed-card surface ARV-D-087 built.
3 ARCHIVE / RESTORE — one verifier for both directions, since they are the same fact inverted.
  This pair was already the best-behaved code in the app (revert + toast on a throw) but a
  throw is not the criterion: the archive may have landed with the response lost.
4+5 SECTION CARD — both go through pushSectionState, the single shared writer, so ONE change
  covers attach, unbind and mark-complete. Y = {chapter, done}; `done` is compared only when
  asked for, so an attach is never failed by a done-flag it did not set. On mismatch the shell
  re-pulls that section before speaking. A module-level handler rather than a return value,
  because pushSectionState is fire-and-forget from a dozen call sites.

COMPARATORS TESTED: tests/test_verify_readiness.mjs, 17 -> 31 checks, all green. The additions
assert the things that would make it cry wolf: another grade's plan does not count as hers; an
attach is not failed by a done flag; a section she never touched is not judged.

STILL TRUE, and the reason this is a rule rather than error-handling: a throw is never the
criterion, and an unreachable server is 'cannot tell', not 'failed'. Only a read-back
disagreement speaks.

doctrine_notes.title: S7 founder calls that must carry into BULK BATCH GENERATION
doctrine_notes.note:
Recorded at S7 C3 (2026-08-10) at the founder's instruction: 'keep track of all of this as when we do bulk batch generation, we will apply same logic there too.' These are STANDING decisions, not S7 findings, and the batch pre-warm must apply them rather than re-derive them.

1. NUMERIC LIMITS ARE THE FIRST THING LIVE GENERATION DISPROVES. Four fell in one chapter: Rule 5's consecutive-method cap (amended, v3.5), Rule 2's two-adjacent-period cap (amended, v3.6, and it was FORCING the revisits), Rule 1's one-or-two-sections cap (amended, v3.7), Rule 10's 10-word bracket cap (waived, ARV-D-096). The 25-word inclusivity cap (ARV-D-097) is the same class and is still open. AT BATCH: read every numeric bound in a constitution before authoring at scale, because catching one at P1 is free and catching it after 926 runs is not.

2. RULE 1 AND RULE 2 CAP THE SAME RELATION FROM OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Rule 2 governs one SECTION over many PERIODS; Rule 1 governs one PERIOD over many SECTIONS. Amending one without the other leaves the model boxed in on the axis you did not touch. Both now read 'as many ADJACENT … as its content warrants'.

3. THE MODEL ENDS PLANS BY LOOPING BACK, and prose does not stop it. Three occurrences in one chapter, twice against text forbidding it in terms. Same lesson as option ordering (became STEP 6) and the register (became a machine gate). AT BATCH: the contiguity certifier check is owed BEFORE volume, or the defect ships at corpus scale.

4. THE HEADER BLOCK IS NOT COMING (ARV-D-095). No stage emits it; middle structurally cannot, because its handoff carries no competency channel and Rule 8 forbids one. Do not treat its absence as a batch defect.

5. CONTAINER SHAPE IS THE RECURRING BUG CLASS — five instances now: science's `questions` wrapper (S3), carriers.raw_item_list, extract_determinate.py, normalize_options' guide path, and the assessment item-group nesting. AT BATCH: any tool that walks items must be shape-based and must be exercised on a maths-middle file, an english file and a science file before it runs at volume — a silent zero reads exactly like a clean pass.

6. A GENERATOR MUST NOT BE ABLE TO DESTROY A FILLED ARTEFACT (ARV-D-091). Guard every artefact-writing tool, and negative-test the guard.

doctrine_notes.title: textbook reproduction — the open question (C14)
doctrine_notes.note:
DEFERRED by the founder, 2026-08-10, and framed by him thus: 'what are the copyright aspects involved when books are NOT being reproduced? Assessment items are GENERATED, and textbook items are shown as ADDITIONAL WORK only and are not solved for.'

That framing is the strongest fact in Aruvi's favour and should lead the analysis: the student-facing question is authored by Aruvi from the chapter summary's prose; the textbook item is a POINTER offered to the teacher as parallel practice, and Aruvi neither reprints nor solves it.

SCOPE, measured 2026-08-10 — narrower than it looks:
  · assessment `exercise` companion (book_ref + description): mathematics MIDDLE and PREPARATORY ONLY. Maths secondary has none; science, social_sciences, TWAU and all three English stages have none.
  · LP `book_ref` citation: all THREE maths stages (middle 11 hits, prep 11, secondary 8). Secondary LOCATES only in prose but still carries a `description` string in its structured items — so a policy scoped to 'middle and prep' would miss it.
  · non-maths subjects never cite a textbook item at all.

THE INTERNAL CONTRADICTION to resolve either way: the LP constitution's DESIGN PRINCIPLE says the LP 'does NOT reprint item content', and Rule 10 forty lines later mandates the description 'in brackets and inverted commas'. Also, `step_1_chapter_summary.md` never says whether `description` should be verbatim or a gist, so every description in the corpus is unconstrained — today they read as paraphrase.

FOUNDER'S LEANING: quote the content in inverted commas and credit '(Source: NCERT)'. Two cautions recorded with it — attribution is not permission (it addresses passing-off, not copying), and marking a paraphrase as a quotation misattributes Aruvi's words to NCERT, so quotes require verbatim capture and therefore a summary re-author. Suggested refinement: credit once per artefact from a recorded `textbook_source` field rather than per item and rather than hard-coding a publisher.

NOT A LEGAL OPINION. Needs counsel before spend. Precedent already inside the product: Rule 7 forbids reproducing FIGURES and says to point at them instead — 'Refer to Fig. 5.6 in §5.3 of your textbook'.
